title: Biomarkers in Patients With Acute Ischaemic Stroke Undergoing Thrombectomy Compared With Controls: A Pilot Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Detection of cerebral ischaemia is challenging in patients who are anaesthetised, sedated or have reduced levels of consciousness, as neurological examination is difficult or even impossible to assess. Furthermore, as some patients cannot be transported for radiology, for example during surgery, a reliable blood biomarker for detecting acute cerebral events would be of considerable clinical value. We aimed to compare levels of brain injury biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and total tau (tau) in patients with acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy under general anaesthesia or sedation to controls undergoing non-cerebral surgery under general anaesthesia. These biomarkers were chosen because previous studies have demonstrated their potential as blood biomarkers of acute cerebral injury and ischaemic stroke.

METHODS: In this prospective, observational pilot study, conducted at the Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg, Sweden, between 2021 and 2024, GFAP, NfL, and tau were analysed using the Simoa Neurology 4-plex assay, before thrombectomy or surgery and at 2- and 24 h thereafter.

RESULTS: Blood samples from 21 patients with AIS and 19 controls were analysed. GFAP concentrations in patients with AIS increased significantly from baseline to 24 h (median 301.0 → 1443.0 pg/mL; p = 0.001) and were higher than in controls at all time points (p < 0.01). In the controls there was no significant increase in GFAP from baseline to 24 h (p = 0.449). NfL and tau increased significantly in patients with AIS (p = 0.001 and 0.002) but also in the controls (p = 0.001 and 0.047).

CONCLUSION: GFAP and NfL concentrations were higher in patients with acute ischaemic stroke than in surgical controls at all sampling time points, whereas tau differed only after 24 h. Unlike NfL and tau, GFAP did not increase significantly in controls, suggesting that it may be less influenced by anaesthesia and surgery. These findings support further evaluation of GFAP as a potential biomarker of acute cerebral injury in perioperative and critical care settings.

EDITORIAL COMMENT: A biomarker of ischaemic cerebral injury could be attractive to support treatments to protect brain health during anaesthesia and surgery. In a pilot study, glial fibrillary acidic protein emerged as a potential candidate as it was increased in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy for large-vessel ischaemic stroke compared to anaesthetised patients undergoing non-cerebral surgery.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03919370.

title: Late venous thromboembolic events in survivors of childhood cancer: a report from the St Jude Lifetime Cohort Study.
abstract: Survivors of childhood cancer are at risk of adverse sequelae related to previous therapies. We describe the prevalence of and risk factors for late (≥5 years from cancer diagnosis) venous thromboembolism (VTE) among participants of the St. Jude Lifetime Cohort Study (N = 5229). Prevalence of late VTE was compared between survivors and community controls (N = 737) without a history of childhood cancer. Associations with treatment and clinical factors were assessed in multivariable regression models. Ninety-four (1.8% [95% confidence interval (CI), 1.5-2.2]) survivors (median age at cancer diagnosis 9.4 years [range, 0.0-20.9]; 38.5 years [12-65.9] at evaluation) had 108 VTEs vs 5 (0.7% [95% CI, 0.2-1.6]) among controls (P = .02; 31.1 years [12.1-70.2] at evaluation). The cumulative incidence 35 years from diagnosis was highest among survivors of Hodgkin lymphoma (7.6% [95% CI, 4.5-11.8]). Fifty-eight of 108 (53.7%) were in an extremity (upper = 7, lower = 51), followed by pulmonary (38 [35.2%]), abdomen (n = 5 [4.6%]), neck (n = 3 [2.8%]), cerebral sinus (n = 1 [0.9%]), and other (n = 3 [2.8%]). No associations with early (<5 years from cancer diagnosis) VTE were identified (P = .7). In adjusted models, late VTE was associated with exposure to chest (odds ratio [OR], 2.0; 95% CI, 1.01-4.0) and abdominal (OR, 2.2; 95% CI, 1.04-4.8) radiation, not combined radiation fields (OR, 1.2; 95% CI, 0.7-2.0) and sex hormone use (OR, 2.2; 95% CI, 1.2-3.7). The prevalence of and risk for VTE are elevated among survivors of childhood cancer, particularly those treated with radiation or using sex hormones. Incorporating these factors into risk assessments may guide monitoring, prophylaxis, or interventions, particularly in high-risk situations.

title: Individualised Versus Conventional Balloon Dilation for TIPS: Hepatic Encephalopathy in a Propensity-Matched Before-After Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatic encephalopathy (HE) is a major complication of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS). Stent under-dilation reduces HE, but a fixed diameter cannot be individualised to patient risk. An individualised scoring system tailoring balloon diameter to patient characteristics, without compromising efficacy or increasing variceal re-bleeding or stent dysfunction, is needed.

METHODS: In this retrospective study, 717 patients with cirrhosis underwent TIPS with 8-mm covered stents between December 2015 and December 2023. Patients received conventional 8-mm full dilation (n = 408; before December 1, 2020) or individualised dilation (n = 309; from December 1, 2020 onward), with the balloon diameter (5-7 mm) chosen by an 11-factor scoring system. The primary endpoint was overt HE (West Haven grade II-IV) within 6 months. Propensity score matching, inverse probability weighting, Fine-Grey and E-value analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Six-month overt HE was lower in the individualised group (14.6%; 45 of 309) than in the conventional group (27.5%; 112 of 408), yielding an absolute risk reduction of 12.9 percentage points (number needed to treat, 8; p < 0.001). After propensity score matching on 18 covariates (259 pairs), the conditional odds ratio was 0.42 (95% CI, 0.27-0.66; p < 0.001), consistent with inverse probability weighting (odds ratio, 0.47). Six-month re-bleeding (1.5% vs. 1.3%), stent dysfunction (3.9% vs. 4.2%) and ascites improvement (61.0% vs. 62.1%) did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSIONS: An individualised balloon dilation strategy incorporating an 11-factor scoring system was associated with reduced post-TIPS HE, with no clear difference in variceal re-bleeding, stent dysfunction or ascites recurrence.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2400087533.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatic encephalopathy (HE) is a major complication of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS). Stent under-dilation reduces HE, but a fixed diameter cannot be individualised to patient risk. An individualised scoring system tailoring balloon diameter to patient characteristics, without compromising efficacy or increasing variceal re-bleeding or stent dysfunction, is needed.

title: Changes in Circulating Insulin and Glucose Homeostasis After Portosystemic Shunt Creation and Obliteration: A Systematic Review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND & AIMS: The liver removes about half of secreted insulin on first pass. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt creation diverts portal blood past the liver; endovascular shunt obliteration restores it. We systematically reviewed glycaemic and insulin outcomes after both.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase and Web of Science were searched through September 2026 for paired glucose or insulin measurements before and after either intervention. Ratios of post-intervention to pre-intervention means were pooled by random effects with Hartung-Knapp adjustment, excluding cohorts at critical risk of bias.

RESULTS: Fifteen cohorts (17 records) were included. After shunt creation, fasting insulin rose 49% (95% confidence interval 24% to 80%; 6 cohorts) and the homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance rose 55% (5% to 129%; 4 cohorts), whereas fasting glucose (2.5%; -0.3% to 5.4%; 5 cohorts), glycated haemoglobin, and fructosamine were unchanged. Glucose tolerance worsened in one of two cohorts tested (area under the curve +14%). Insulin rose more than C-peptide or proinsulin in four cohorts; clamp-measured insulin sensitivity was unchanged. After obliteration, fasting insulin fell 15% (one cohort) and insulin area under the curve 17% and 19% (two cohorts). Antihyperglycaemic requirements changed in both directions after shunt creation and fell after obliteration.

CONCLUSIONS: Shunt creation raises insulin by nearly half without changing fasting glucose or glycation markers, and obliteration reverses the pattern. Secretion markers change less than insulin, indicating altered first-pass hepatic insulin extraction rather than secretion. Insulin-based resistance indices may mislead after shunting, and the consequences of chronic shunt-induced hyperinsulinemia need prospective study.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND & AIMS: The liver removes about half of secreted insulin on first pass. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt creation diverts portal blood past the liver; endovascular shunt obliteration restores it. We systematically reviewed glycaemic and insulin outcomes after both.

title: The many faces of contrast-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The increased use of endovascular procedures shows an increase of neurological deficits after intravascular administration of iodine-based contrast media (ICM). Unfortunately, nonuniform terminology is confusing and may explain low awareness of this ICM-associated neurological adverse drug reaction (nADR). Consequently, we conducted this study to summarize identified risk factors, clinical presentations, radiological features, pathophysiological mechanisms, and treatment strategies of ICM-associated nADR. Additionally, we evaluated, if unifying different terminology of nADR seems to be warranted.

METHODS: A PRISMA-2020 systematic literature search was conducted. We included scientific articles on contrast-induced encephalopathy (CIE), contrast-induced neurotoxicity (CIN), and transient cortical blindness (TCB) following administration of ICM. A total of 228 records were eligible for inclusion.

RESULTS: The majority of neurological adverse reactions manifests after invasive contrast enhanced procedures and are mostly described as CIE, CIN, and TCB. Patients present with stroke mimickers and TCB. The onset of symptoms varies from shortly after the administration of ICM till up to 24 h following ICM application. In most of the patients the neurological symptoms are reversible. The available evidence suggests that there seems to be a common underlying pathophysiology, most likely due to dysfunction of the blood brain barrier. Risk factors include chronic or end stage renal disease, underlying vascular dysfunction, ICM volume, and the territory of ICM administration.

CONCLUSIONS: There is need for implementation of formal criteria and raising awareness on risk factors and therapeutic management of nADR following ICM administration. The authors suggest to summarize currently different terminology under 1 umbrella of contrast-associated encephalopathy.

ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: The increase of diagnostic and therapeutic endovascular procedures reveals ICM-associated neurological adverse reactions. Knowledge and awareness on neurotoxic effects after ICM application must be raised among radiologists and clinicians which may be enhanced by unifying the nomenclature.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: The increased use of endovascular procedures shows an increase of neurological deficits after intravascular administration of iodine-based contrast media (ICM). Unfortunately, nonuniform terminology is confusing and may explain low awareness of this ICM-associated neurological adverse drug reaction (nADR). Consequently, we conducted this study to summarize identified risk factors, clinical presentations, radiological features, pathophysiological mechanisms, and treatment strategies of ICM-associated nADR.

title: Intraoperative Diastolic Blood Pressure Variability and Myocardial Injury in Acute Ischemic Stroke after Endovascular Treatment: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The association between intraoperative blood pressure variability and postoperative myocardial injury (PMI) after endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is unknown.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled AIS patients who underwent EVT between June 28th, 2016, and January 11th, 2021. PMI was assessed using cardiac troponin I measurement. Intraoperative diastolic blood pressure (DBP) variability was assessed using the coefficient of variation (CV). A population-level CV threshold was derived from the inflection point of the logistic regression curve. The primary outcome was PMI during hospitalization. To establish the association between DBP variability and PMI, multivariable logistic regression was used to adjust for possible confounders.

RESULTS: During the study period, 469 AIS patients were included. The median age was 63 years, and 142 (30.3%) were women. A total of 84 (17.9%) patients experienced PMI. An intraoperative diastolic CV of 16% was estimated as the threshold. After adjusting for confounders, with every 1% increase in diastolic CV above 16%, there was a 17% increase in the odds of experiencing PMI (OR=1.17; 95% CI: 1.09-1.27; P≤0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: DBP variability is associated with PMI in AIS patients undergoing EVT. Future randomized clinical trials should evaluate whether stabilizing diastolic perfusion pressure reduces the incidence of PMI.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The association between intraoperative blood pressure variability and postoperative myocardial injury (PMI) after endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) is unknown. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled AIS patients who underwent EVT between June 28th, 2016, and January 11th, 2021. PMI was assessed using cardiac troponin I measurement.

title: "Mind or machine?": Study protocol for a mixed-methods study evaluating the effectiveness and lived experience of active versus passive prophylaxis in older hip fracture patients.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hip fracture in older adults causes a "dual crisis" of venous thromboembolism (VTE) and rapid muscle atrophy. Pharmacological prevention is effective but carries significant bleeding risks for these frail patients. Current physical prophylaxis is often too weak to restore muscle pump function. Therefore, this study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of two enhanced strategies, active resistance training and passive neuromuscular electrical stimulation, against standard care for VTE prevention and muscle preservation.

METHODS: A three-arm, assessor-blinded, parallel-group RCT will be conducted at a tertiary hospital in Qingdao, China. Older patients (n = 222) recovering from hip fracture fixation will be randomized in a 1:1:1 ratio to: (1) the control group; (2) the control plus lower-limb resistance training group; or (3) the control plus neuromuscular electrical stimulation group. The primary outcome is the incidence of ultrasound-confirmed VTE within the intervention period. Secondary outcomes include venous hemodynamics, muscle architecture, self-reported fatigue, and cost-effectiveness. Quantitative data will be analyzed using intention-to-treat principles. Following the RCT, a qualitative interpretive phenomenological analysis study will be conducted with a purposive sample of 10-12 participants to explore the lived experiences, barriers, and facilitators associated with adhering to "active" versus "passive" rehabilitation models.

DISCUSSION: This study addresses the lack of data comparing active versus passive therapies for hip fracture patients. Active training promotes voluntary muscle use, potentially boosting patient confidence. In contrast, electrical stimulation guarantees muscle pumping regardless of fatigue. If effective, this study will validate a new "dual protection" strategy. This will help establish an optimal rehabilitation model to solve the "dual crisis" of thrombosis and muscle loss.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: The study was pre-registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry on March 17, 2026. Trial Registration Number: ChiCTR2600120624.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Hip fracture in older adults causes a "dual crisis" of venous thromboembolism (VTE) and rapid muscle atrophy. Pharmacological prevention is effective but carries significant bleeding risks for these frail patients. Current physical prophylaxis is often too weak to restore muscle pump function.

title: Factor XI Inhibitor for Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism in Patients Undergoing Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Phase 2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Factor XI is critical for postoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE). Factor XI inhibition prevents VTE effectively in Western populations, yet its efficacy and safety in Chinese populations remain to be verified.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the efficacy and safety of a novel recombinant humanized factor XI inhibitor (KN060) in Chinese patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: In this multicenter, randomized, open-label, positive-controlled, phase 2 trial at 19 medical centers in China, 241 patients undergoing primary unilateral total knee arthroplasty were randomized to receive a single postoperative intravenous infusion of KN060 (2.5 mg/kg, 5.0 mg/kg, or 7.5 mg/kg) or subcutaneous enoxaparin (40 mg once daily). The study took place from December 19, 2023, through April 15, 2025, and these data were analyzed from from June 30, 2025, to September 27, 2025.

INTERVENTION: Single infusion of KN060 vs daily enoxaparin.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary efficacy outcome was VTE, assessed by mandatory digital subtraction angiography (DSA) of the operated leg on days 10 to 14. The principal safety outcome was a composite of major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding.

RESULTS: Of 241 patients enrolled, 213 were included in the efficacy analysis (157 were female [73.7%] and 56 were male [26.3%]; median [IQR] age, 68 [62-70] years). VTE occurred in 0 of 52 patients (0%) in the 2.5 mg/kg KN060 group, 1 of 52 patients (1.9%) in the 5.0 mg/kg group, and 1 of 54 patients (1.9%) in the 7.5 mg/kg group, as compared with 4 of 55 patients (7.3%) in the enoxaparin group. Each dose group of KN060 met the noninferiority end point. No major bleeding or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding occurred in any of the patients. Minor bleeding occurred in 1.8%, 3.6%, and 1.7% of the patients in the 2.5 mg/kg, 5.0 mg/kg, and 7.5 mg/kg KN060 groups, respectively, and in 3.5% of the patients in the enoxaparin group.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this randomized clinical trial of a factor XI inhibitor in Chinese populations, a single intravenous dose of KN060 was effective for the prevention of VTE after total knee arthroplasty and was associated with a low risk of bleeding.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06180889.
englishSummary: IMPORTANCE: Factor XI is critical for postoperative venous thromboembolism (VTE). Factor XI inhibition prevents VTE effectively in Western populations, yet its efficacy and safety in Chinese populations remain to be verified. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the efficacy and safety of a novel recombinant humanized factor XI inhibitor (KN060) in Chinese patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty.

title: Diagnostic performance of B-Flow ultrasound for preoperative assessment of hemodialysis arteriovenous fistula stenosis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of B-Flow imaging for vascular stenosis in arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) and, using contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) as the reference standard, to compare its value for lesion detection, quantitative measurement, and preinterventional assessment.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 50 patients with AVF stenosis who underwent ultrasound-guided balloon angioplasty. All patients underwent conventional B-mode ultrasound, color Doppler flow imaging (CDFI), B-Flow imaging, and CEUS before intervention. The number of stenotic lesions, luminal diameter at the stenotic site, and stenotic extent were compared across modalities. Pearson correlation, Bland-Altman analysis, and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) were used to assess agreement with CEUS. Changes in access flow volume (VolFlow) before and after angioplasty were analyzed with a paired t test.

RESULTS: Ninety-four stenotic lesions were identified. B-Flow showed complete agreement with CEUS for lesion detection and achieved the highest correlation for lesion count, luminal diameter, and stenotic extent (all P < 0.001), with the lowest measurement errors. It outperformed CDFI and conventional B-mode ultrasound in all three dimensions. After angioplasty, VolFlow increased significantly from 306.99 ± 99.71 mL/min to 831.64 ± 287.84 mL/min (P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: B-Flow provides more accurate and consistent preoperative assessment of AVF stenosis than CDFI and conventional B-mode ultrasound and may serve as a valuable noninvasive tool for perioperative evaluation and treatment planning.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 50 patients with AVF stenosis who underwent ultrasound-guided balloon angioplasty. All patients underwent conventional B-mode ultrasound, color Doppler flow imaging (CDFI), B-Flow imaging, and CEUS before intervention.

title: Enoxaparin 40 mg versus 60 mg for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in obese adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²) is an independent risk factor for venous thromboembolism (VTE). Fixed-dose thromboprophylaxis with low-molecular-weight heparins may result in inadequate prophylactic anticoagulant exposure. Although higher enoxaparin doses have been proposed in obese patients, evidence remains inconsistent.

OBJECTIVES: To compare attainment of prophylactic anti-factor Xa targets with enoxaparin 60 mg versus 40 mg in hospitalized adults with obesity.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials identified through searches of PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central from inception to November 2025, comparing enoxaparin 60 mg with the standard 40 mg regimen in hospitalized obese adults. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2. Risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated, and heterogeneity was assessed using I². Analyses were performed using R. The protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251181081).

RESULTS: Three RCTs enrolled 235 patients, of whom 225 contributed to the quantitative synthesis. Among the analyzed participants, 113 (50.2%) received enoxaparin 60 mg and 134 (59.6%) underwent bariatric surgery. Enoxaparin 60 mg was associated with a higher likelihood of achieving prophylactic anti-factor Xa targets than 40 mg (RR 2.17; 95% CI 1.22-3.85; p = 0.0082; I²=63.1%). Moderate heterogeneity reflected differences in clinical context, obesity severity, and timing of anti-factor Xa assessment. No VTE events were reported, and bleeding events were infrequent; however, the trials were not powered to assess clinical outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Enoxaparin 60 mg was associated with more consistent attainment of prophylactic anti-factor Xa levels than 40 mg in hospitalized adults with obesity. Higher-dose prophylactic regimens may optimize anticoagulant exposure, although randomized evidence remains insufficient to determine effects on clinical outcomes.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²) is an independent risk factor for venous thromboembolism (VTE). Fixed-dose thromboprophylaxis with low-molecular-weight heparins may result in inadequate prophylactic anticoagulant exposure. Although higher enoxaparin doses have been proposed in obese patients, evidence remains inconsistent.

title: Public Reporting of Vascular Quality Initiative Participation Among Vascular Surgery Training Programs: A Cross-Sectional Analysis of Website Disclosure.
abstract: BackgroundThe Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) promotes nationwide quality improvement and outcome benchmarking in vascular surgery. This study evaluated the extent to which accredited vascular surgery training programs in the United States publicly advertise participation in the VQI or other quality metrics on institutional websites.MethodsThis descriptive, cross-sectional study used quantitative content analysis. All Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME)-accredited vascular surgery programs were identified, and VQI participation was obtained from the Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) website. Program websites were systematically reviewed between December 2023 and January 2024 for mention of VQI participation, VQI star rating, or other quality metrics. VQI registry involvement was then compared between programs that mentioned participation and those that did not. Data were summarized using descriptive statistics.ResultsOf 119 programs, 105 (88.2%) participated in the VQI. Only 34 (32.4%) publicly mentioned participation, and 14 (13.3%) reported their star rating. Among participating programs, mention rates were higher in integrated-only (6/10, 60.0%) and dual-pathway (29/54, 53.7%) compared with fellowship-only programs (13/41, 31.7%). Programs that mentioned participation demonstrated greater involvement across all VQI registries. Over half of all programs (57.1%) reported other quality metrics, including the U.S. News & World Report rankings and the Intersocietal Accreditation Commission (IAC).ConclusionsAlthough VQI participation is nearly universal, public disclosure remains limited compared with other quality measures. Programs that do report participation demonstrate greater VQI registry involvement.

title: Determinants and Prognostic Impact of Infarct Growth After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Infarct growth (IG) on diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) may predict outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT); however, its value in real-world consecutive cohorts remains unclear. This study aimed to identify the determinants of IG and evaluate its predictive value for functional outcomes in consecutive EVT patients.

METHODS: We enrolled 262 patients who underwent EVT within 24 hours of stroke onset. Infarct volume was measured on pre-EVT DWI and 5 to 7-day follow-up DWI scans. The IG was defined as a volumetric difference. Multivariable regression and receiver operating characteristic curve analyses were performed to identify the determinants of IG and its predictive value for favorable outcomes.

RESULTS: Of the 262 patients, 133 achieved favorable outcomes. Pre-EVT DWI volume (B=0.414, P<0.001), National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) on admission (B=0.052, P<0.001), clot retrieval attempts (CRAs) (B=0.221, P<0.001), and successful reperfusion (B=-0.726, P<0.001) were independent determinants of post-EVT infarct volume. IG [odds ratio (OR)=0.015, P<0.001], NIHSS (OR=0.124, P<0.001), and successful reperfusion (OR=2.679, P<0.001) independently predicted favorable outcomes. The IG model [area under the curve (AUC)=0.808] performed comparably to the clinical model (AUC=0.807), and the combined model achieved the highest AUC (0.839).

CONCLUSIONS: Baseline DWI volume, NIHSS on admission, CRAs, and successful reperfusion are independent determinants of IG. The IG is a strong predictor of unfavorable outcomes with incremental value over clinical variables, supporting its use as a practical imaging biomarker for risk stratification after EVT.

This study aimed to identify the determinants of IG and evaluate its predictive value for functional outcomes in consecutive EVT patients. METHODS: We enrolled 262 patients who underwent EVT within 24 hours of stroke onset.

title: Anatomy- and venous dominance-guided outflow reconstruction for left-sided pediatric liver grafts: algorithm, technique, and donor pool expansion.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Variant left hepatic vein (LHV) and middle hepatic vein (MHV) anatomy complicates venous outflow reconstruction in pediatric living donor liver transplantation (LDLT). We evaluated an anatomy- and venous dominance-guided reconstruction strategy for left-sided grafts.

METHODS: We retrospectively studied 77 consecutive pediatric LDLTs using left-sided grafts (2017-2025). Donor venous anatomy was assessed with three-dimensional computed tomography, and reconstruction was performed using a predefined anatomy- and dominance-based algorithm.

RESULTS: Of the 77 recipients, 57 (74.0%) received left lateral segment (LLS) grafts and 20 (26.0%) received left lobe (LL) grafts. In the LLS cohort, LHV anatomy was classified as type 1 in 33 donors (57.9%), a type 1 variant in 1 (1.8%), type 2 in 13 (22.8%), and type 3 in 10 (17.5%). Type 1 required no reconstruction, type 2 underwent venoplasty, and type 3 required tailored reconstruction based on dominance; right hepatic vein-dominant grafts (n=6) underwent selective MHV inclusion to obtain a single, anatomically aligned unified outflow, whereas MHV-dominant grafts (n=4) required bench neo-LHV reconstruction. Among LL grafts, 12 donors (60.0%) had standard grafts with complete MHV inclusion, while 8 (40.0%) required modified procurement (subtotal, partial, or no MHV inclusion). Hepatic venous outflow obstruction (HVOO) occurred in three patients (3.9%); two LLS recipients (MHV-dominant type 3) required endovascular intervention, while one modified LL recipient was managed conservatively. No donor complications were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: Anatomy- and venous dominance-guided reconstruction safely expands the use of left-sided grafts, minimizes unnecessary reconstruction, maintains low HVOO rates, and broadens the pediatric living donor pool.

We evaluated an anatomy- and venous dominance-guided reconstruction strategy for left-sided grafts. METHODS: We retrospectively studied 77 consecutive pediatric LDLTs using left-sided grafts (2017-2025).

title: Impact of semaglutide on limb events: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract:
AIMS: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is a prevalent and debilitating complication of diabetes and obesity, yet it remains underrecognized and undertreated. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, such as semaglutide, have shown cardiovascular benefits, but their impact on peripheral vascular outcomes remains unclear.

OBJECTIVE: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the effect of semaglutide on limb events (LEs) in individuals with type 2 diabetes and/or overweight or obesity.

METHODS AND RESULTS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines, 19 randomized controlled trials encompassing 51 557 participants were included. Major limb events, prespecified and reported as safety outcomes in the original trials, were defined a priori as the primary outcome of this meta-analysis, comprising revascularizations, amputations, and PAD progression. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using a random-effects model. Semaglutide significantly reduced the risk of LEs compared with control interventions (OR 0.70; 95% CI 0.60-0.82; P < 0.0001), with no heterogeneity across studies (I² = 0%). Benefits were consistent across patient subgroups, in patients with diabetes (OR 0.70; 95% CI: 0.57-0.87; P = 0.001) or obesity (OR 0.71; 95% CI: 0.56-0.89; P = 0.003); oral formulation (0.71; 95% CI: 0.53-0.94; P = 0.02) or subcutaneous (0.68; 95% CI: 0.49-0.95; P = 0.02 and 0.71; 95% CI: 0.57-0.89; P = 0.003, for 1.0 and 2.4 mg, respectively); and regardless of background SGLT2 inhibitor use. Meta-regression showed no significant effect modification by age, body mass index, HbA1c, follow-up duration, or sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors use.

CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis suggests that semaglutide is associated with a significant reduction in major LEs across diverse populations and treatment settings, supporting a potential protective effect on limb-related vascular safety.

LAY SUMMARY: This meta-analysis evaluates whether semaglutide can reduce the risk of peripheral artery disease (PAD) complications in people with diabetes or obesity. By analysing data from 19 randomized controlled trials involving over 51 000 participants, the findings highlight semaglutide's potential role in lowering the risk of amputations, revascularizations, and disease progression, beyond its established benefits on weight loss and glycaemic control.Key findings:Semaglutide reduced the risk of PAD-related events by about 30% compared with other treatments.The protective effect was consistent across patient subgroups, formulations (oral or injectable), and irrespective of concomitant SGLT2 inhibitor use.

Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, such as semaglutide, have shown cardiovascular benefits, but their impact on peripheral vascular outcomes remains unclear. OBJECTIVE: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the effect of semaglutide on limb events (LEs) in individuals with type 2 diabetes and/or overweight or obesity.

title: Effect of a home-based calf neuromuscular electrical stimulation programme on walking capacity in adults with lower-extremity peripheral artery disease: the ELECTRO-PAD RCT.
abstract:
AIMS: This study aims to evaluate whether a 3-month home-based neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) programme improved maximal walking distance (MWD) in patients with lower-extremity peripheral artery disease (PAD) compared with usual care.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This multicentre randomized clinical trial included 73 adults with PAD and walking impairment from five French university hospitals between September 2019 and July 2022, with final follow-up in November 2022. Participants were randomized to a NMES group (n = 34) or a usual care group (n = 39) for 3 months. Both groups received standard medical management and lifestyle advice; the NMES group performed calf NMES sessions at home for 2-3 h/day, 5 days/week. The primary outcome was the 3-month change in treadmill MWD. Secondary outcomes included change in 6-min total walking distance. Of the 73 randomized participants [mean (SD) age, 62.8 (9.2) years; 14 (19.2%) women], 64 (88%) completed the 3-month follow-up. Mean treadmill MWD increased from 148.5 m at baseline to 254.1 m at 3 months in the NMES group and from 142.5 to 175.8 m in the usual care group [between-group difference, 69.9 m (95% CI, 10.8-129.0 m); P = 0.02]. The 6-min total walking distance improved from 371.0 to 405.4 m with NMES and from 342.5 to 348.8 m with usual care [between-group difference, 29.6 m (95% CI, 5.1-54.1 m); P = 0.02].

CONCLUSION: In patients with PAD and walking impairment, a 3-month home-based calf NMES programme significantly improved walking capacity. Further studies are needed to assess long-term effects.

REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03795103.

LAY SUMMARY: This study found that using a small electrical stimulation device at home for 3 months (2-3 h/day, 5 days/week) helped people with lower-extremity peripheral artery disease walk farther than those receiving only usual care including usual medical treatment and a brochure with general advice for an active lifestyle.Participants who used the device walked about 70 m farther on a treadmill than those who did not.They also improved their 6-min walking distance by about 30 m and tended to increase their daily physical activity level.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This multicentre randomized clinical trial included 73 adults with PAD and walking impairment from five French university hospitals between September 2019 and July 2022, with final follow-up in November 2022. Participants were randomized to a NMES group (n = 34) or a usual care group (n = 39) for 3 months.

title: Comprehensive risk factor control in Type 2 diabetes and incident peripheral artery disease.
abstract:
AIMS: Patients with Type 2 diabetes (T2D) are at an elevated risk of peripheral artery disease (PAD) compared with the general population. This study aimed to investigate whether joint risk factor control could mitigate the T2D-related excess risk of PAD.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This study included 14 458 participants with T2D who were initially free of cardiovascular disease and PAD and matched them with 56 961 control individuals from the UK Biobank cohort. Participants with T2D were categorized according to the number of risk factors controlled, including no current smoking, being physically active, healthy diet, and guideline-recommended levels of glycated haemoglobin, body mass index, blood pressure, LDL cholesterol, and urinary albumin. During a median follow-up of 11.9 years, 408 (2.8%) participants with T2D and 671 (1.2%) matched non-T2D individuals developed PAD. Among participants with T2D, a greater number of controlled risk factors were associated with lower PAD incidence (∼23% lower risk per additional factor). Compared with the matched non-T2D individuals, the hazard ratio [95% confidence interval (CI)] for PAD among participants with T2D gradually decreased from 2.49 (1.94, 3.19) for those with ≤2 risk factors controlled to 0.82 (0.51, 1.31) for those with ≥6 risk factors controlled. At 45 years of age, the difference in PAD-free survival time was on average -1.41 (95% CI -1.78, -1.03) years for participants with T2D who had ≤2 risk factors controlled and -0.11 (95% CI -0.38, 0.16) years for those who had ≥6 risk factors controlled compared with the non-T2D individuals.

CONCLUSION: Individuals with T2D who achieved optimal risk factor control had no excess risk of PAD than matched non-T2D counterparts. Efforts to promote comprehensive risk factor management in T2D are imperative for reducing the burden of PAD.

This study aimed to investigate whether joint risk factor control could mitigate the T2D-related excess risk of PAD. METHODS AND RESULTS: This study included 14 458 participants with T2D who were initially free of cardiovascular disease and PAD and matched them with 56 961 control individuals from the UK Biobank cohort.

title: The association between small dense low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and peripheral artery disease: a large-scale cohort study and meta-analysis.
abstract:
AIMS: High levels of small dense low-density lipoprotein (sdLDL) cholesterol are associated with an increased risk of ischaemic heart disease and stroke; however, data on peripheral artery disease are sparse and results inconclusive. We tested the hypothesis that higher levels of sdLDL cholesterol are associated with an increased risk of peripheral artery disease.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We studied 31 036 individuals free of lipid-lowering therapy, ischaemic heart disease, and ischaemic stroke with measurements of sdLDL cholesterol at study entry in 2013-17. During a median follow-up of 6.2 years, 155 were diagnosed with peripheral artery disease. The association was confirmed using the Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) ≤ 0.9 as an endpoint. Furthermore, a meta-analysis of current and previous studies was conducted in 46 748 individuals including 660 peripheral artery disease cases. Finally, as a comparison across different vascular beds, risk estimates for myocardial infarction and ischaemic stroke were calculated. In multivariable adjusted models per 1 mmol/L (39 mg/dL) higher sdLDL cholesterol, the hazard ratio for peripheral artery disease was 2.06 [95% confidence interval (95% CI): 1.45-2.92] while the odds ratio for ABI ≤0.9 was 1.53 (1.08-2.15). Fixed and random effect meta-analysis risk estimates for peripheral artery disease did not differ and was 1.62 (1.27-2.06) for the highest vs. the lowest quartile of sdLDL cholesterol. For the 91st-100th vs. the 1st-50th percentiles of sdLDL cholesterol, we found hazard ratios of 2.59 (1.55-4.33) for peripheral artery disease, 2.18 (1.58-3.02) for myocardial infarction, and 1.84 (1.37-2.48) for ischaemic stroke.

CONCLUSION: Higher levels of sdLDL cholesterol were robustly associated with increased risk of peripheral artery disease in the present study and in a meta-analysis.

We tested the hypothesis that higher levels of sdLDL cholesterol are associated with an increased risk of peripheral artery disease. METHODS AND RESULTS: We studied 31 036 individuals free of lipid-lowering therapy, ischaemic heart disease, and ischaemic stroke with measurements of sdLDL cholesterol at study entry in 2013-17.

title: Global, regional, and national perspectives on aortic aneurysm burden from 1992 to 2021: temporal patterns and age-period-cohort analyses.
abstract:
AIMS: To assess the global, regional, and country-specific trends in the burden of Aortic aneurysm (AA) from 1992 to 2021, with a focus on mortality rates, disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs), and socio-demographic inequalities.

METHODS AND RESULTS: The Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study data were utilized to calculate the age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR) and disability-adjusted life-year rates (ASDR) for AA in 204 countries. Temporal patterns were assessed using Joinpoint regression and age-period-cohort modelling. Cross-country inequalities were evaluated using the slope index of inequality (SII) and concentration index. Globally, the disease burden of AA showed a downward trend. The ASMR for AA decreased from 2.57 per 100 000 (95% uncertainty interval (UI): 2.37, 2.72) in 1992 to 1.86 per 100 000 (95% UI: 1.67, 2.00) in 2021 (EAPC: -1.36%). The age effect indicated that the age-specific mortality rate sharply escalates with age, but opposite trends exist in period and cohort effects. The gender-specific analysis confirmed a consistently higher burden in males, with more pronounced reductions in high socio-demographic index (SDI) regions. Cross-country analyses highlighted widening absolute inequalities (SII: 74.4 to 84.1) but reduced relative inequalities (concentration index: 0.48 to 0.28) over time.

CONCLUSION: There is a downward trend in the global burden of AA from 1992 to 2021, with significant disparities observed across genders, age groups, and SDI regions. These findings emphasize the need for prevention through base healthcare services, risk factor management, and equitable access to interventions to effectively address the disproportionate AA burden.

METHODS AND RESULTS: The Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study data were utilized to calculate the age-standardized mortality rates (ASMR) and disability-adjusted life-year rates (ASDR) for AA in 204 countries. Temporal patterns were assessed using Joinpoint regression and age-period-cohort modelling.

title: Postbariatric Abdominoplasty: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Complications and Predictors (2006-2025).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postbariatric abdominoplasty is increasingly performed after massive weight loss, but postoperative complication rates and associated risk factors remain variably reported. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates early postoperative complications and potential predictors in this population.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases were searched for English-language studies reporting early (≤90-day) complications after abdominoplasty following bariatric surgery. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using ROBINS-I or the Institute of Health Economics checklist. Pooled event rates were calculated using random-effects models, with subgroup and sensitivity analyses performed where appropriate.

RESULTS: Twenty-five studies including 3987 patients were analyzed. The pooled rate of any complication was 10.4% (95% CI, 3.4%-17.4%). Rates of seroma and wound dehiscence were 11.8% (95% CI, 9.5%-14.5%) and 13.1% (95% CI, 9.9%-18.1%), respectively. Venous thromboembolism occurred in approximately 0.9% of patients. Complication rates varied according to surgical technique, and obesity, particularly body mass index of 30 kg/m2 or higher, was associated with increased postoperative risk.

CONCLUSIONS: Postbariatric abdominoplasty is associated with clinically relevant but generally acceptable early morbidity. Patient selection, weight optimization, and standardized perioperative strategies may reduce complications. Higher-quality prospective studies using uniform outcome definitions are needed.

This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates early postoperative complications and potential predictors in this population. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases were searched for English-language studies reporting early (≤90-day) complications after abdominoplasty following bariatric surgery.

title: Ischemic Stroke Guidelines in Latin America: A Systematic AGREE II Appraisal.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of disability and death in Latin America, yet the methodological rigor and standardization of regional clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) remain inconsistent. Therefore, this study aimed to compare the quality and the diagnostic and pharmacological treatment recommendations of ischemic stroke CPGs across the region.

METHODS: Systematic literature review and guideline appraisal. Six evidence-based ischemic stroke CPGs developed by scientific societies or recognized public health entities in Latin America, selected from 2,339 identified records. The primary outcome was the methodological quality of the CPGs, independently evaluated using the AGREE II instrument. The secondary outcome was the alignment of their recommendations against the Canadian Stroke Best Practice Recommendations (CSBPR), which served as the highest-quality reference standard.

RESULTS: The analyzed CPGs originated from Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Cuba, Mexico, and Peru. Three CPGs (Colombia, Mexico, and Peru) were strongly recommended (scoring ≥60% in ≥4 AGREE II domains), and three (Brazil, Chile, and Cuba) were not recommended. The highest-rated domain was "clarity of presentation" (median: 83%), and the lowest was "applicability" (median: 33%). Critical therapeutic gaps were identified: no Latin American CPG included a target door-to-needle time of ≤30 minutes for intravenous thrombolysis, none mentioned tenecteplase, and notable discrepancies existed regarding endovascular thrombectomy care.

CONCLUSIONS: Latin American ischemic stroke CPGs show significant heterogeneity in methodological rigor and adherence to international evidence. Addressing critical gaps in acute management recommendations, particularly concerning rapid thrombolysis and thrombectomy, is vital to optimize regional stroke care.

PROSPERO REGISTRATION NUMBER: CRD42024506861.

title: Impact of BeFlared Bridging Stent Graft on Fluoroscopy and Procedure Time for Fenestrated Endovascular Aneurysm Repair.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to determine whether BeFlared bridging stent grafts (BSG) reduce fluoroscopy and procedure times during Fenestrated Endovascular Aneurysm Repair (FEVAR) compared to traditional BSGs. Secondary endpoints included radiation doses, contrast agent volumes, and 30-day outcomes.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort of patients treated with FEVAR from 2021 to 2026 was analyzed. Patients receiving BeFlared BSG (2025-2026) were compared with those treated with traditional BSGs (2021-2025). Demographics and procedural parameters, including fluoroscopy and procedure times, radiation doses, and contrast volumes, were collected. Technical success and 30-day outcomes, including target vessel instability (TVI), were assessed through clinical visits and computed tomography angiography.

RESULTS: A total of 48 patients with 177 target vessels (TVs) were included: 59 TVs treated with BeFlared BSG and 118 with Advanta/BeGraft. The BeFlared group had significantly shorter fluoroscopy time (54 (95% CI: 49-70) minutes vs. 79 (76-91) minutes; p < 0.01) and procedure time (169.5 minutes (153.5-187) vs. 208.5 minutes (196-247) ; p = 0.02). Significant differences were also noted in radiation dose (Air Kerma, 1500 (1191-1906) vs. 2448 (1725-2950) p = 0.01; DAP, 157.8 (131.3-192.8) vs. 260.7 (187.7-374.5) p = 0.04). Contrast volumes were similar (p = 0.5). Technical success was good in both groups (BeFlared 98.3% vs. Advanta/BeGraft 97.4%; p = 0.37); with TVI at 3% in the BeFlared group versus 2% in Advanta/BeGraft (p = 0.59). No stent-related endoleaks were observed.

CONCLUSIONS: BeFlared BSG use in FEVAR led to reduced fluoroscopy and procedure times, along with lower radiation doses, while both graft types demonstrated excellent short-term outcomes.

Secondary endpoints included radiation doses, contrast agent volumes, and 30-day outcomes. METHODS: A retrospective cohort of patients treated with FEVAR from 2021 to 2026 was analyzed.

title: Bilateral carotid stenosis diagnosed during shoulder arthroplasty with cerebral oximetry monitoring in the beach chair position.
abstract: The beach chair position, commonly used in shoulder surgery, may be associated with neurological complications. Significant desaturation can be detected using near-infrared spectroscopy to measure cerebral oxygenation. We report the case of an 88-year-old woman, ASA III, with cardiovascular and kidney disease who was scheduled for shoulder arthroplasty under INVOS™ (Medtronic) monitoring. While she was being placed in the beach-chair position she presented a significant, sustained loss of regional cerebral oxygen saturation (> 20%) that did not respond to fluid therapy or vasoconstrictors. The procedure was suspended, and cerebral CT angiography revealed critical stenosis of the right internal carotid artery and moderate stenosis of the left, with no evidence of acute ischaemia. This case shows that cerebral oximetry can be used to detect early hypoperfusion and the importance of using it to monitor at-risk patients.

title: Impact of targeted biological and synthetic therapies on cardiovascular risk in patients with psoriatic disease or spondyloarthritis: A scoping review.
abstract: Patients with psoriatic disease- psoriasis (PsO), psoriatic arthritis (PsA)-and spondyloarthritis (SpA) face elevated cardiovascular (CV) risk driven by chronic systemic inflammation. We aimed to map the CV safety landscape of biological and targeted synthetic drugs (b/tsDMARDs), evaluating reported major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), intermediate metabolic markers, and surrogate indicators of vascular health. Following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we searched PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane for randomized trials and extension studies with at least 52 weeks of cumulative exposure in PsO, PsA, and SpA. Altogether, 152 unique studies (reported across 183 publications) were included (PsO: 83; PsA: 41; SpA: 28). MACE and mortality rates remained low, predominantly clustering in individuals with high baseline CV risk. In PsO, interleukin (IL)-17 and IL-23 inhibitors showed a low hard arterial event incidence; exploratory assessments noted improved endothelial function (+2.1% flow-mediated dilation, p = 0.0022) with secukinumab, which cannot be assumed to translate into clinical event reduction. In PsA and SpA, Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitors exhibited infrequent MACE reporting, with sporadic adjudicated venous thromboembolism events in selected long-term extensions. Apremilast was associated with moderate weight reduction, while tofacitinib showed dose-dependent lipid increases with a stable total/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol ratio. Most evidence derived from long-term extension studies, carrying an inherent high risk of bias due to uncontrolled designs, patient attrition, and survivor selection. In conclusion, trial data document low absolute MACE rates, yet uncontrolled extension designs preclude definitive causal or comparative inferences. Given the systematic exclusion of multimorbid individuals, individualized baseline risk stratification and prospective cardiovascular-endpoint trials remain essential.

title: Abdominal aortic aneurysm in patients with malignancy: a population-based claims study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The co-occurrence of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) and malignancy is increasingly relevant in an aging population. However, the population-based co-prevalence, temporal relationship, and potential impact of concomitant cancer on AAA management remain incompletely understood.

METHODS: This retrospective population-based cohort study analyzed claims data from 3,088,992 individuals insured by a large German statutory health insurance provider (AOK PLUS) between 2010 and 2023. AAA and cancer cases were identified using standardized ICD-10-GM and OPS codes.

RESULTS: AAA was recorded in 13,494 individuals (period prevalence: 4,368/1,000,000) and cancer in 316,603 (10,249/100,000). A recorded diagnosis of both conditions during the observation period was identified in 4,745 patients (35.2% of patients with AAA), predominantly men (5:1). Among patients with incident diagnoses of both diseases (n = 531), AAA was recorded before cancer in 51.6%, cancer before AAA in 41.2%, and both simultaneously in 7.2%. At the first recorded AAA diagnosis, rupture was less frequently documented in patients with recorded cancer than in those without (2.9% vs. 5.9%; p < 0.001). Among patients with AAA, the proportion undergoing aneurysm repair was comparable between patients with and without recorded cancer (25.5% vs. 26.2%). Exploratory Kaplan-Meier analysis suggested a longer interval from first recorded AAA diagnosis to treatment in patients with recorded cancer (p = 0.041), while competing-risk analysis showed a slightly lower cumulative incidence of repair (p = 0.02) and more frequent death before repair (p < 0.01). Systemic cancer therapies were administered with similar frequency in AAA patients with cancer and the overall cancer cohort (26.5% vs. 28.1%).

CONCLUSION: The co-prevalence of AAA and malignancy is substantial. In patients with a recorded cancer diagnosis, exploratory analysis suggested a longer observed interval from the first recorded AAA diagnosis to aneurysm treatment, while competing-risk analysis showed a slightly lower cumulative incidence of repair and more deaths before repair. Cancer-related imaging may influence AAA detection, but disease onset and progression could not be assessed. These findings support coordinated vascular-oncology care and warrant further studies integrating detailed clinical and imaging data.

However, the population-based co-prevalence, temporal relationship, and potential impact of concomitant cancer on AAA management remain incompletely understood. METHODS: This retrospective population-based cohort study analyzed claims data from 3,088,992 individuals insured by a large German statutory health insurance provider (AOK PLUS) between 2010 and 2023.

title: Bleeding risk in patients with venous thromboembolism receiving concomitant direct oral anticoagulants and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients initiating direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) often use concomitant medications that may increase bleeding risk, such as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs); however, data on DOACs combined with SSRIs are limited.

OBJECTIVES: To compare the risk of major bleeding in venous thromboembolism (VTE) patients receiving DOACs with or without concomitant SSRI treatment. Secondary aims included major bleeding stratified by sex, age, type of DOAC, type of SSRI, and coexisting cancer as well as fatal bleeding and all-cause mortality.

METHODS: Nationwide Swedish register-based study of patients ≥18 years with first-time VTE initiating DOAC (apixaban or rivaroxaban), between 2014 and 2023. In a 1:2 propensity-score-matched cohort, Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for major bleeding, fatal bleeding, and all-cause mortality during 1-year follow-up.

RESULTS: Of 46,479 eligible patients, 4574 receiving DOAC + SSRI were matched to 9148 on DOAC-alone. Median age was 73 years, 65% were women. Major bleeding rate was 5.2 (95% confidence interval [CI], 4.4-6.1) per 100 patient-years on DOAC + SSRI and 4.4 (95% CI, 3.8-4.9) on DOAC-alone; HR 1.13 (95% CI, 0.92-1.39), with no significant difference between the groups. No difference was observed for fatal bleeding; HR 1.31 (95% CI, 0.86-2.02), whereas mortality rate was higher on DOAC + SSRI than on DOAC-alone; HR 1.28 (95% CI, 1.14-1.44).

CONCLUSION: The absence of differences in major bleeding is reassuring given the common use of concomitant treatment. Higher mortality on DOAC + SSRI, despite no difference in fatal bleeding, may reflect residual confounding but warrants further investigation.

title: [Acute Mesenteric Ischaemia: Endovascular and Surgical Management].
abstract:
AIM: Acute mesenteric ischaemia is a life-threatening emergency associated with high mortality and requires rapid diagnosis and immediate initiation of treatment. Early restoration of mesenteric perfusion is crucial for patient outcome. Revascularisation can be achieved by endovascular or open surgical techniques. The aim of this report is to illustrate different revascularisation strategies in two patients with acute superior mesenteric artery occlusion and to discuss their clinical indications and limitations.

INDICATIONS: Two patients with acute thrombotic occlusion of the superior mesenteric artery were treated using different revascularisation strategies. In the first patient, early diagnosis and the absence of radiological signs of advanced intestinal ischaemia led to primary endovascular aspiration thrombectomy. In the second patient, advanced intestinal ischaemia with transmural bowel necrosis and perforation necessitated open surgical revascularisation combined with intraoperative assessment and treatment of bowel viability.

METHODS: This study is a case-based video report supplemented by a selective narrative review of the literature. The diagnostic findings, technical aspects of revascularisation, management of intestinal viability, and postoperative courses are presented. The two treatment strategies are discussed in the context of the available literature. No systematic literature review or quantitative meta-analysis was performed.

CONCLUSION: Acute mesenteric ischaemia requires a rapid, time-critical, and interdisciplinary treatment approach. Endovascular treatment may be an appropriate minimally invasive option, particularly in patients with early diagnosis and without evidence of advanced intestinal ischaemia. Open surgical treatment remains essential in advanced or complex cases, particularly when bowel necrosis or perforation requires surgical exploration and resection. Current evidence suggests potential advantages of endovascular treatment; however, due to heterogeneous and predominantly retrospective data, general superiority of either endovascular or open surgical treatment cannot be established.
englishSummary: AIM: Acute mesenteric ischaemia is a life-threatening emergency associated with high mortality and requires rapid diagnosis and immediate initiation of treatment. Early restoration of mesenteric perfusion is crucial for patient outcome. Revascularisation can be achieved by endovascular or open surgical techniques.

title: Systematic Review of Patient Priorities and Shared Decision Making in Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease Treatment Decisions.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this review was to synthesise evidence on patient priorities, preferences for treatment, and shared decision making experiences in lower extremity peripheral artery disease (PAD) treatment decisions across intermittent claudication, chronic limb threatening ischaemia, and amputation level contexts.

DATA SOURCES: Key databases including MEDLINE and Embase.

REVIEW METHODS: This was a systematic review (PROSPERO ID: CRD420251106155). Key databases including MEDLINE and Embase were searched for English language studies published from 1 January 2000 to 17 December 2025. Eligible studies included adults with symptomatic PAD, reporting experiences, information needs, priorities, or decision making related to PAD treatment. Two reviewers independently screened studies, resolving disagreements by consensus with a third reviewer. Study quality was assessed using design appropriate tools. Qualitative and quantitative findings were integrated using a structured thematic narrative approach.

RESULTS: Thirty-four studies were included in the systematic review, comprising qualitative, mixed methods, observational registry or cohort, and stated preference studies, and one stepped wedge cluster randomised trial. Most qualitative and cohort studies were rated moderate to high quality. Participant reporting in the 34 studies was limited: seven studies (21%) did not report sex, two (6%) recruited men only, and most mixed sex studies recruited predominantly men; and 18 (53%) did not report ethnicity and, where reported, participants were predominantly White. Across heterogeneous studies, recurring patient valued domains included pain relief, walking ability, independence, emotional wellbeing, function, quality of life, treatment burden, risk, and uncertainty. Decision making processes were shaped by preferred involvement, trust, communication, clarity of options, and continuity of care. Studies identified a mismatch between patients' preferred and experienced decisional roles, with reported involvement lower than desired. Stated preference evidence showed heterogeneity in risk tolerance and treatment trade offs. Trial evidence reported improvements in shared decision making measures and patient knowledge after structured decision support and clinician training.

CONCLUSION: Patient valued outcomes and treatment trade offs vary across lower extremity PAD contexts and individuals. Shared decision making may help incorporate these priorities into treatment decisions, supported by tailored information, continuity of care, clinician training, and decision support tools.

DATA SOURCES: Key databases including MEDLINE and Embase. REVIEW METHODS: This was a systematic review (PROSPERO ID: CRD420251106155).

title: Predicting Morbidity, Mortality, Revision, and Ambulation in Patients Undergoing Major Lower Limb Amputation for Peripheral Arterial Disease or Diabetes Mellitus: The Case for Regional Level Clinical Prediction Models.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Several outcome prediction tools exist to support decision making for patients undergoing major lower limb amputation (MLLA). However, most predict a single outcome, are derived from registry level data, and lack external validation. The present study aimed to develop clinically focussed, multi-outcome prediction tools using granular regional data with immediate external validation on an international database.

METHODS: This study involved development, and internal and external validation of multivariable binomial and multinomial regression prediction models. All patients undergoing MLLA for ischaemic or diabetic indications between 1 January 2013 and 1 July 2023 at a single regional vascular hub were used for model development. Clinically focussed logistic multivariable binomial and multinomial regression models were developed predicting 30 day and 1 year mortality and revision, 30 day major morbidity or mortality, and best mobility achieved (binary and 3 category). Model complexity, crossvalidated receiver operating curve (ROC) discrimination and calibration were assessed and optimised, with the best performing models undergoing external validation on PERCEIVE study data. External validity was assessed using discrimination and calibration statistics, with one revision attempt permitted.

RESULTS: The development dataset included 609 patients (75.2% men, median age 69 years). Internal crossvalidated ROC values were 0.774 for 30 day mortality, 0.752 for 1 year mortality, 0.679 for 30 day revision, 0.707 for 1 year revision, 0.699 for 30 day major morbidity or mortality, 0.876 for binary best ambulation, and 0.752 for 3 category best ambulation predictions. All models were well calibrated. On external validation the ROC values were 0.616, 0.722, 0.617, 0.488, 0.697, 0.643, and 0.602, respectively.

CONCLUSION: The prediction models performed well for internal "regional" patient outcomes, especially for mortality and ambulation. On external validation, like other models externally validated on the PERCEIVE data, they failed to generalise to the wider population undergoing MLLA, except for 1 year mortality. Predicting patient outcomes from pre-operative variables remains challenging; however, regional level modelling may provide better performance over more general prediction tools.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Several outcome prediction tools exist to support decision making for patients undergoing major lower limb amputation (MLLA). However, most predict a single outcome, are derived from registry level data, and lack external validation. The present study aimed to develop clinically focussed, multi-outcome prediction tools using granular regional data with immediate external validation on an international database.

title: Association between the platelet to lymphocyte ratio and the clinical outcome of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate the association between platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio and clinical outcomes in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage. We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. Study quality was assessed using appropriate tools, and pooled estimates were calculated using a random-effects model with sensitivity and subgroup analyses. Ten studies involving patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage were included. The meta-analysis showed that a higher platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio was associated with an increased likelihood of poor functional outcome. In contrast, no clear association was observed between platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio and delayed cerebral ischemia in the pooled analysis. The odds ratios for pneumonia and deep vein thrombosis each came from a single independent study rather than from pooled meta-analytic analyses; these unpooled estimates therefore remain exploratory and should not be interpreted as combined effect sizes. Substantial heterogeneity was present across analyses, and sensitivity analyses suggested that the results for functional outcome and delayed cerebral ischemia were not entirely stable. The available evidence is limited by the small number of studies, heterogeneity in threshold values and outcome definitions, and geographic concentration of the included populations. In conclusion, the platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio may serve as a readily available prognostic marker in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, but current evidence is insufficient to support its routine clinical use. Further large, well-designed multinational studies are needed to establish optimal thresholds and to clarify its incremental value in prognostic assessment.

We searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library. title: Prevalence and associated factors of peripheral arterial disease in hemodialysis patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is common in hemodialysis patients and associated with adverse outcomes, but its prevalence and associated factors remain heterogeneous.

METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus, CINAHL, CNKI, and Wanfang were searched from inception to April 8, 2026. Cross-sectional and cohort studies reporting PAD prevalence or associated factors were included. Random-effects models were used. Heterogeneity was explored using subgroup, meta-regression, and sensitivity analyses.

RESULTS: The pooled prevalence was 23% (95%Confidence Intervals [CI], 20%∼26%) based on ankle brachial index ≤ 0.9, 42% (95%CI, 29%∼56%) based on ultrasonography or other imaging, and 19% (95%CI, 11%∼33%) based on clinical criteria. Both research regions and proportion of male were associated with heterogeneity. Factors associated with PAD included abdominal obesity (Odds Ratio [OR]=5.41), diabetes mellitus (OR=2.90), cardiovascular disease (OR=2.01), cerebrovascular disease (OR=1.91), male sex (OR=1.70), smoking (OR=1.64), hypertension (OR=1.34), C-reactive protein (OR=1.06), age (OR=1.04), low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (OR=1.02), dialysis vintage (OR=1.01), albumin (OR=0.97), high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (OR=0.94), Black race (OR=0.78), and serum creatinine (OR=0.75). Associations varied by diagnostic criteria.

CONCLUSIONS: PAD is common in hemodialysis patients, with prevalence varying substantially by diagnostic criteria and study settings. Several demographic and clinical characteristics were associated with PAD; however, most evidence was derived from cross-sectional studies and was of low or very low certainty. These findings should not be interpreted causally. Standardized diagnostic criteria and well-designed prospective studies are needed to improve the certainty and comparability of future evidence.

title: Research Progressin Vitamins as Potential Nutritional Intervention Targets for Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a highly fatal vascular disease,yet effective pharmacological interventions to halt its progression are currently lacking.In recent years,vitamins have garnered significant attention as potential nutritional intervention targets due to their diverse physiological functions.This review systematically summarizes the research progress in the correlation between vitamins and AAA pathogenesis,and delves into the roles of vitamins in modulating key pathological processes such as inflammation,oxidative stress,matrix degradation,vascular smooth muscle cell function,and vascular calcification.Furthermore,this review analyzes the limitations of available studies and outlines future directions for nutritional interventions in AAA,with the ultimate goal of providing novel insights and scientific evidence for formulating the prevention and treatment strategies for AAA.

title: Female Sex Is Associated With Increased Health Care Use and Revision Risk After Achilles Tendon Repair.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To evaluate sex-based differences in complications, health care use, and revision rates after Achilles tendon repair.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX Research Network. Adults undergoing primary Achilles tendon repair between 2015 and 2023 were identified, stratified by sex, and matched 1:1 using propensity scores. The primary outcome was revision Achilles tendon repair; secondary outcomes were postoperative complications, emergency department visits, inpatient admissions, and opioid prescriptions, assessed at 90-day and 2-year intervals. Follow-up duration was recorded for each cohort. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals were calculated, with significance set at P < .05.

RESULTS: A total of 11,251 patients were identified (68.2% men, 31.8% women). The mean follow-up was 82.0 days (men) and 81.8 days (women) for the 90-day analysis and 535.5 days (men) and 569.9 days (women) for the 2-year analysis, with a median follow-up that reached the full window in each cohort. Within 90 days postoperatively, both male and female patients experienced similar rates of wound dehiscence (P = .098), infections (P = .835), and deep vein thrombosis (P = .677). Female patients had significantly more postoperative emergency department visits (7.8% vs 5.6%, OR 1.42, P = .001) and opioid prescriptions (29.4% vs 26.8%, OR 1.14, P = .025) than males. At 2 years, female patients also showed a higher rate of revision surgery (4.4% vs 3.4%, OR 1.31, P = .048).

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with male patients, female patients undergoing Achilles tendon repair had significantly higher rates of health care use (emergency department visits and opioid prescriptions) within 90 days and revision surgery within 2 years postoperatively. Differences in revision were small and may not be clinically meaningful.

LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, retrospective cohort study.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the TriNetX Research Network. Adults undergoing primary Achilles tendon repair between 2015 and 2023 were identified, stratified by sex, and matched 1:1 using propensity scores.

title: Prevalence of a Bicuspid Aortic Valve Among Patients Undergoing Surgery for Aortic Dissection and the Influence of Native Aortic Valve Morphology on Surgical Outcome: A Retrospective Observational Study.
abstract: Background A bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is associated with aortopathy and an increased risk of aortic dissection, but most patients presenting with dissection have a tricuspid aortic valve. We determined the proportion of patients with BAV among those undergoing surgery for aortic dissection and compared operative strategy, morbidity, mortality, and survival by native valve morphology. Methods This retrospective single-centre study included 132 consecutive patients who underwent surgery for aortic dissection between 2000 and 2025. Dissection was diagnosed by CT, and valve morphology (bicuspid or tricuspid) was determined by intraoperative inspection. Categorical variables were compared using Fisher's exact test, continuous variables using the Mann-Whitney U test, and survival using Kaplan-Meier analysis with the log-rank test. Results The mean age was 47.6 ± 13.0 years, and 102 patients (77.3%) were male. Supracoronary ascending aortic replacement (SCAAR) was performed in 102 patients (77.3%) and a Bentall procedure in 30 (22.7%). Ten patients (7.6%, 95% CI: 4.2-13.4%) had a bicuspid valve. Assuming a general-population BAV prevalence of 0.5-2%, this corresponds to an estimated relative risk of dissection of about 4-16. Overall mortality was 14.4% (19 patients), including 17 in-hospital deaths (12.9%). Mean follow-up was 4.70 ± 4.80 years (range: 0-22). Age, ICU stay, and hospital stay did not differ between the groups. Bicuspid patients more often underwent a Bentall procedure (50.0% vs 20.5%, p = 0.047) and had higher mortality (40.0% vs 12.3%, p = 0.037). Survival differed between the groups (log-rank χ² = 5.100, p = 0.024), with the divergence occurring early after surgery. Conclusions BAV was present in 7.6% of patients undergoing surgery for aortic dissection, which suggests a higher relative risk of dissection than in the general population, although most dissections occurred with tricuspid valves. Bicuspid morphology was associated with more frequent root replacement and higher early mortality.

We determined the proportion of patients with BAV among those undergoing surgery for aortic dissection and compared operative strategy, morbidity, mortality, and survival by native valve morphology. Methods This retrospective single-centre study included 132 consecutive patients who underwent surgery for aortic dissection between 2000 and 2025.

title: Pharmacologic bridging to PTA in hyperkalemic hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVF: Impact on day surgery workflow and procedural feasibility.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hyperkalemia can delay percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) when dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) limit dialysis. We evaluated pharmacologic potassium lowering as a bridge to PTA on the day of presentation.

METHODS: We retrospectively screened 871 PTA encounters in a day surgery unit; 122 met potassium ⩾5.5 mmol/L. Six underwent emergency dialysis and 116 received pharmacologic bridge treatment. The primary endpoint was PTA on the day of presentation without rescue dialysis before PTA.

RESULTS: The primary endpoint occurred in 110/116 encounters (94.8%; 95% CI, 89.1%-98.1%). Paired potassium values were retrievable in 53 patients, decreasing from 6.14 ± 0.42 to 5.10 ± 0.65 mmol/L (p < 0.001). Technical, clinical, and immediate dialysis success were 100%, 98.1%, and 96.2%, respectively, in this detailed cohort. Numeric potassium after treatment was undocumented before the PTA decision in 57/116 encounters.

CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacologic bridging was feasible, but incomplete retrospective reassessment limits conclusions about safety and uniform biochemical reassessment.

We evaluated pharmacologic potassium lowering as a bridge to PTA on the day of presentation. METHODS: We retrospectively screened 871 PTA encounters in a day surgery unit; 122 met potassium ⩾5.5 mmol/L.
