title: Real-World 30-day Outcomes Following Commercial Adoption of the GORE EXCLUDER Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis: A National Medicare Analysis.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) recently received FDA approval as the first off-the-shelf endovascular device for complex aneurysmal disease involving the visceral aorta. Prior to formal FDA approval, a pivotal pre-approval analysis demonstrated high procedural success, low perioperative morbidity, and no perioperative mortality. Using Medicare Fee-for-Service (FFS) data, we sought to evaluate real-world adoption patterns and 30-day outcomes following TAMBE implementation nationwide.

METHODS: Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries undergoing TAMBE between October 2024 and December 2025 were identified using the TAMBE-specific ICD-10-PCS code (X2VE3SA). Outcomes were compared to a contemporaneous cohort undergoing ≥4-vessel F/BEVAR in 2023, the year preceding TAMBE approval. Primary outcomes included 30-day mortality, stroke, myocardial infarction (MI), acute kidney injury (AKI), spinal cord ischemia (SCI), bowel ischemia, and reintervention, and were analyzed using Fine-Gray competing-risk regressions with adjustment for demographic, clinical, and procedural characteristics. Pre-specified sub-analyses examined outcomes by aortic indication, hospital procedure volume, and adoption period. Consistent with CMS small-cell suppression policy, any outcome frequencies <11 events were masked and not reported.

RESULTS: The primary cohort consisted of 869 patients treated at 351 hospitals, compared with 678 patients undergoing 4-vessel F/BEVAR. TAMBE was associated with significantly higher unadjusted 30-day mortality (6.7% vs. 4.0%; P=.02), though this difference did not persist after adjustment (adjusted HR 1.37 [0.85-2.21]). No differences were observed in stroke (<1.3% vs. <1.6%), MI (2.0% vs. <1.6%), AKI (7.2% vs. 6.9%) or SCI (5.0% vs. 4.1%) (all P>.05). The majority of implanting hospitals (N=195; 56%) performed a single TAMBE during the study period, and 30-day outcomes did not differ significantly by hospital volume after adjustment. A sensitivity analysis restricted to unambiguously coded, elective TAMBE cases compared with elective F/BEVAR showed similarly elevated 30-day mortality (6.8% vs. 4.0%), albeit not statistically different following adjustment (aHR 1.46 [0.75-2.84]).

CONCLUSION: In this national analysis of Medicare FFS beneficiaries, real-world 30-day outcomes following TAMBE in the first year-plus of commercial availability were notably worse than those reported in the pivotal trial and early single-institution post-market series, with a nearly 7% 30-day mortality rate that persisted across indications, hospital volumes, and time periods. The rapid dissemination of TAMBE to over 351 hospitals, most performing only a single procedure, highlights a fundamental tension between the device's off-the-shelf accessibility and the institutional readiness required for safe deployment, underscoring the need for ongoing post-market surveillance, structured proctorship programs, and a more deliberate approach to patient and operator selection as TAMBE adoption continues.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: The Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) recently received FDA approval as the first off-the-shelf endovascular device for complex aneurysmal disease involving the visceral aorta. Prior to formal FDA approval, a pivotal pre-approval analysis demonstrated high procedural success, low perioperative morbidity, and no perioperative mortality. Using Medicare Fee-for-Service (FFS) data, we sought to evaluate real-world adoption patterns and 30-day outcomes following TAMBE implementation nationwide.

title: Risk and Outcomes of Acute Aortic Events in Patients With Polycystic Kidney Disease.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluated whether polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is associated with an increased risk of life-threatening acute aortic events (AAEs) and adverse clinical outcomes.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective cohort study used the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) from 2000 to 2022. Patients with PKD were propensity score-matched 1 : 10 to controls from an age- and sex-matched control pool. The mean follow-up was 9.5 years. The primary outcome was the incidence of AAE, defined as aortic rupture, aortic dissection, or death due to aortic disease. Secondary outcomes were in-hospital and post-discharge complications. The matched cohort comprised 3,655 patients with PKD and 36,550 controls. PKD was associated with significantly increased risks of aortic rupture (hazard ratio [HR] 4.20; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.74-10.16), aortic dissection (HR 2.31; 95% CI 1.50-3.54), and death due to aortic disease (HR 3.82; 95% CI 2.02-7.23). Among 40,995 admissions for AAEs, patients with PKD had a higher risk of new-onset dialysis (odds ratio 2.59; 95% CI 1.13-5.91). After discharge, patients with PKD also had higher risks of stroke, readmission, and new-onset maintenance dialysis than controls.

CONCLUSIONS: PKD was associated with increased risks of life-threatening AAEs and subsequent adverse outcomes. These findings support heightened clinical awareness and risk-based cardiovascular assessment in select high-risk patients.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: This study evaluated whether polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is associated with an increased risk of life-threatening acute aortic events (AAEs) and adverse clinical outcomes. METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective cohort study used the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) from 2000 to 2022. Patients with PKD were propensity score-matched 1 : 10 to controls from an age- and sex-matched control pool.

title: Association Between Adjunctive Single-Ingredient Diosmin Prescribing and Short-Term Clinical Outcomes in Acute Lower-Extremity Superficial Vein Thrombosis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To estimate the association between documented adjunctive single-ingredient diosmin prescribing and short-term clinical outcomes in adults with acute lower-extremity superficial vein thrombosis.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective 48-hour landmark cohort study of 1,820 consecutive adults with duplex-confirmed acute lower-extremity superficial vein thrombosis treated from January 1, 2021, through December 31, 2025. Exposure was a diosmin prescription issued within 48 hours and intended for at least 7 days. The primary outcome was complete resolution or marked clinical improvement at the in-person assessment closest to day 14 within days 10 to 18. Missing baseline covariates were multiply imputed, and propensity scores were estimated within 20 imputed data sets. Stabilized inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting targeted the average treatment effect under measured-confounding assumptions. Secondary outcomes, including day-7 pain, were exploratory.

RESULTS: Diosmin was prescribed to 910 patients and not prescribed to 910. Primary improvement occurred in 728/910 (80.0%) and 669/910 (73.5%), respectively. Weighted standardized probabilities were 79.5% (95% confidence interval, 76.8%-82.2%) and 74.7% (71.8%-77.6%), yielding a risk difference of 4.8 percentage points (1.2-8.4) and a risk ratio of 1.06 (1.01-1.12). The E-value was 1.31 for the point estimate and 1.11 for the confidence limit. Excluding 142 patients with concomitant distal deep vein thrombosis gave a similar estimate (risk difference, 4.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, 1.3-8.5). Exploratory day-7 pain-response probabilities were 75.0% and 61.5% after imputation, weighting, and marginal standardization. Thrombotic and bleeding estimates were imprecise.

CONCLUSIONS: Documented adjunctive diosmin prescribing was associated with a small increase in short-term clinical improvement. Clinical importance is uncertain, and relatively weak unmeasured confounding could explain the primary association. The exploratory pain finding is hypothesis-generating. These data are insufficient to support routine diosmin use or substitution for guideline-directed anticoagulation; adequately powered randomized trials are needed.

METHODS: We conducted a single-center retrospective 48-hour landmark cohort study of 1,820 consecutive adults with duplex-confirmed acute lower-extremity superficial vein thrombosis treated from January 1, 2021, through December 31, 2025. Exposure was a diosmin prescription issued within 48 hours and intended for at least 7 days.

title: Transcarotid Artery Revascularization in Patients with Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis Demonstrates Excellent Outcomes: A Decade Review of Three Stroke Centers.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) represents an alternative to carotid endarterectomy (CEA) for high-grade carotid artery stenosis treatment. We compared perioperative safety, long-term neurologic and cardiovascular outcomes, and durability after TCAR and CEA across three stroke centers.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

METHODS: We analyzed CEA and TCAR procedures for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis from January 2017 through February 2026 across three institutions. One-to-one nearest-neighbor propensity score matching was performed without replacement. Thirty-day outcomes were compared using the exact McNemar test. Long-term outcomes were evaluated using Cox regression with robust variance estimates. Fine-Gray regression was used to treat death as a competing event for nonfatal outcomes.

RESULTS: The final cohort included 889 procedures, 750 CEAs and 139 TCARs. Matching yielded 136 balanced pairs. No ipsilateral stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), myocardial infarction (MI), or death occurred within 30 days after TCAR, and no 30-day outcome differed significantly between matched groups. In adjusted analyses of the full cohort, TCAR was associated with mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.57; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07-2.31), stroke or death (aHR, 1.64; 95% CI, 1.13-2.36), and the composite of TIA, stroke, MI, or death (aHR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.11-2.24). After matching, these associations did not reach statistical significance. Median follow-up in the matched cohort was 4.0 years. Long-term neurologic outcomes also did not differ significantly. Restenosis did not differ significantly (subdistribution HR, 1.43; 95% CI, 0.62-3.30; P = 0.399), and one reintervention occurred in each matched group.

CONCLUSION: Among selected asymptomatic patients, TCAR had low perioperative event rates. After matching, no significant differences from CEA were detected in long-term neurologic outcomes, mortality, composite outcomes, restenosis, or reintervention, while late MI remained higher after TCAR. These findings support TCAR as an attractive revascularization option when CEA is less suitable.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) represents an alternative to carotid endarterectomy (CEA) for high-grade carotid artery stenosis treatment. We compared perioperative safety, long-term neurologic and cardiovascular outcomes, and durability after TCAR and CEA across three stroke centers. DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

title: One-Year Results From the EMBRACE Registry Evaluating the GORE VIABAHN VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis during BEVAR for Complex Abdominal and Thoracoabdominal Aneurysms.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The stability of bridging stents is critical to ensure the effectiveness and safety of branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) for complex and thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAA). The goal of this multicenter registry was to assess the clinical performance and safety of the GORE VIABAHN VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis (VBX Stent Graft) as a bridging stent in BEVAR.

METHODS: The EMBRACE registry is a multicenter study across 14 European centers with retrospective enrollment and prospective follow-up. Patients were divided into BEVAR and fenestrated endovascular aneurysm repair (FEVAR) arms. This analysis reports the BEVAR cohort, which included patients receiving the VBX Stent Graft as a bridging stent for at least 1 visceral vessel. The primary endpoint was patient-level primary patency at 12 months. Secondary endpoints included technical success, reintervention, and target vessel patency assessed annually for up to 5 years. Secondary safety outcomes included major adverse events and aneurysm-related mortality.

RESULTS: A total of 165 patients (69.1% male, mean age 72.5 ± 9 years) were enrolled, receiving 454 VBX Stent Grafts (26.0% celiac trunk, 28.9% superior mesenteric artery (SMA), 21.8% left renal, and 23.3% right renal artery). VBX Stent Graft technical success was 99.6%. Thirty-day mortality was 7.9%, with major adverse events in 15.2% (1.8% respiratory failure, 7.3% renal function deterioration, 0.6% bowel ischemia, 4.2% paraplegia, and 1.8% major stroke). Freedom from aneurysm-related mortality was 92.1% at 30 days and 90.2% at 1 year. Freedom from patient-level VBX-related reintervention was 91.7%. Patient-level primary patency and secondary patency were 97.7% and 98.5%, respectively. Freedom from target vessel instability at the patient level was 90.4%.

CONCLUSION: Short-term findings from this multicenter registry confirm that the VBX Stent Graft is a safe and effective bridging stent for BEVAR, demonstrating high technical success, excellent 1-year patency, and low rates of target vessel instability. Ongoing follow-up will evaluate mid-term durability.Clinical ImpactBridging stent performance is fundamental to the success of branched endovascular repair, yet multicenter, real-world data remain limited. This analysis from the EMBRACE registry demonstrates high technical reliability, excellent 1-year target vessel patency, and low rates of VBX Stent Graft-related reintervention. Technical failures were uncommon and were primarily associated with inadequate distal landing zones, highlighting the importance of procedural planning. These findings provide clinicians with contemporary evidence supporting the VBX Stent Graft as a safe and effective bridging stent for BEVAR and may inform procedural decision-making to optimize target vessel durability.

The goal of this multicenter registry was to assess the clinical performance and safety of the GORE VIABAHN VBX Balloon Expandable Endoprosthesis (VBX Stent Graft) as a bridging stent in BEVAR. METHODS: The EMBRACE registry is a multicenter study across 14 European centers with retrospective enrollment and prospective follow-up.

title: Revascularisation Strategies in Dialysis-Dependent Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischaemia.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We reviewed dialysis-specific evidence on bypass and endovascular treatment for chronic limb-threatening ischaemia to assess how the available comparisons inform the initial revascularisation decision.

METHODS: We searched four bibliographic databases and one trial register through 12 September 2026. We synthesised comparisons without meta-analysis and graded certainty for eight outcomes. We applied nested restrictions by excluding mixed-open comparisons, retaining adjusted or matched comparisons, then excluding success-selected cohorts and abstract-only reports.

RESULTS: Sixteen reports represented 13 study families. Comparisons differed in whether they captured treatment attempted, treatment received or successful procedures. Selected comparisons reported associations favouring bypass for limb or wound outcomes. In the as-treated dialysis analysis of the Best Endovascular versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients with Critical Limb Ischaemia trial, single-segment great saphenous vein bypass was associated with lower reintervention hazard (hazard ratio 0.48, 95% confidence interval 0.25-0.94) and higher mortality (1.69, 1.06-2.70) than endovascular treatment. The estimate for amputation or death was imprecise (1.47, 0.95-2.27). Death handling for reintervention was unclear. Mixed-open comparisons suggested lower early amputation and more bleeding and wound complications. After successive restrictions, the remaining evidence did not establish an initial-strategy preference.

CONCLUSIONS: In dialysis-dependent CLTI, SSGSV bypass was associated with lower reintervention hazard but higher mortality in the as-treated BEST-CLI comparison; other favourable limb findings came from non-equivalent cohorts. These associations do not establish a net advantage or preferred initial strategy. Decisions should weigh limb threat, anatomy, conduit suitability, expected survival, perioperative risk, functional goals and treatment burden.

METHODS: We searched four bibliographic databases and one trial register through 12 September 2026. We synthesised comparisons without meta-analysis and graded certainty for eight outcomes.

title: Extensive Cerebral Infarction Following Cerebral Vasospasm Despite Repeated Endovascular Treatment in a Patient With Twig-Like Middle Cerebral Artery.
abstract: Twig-like middle cerebral artery (T-MCA) is a rare cerebrovascular anomaly characterized by replacement of the M1 segment with a plexiform arterial network. Altered cerebral hemodynamics associated with this vascular configuration may contribute to aneurysm formation and hemorrhagic events. However, the influence of cerebral vasospasm on collateral-dependent cerebral perfusion in patients with T-MCA has received little attention. We report a 43-year-old woman who presented with subarachnoid hemorrhage caused by rupture of an anterior communicating artery aneurysm associated with left T-MCA. Cerebral angiography demonstrated markedly limited antegrade flow through the anomalous arterial network, whereas delayed arterial-phase images showed collateral perfusion of the distal middle cerebral artery territory through leptomeningeal pathways arising from the anterior cerebral artery territory. Coil embolization was successfully performed. During the subsequent course, recurrent cerebral vasospasm was treated with repeated intra-arterial fasudil infusions; however, the patient developed extensive cerebral infarction involving both the anterior and middle cerebral artery territories despite repeated endovascular treatment. These findings suggest that cerebral perfusion in patients with T-MCA may depend, at least in part, on collateral circulation from adjacent vascular territories. This case illustrates the potential vulnerability of collateral-dependent cerebral perfusion during vasospasm and suggests that recognition of collateral-dependent perfusion patterns may be important when evaluating and managing vasospasm after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage.
englishSummary: Twig-like middle cerebral artery (T-MCA) is a rare cerebrovascular anomaly characterized by replacement of the M1 segment with a plexiform arterial network. Altered cerebral hemodynamics associated with this vascular configuration may contribute to aneurysm formation and hemorrhagic events. However, the influence of cerebral vasospasm on collateral-dependent cerebral perfusion in patients with T-MCA has received little attention.

title: Complex Endovascular Repair for Genetically-Triggered Aortic Disease in Italy (CENTRAL Multicentric Registry).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) in patients with genetically triggered aortic disease and connective tissue disorders (CTDs) remains controversial due to concerns regarding long-term durability and disease progression. This multicenter study aimed to evaluate early and mid-term outcomes of F/BEVAR in patients with CTD treated for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs).

METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included all consecutive CTD patients with genetically triggered aortic disease undergoing F/BEVAR for TAAA between 2013 and 2024 at 12 Italian centers. Primary endpoints were technical and clinical success, early and mid-term survival, and major adverse events (MAEs). Secondary endpoints included target vessel instability and the need for reintervention. Survival and freedom from adverse events were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 45 CTD patients (62.2% male; mean age, 56.4 ± 11.7 years) were treated with F/BEVAR. Marfan syndrome was present in 80% of patients, and 68.9% were treated for post-dissection TAAA. Most patients presented with type II TAAA (91.1%), and 88.9% had undergone at least 1 prior aortic operation. Technical and clinical success were achieved in 86.6% and 82.2% of cases, respectively. Early mortality and MAEs occurred in 4.4% of patients. During a mean clinical follow-up of 35.0 ± 33.9 months, estimated overall survival at 12, 24, and 36 months was 90.0%, 86.7%, and 79.2%, respectively, with no aorta-related deaths. At a mean imaging follow-up of 33.8 ± 32.2 months, target vessel patency was 98.8%. Target vessel instability occurred in 40% of patients, and 42.2% required 1 or more secondary interventions. Reintervention-free survival at 12, 24, and 36 months was 75.6%, 72.4%, and 59.0%, respectively. No baseline, anatomic, or procedural variable independently predicted late adverse outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of CTD patients, predominantly treated in complex redo settings, F/BEVAR demonstrated acceptable early and mid-term outcomes. Late adverse events and reinterventions were frequent but consistent with the natural history of CTD-related aortic disease and were not driven by identifiable baseline factors. These findings support the role of F/BEVAR as a valuable approach within a comprehensive, lifelong management strategy for CTD patients rather than as a definitive alternative to open surgery (OS).Clinical ImpactPatients with genetically triggered aortic disease often require multiple interventions throughout their lifetime because of the progressive nature of the underlying aortopathy. In this context, fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) should not be considered an alternative to open surgery, but rather a complementary approach within the long-term management of these patients. This multicenter study provides one of the largest dedicated experiences with F/BEVAR in this challenging population, showing that acceptable early and mid-term outcomes can be achieved even in complex redo and post-dissection settings. These findings support the integration of endovascular techniques into individualized, lifelong aortic treatment strategies at experienced centers, acknowledging the need for continued surveillance and secondary interventions.

This multicenter study aimed to evaluate early and mid-term outcomes of F/BEVAR in patients with CTD treated for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs). METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included all consecutive CTD patients with genetically triggered aortic disease undergoing F/BEVAR for TAAA between 2013 and 2024 at 12 Italian centers.

title: Machine Learning Versus Traditional Methods for Predicting Venous Thromboembolism After Surgery: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative venous thromboembolism remains a major cause of preventable morbidity after surgery, and established risk scores may perform inconsistently across surgical populations.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies comparing machine learning with traditional risk models for postoperative venous thromboembolism prediction. Risk-of-bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI. The primary outcome was discrimination measured by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve. Bayesian random-effects network meta-analysis estimated mean differences versus Caprini with 95% credible intervals. Best and worst-version analyses explored the impact of within-study multiplicity, with subgroup analyses by cancer surgery and procedure type.

RESULTS: Eighteen studies including 177 656 validation patients were included. Meta-ensembles showed the largest improvement compared with Caprini in the best-version analysis (mean difference in AUROC, 0.232; 95% credible interval, 0.129-0.334), with a similar finding in the worst-version analysis (0.237; 0.123-0.351). Several other machine learning classes also had higher AUROC estimates than Caprini, whereas most traditional scores and surgeon judgement did not. Geneva showed lower performance than Caprini. Meta-ensembles ranked first overall, while Caprini and Geneva ranked 14th and last, respectively. Meta-ensembles and boosting models had higher AUROC than Caprini in both cancer surgery analyses; in general surgery, no model class showed higher performance than Caprini in the worst-version analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Machine learning models, particularly meta-ensembles, showed higher reported discrimination than traditional scores, but evidence remains limited by heterogeneity, inconsistent calibration reporting, sparse decision-analytic evaluation and infrequent external validation. Clinical adoption requires external validation and demonstration of real-world net benefit.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Postoperative venous thromboembolism remains a major cause of preventable morbidity after surgery, and established risk scores may perform inconsistently across surgical populations. METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies comparing machine learning with traditional risk models for postoperative venous thromboembolism prediction. Risk-of-bias was assessed with PROBAST + AI.

title: Brain-computer interfaces for traumatic brain injury and spinal cord injury: Lesion-pattern matching, functional restoration, and clinical translation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are increasingly being developed for clinically relevant assessment, communication, rehabilitation, and functional restoration after central nervous system injury. However, their clinical roles differ substantially across injury types. This narrative review examines BCI applications in traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) using an injury-pattern-guided framework that links residual neural architecture with clinical tasks, interface selection, and outcome assessment.

MAIN BODY: In SCI, motor intention and cortical activity may remain accessible despite disruption of descending pathways, supporting motor-intention decoding, brain-controlled functional electrical stimulation, neuroprosthetic control, and brain-spine interfaces. In TBI, diffuse and heterogeneous network dysfunction shifts the clinical emphasis toward detection of covert consciousness, assisted communication, neurofeedback, and multimodal rehabilitation. We compare non-invasive, endovascular, electrocorticographic, and intracortical recording approaches; summarize evoked-response, motor-imagery, and continuous decoding paradigms; and distinguish functional substitution from closed-loop restoration of an individual's own movements. Recent invasive systems have supported the restoration of grasping, standing, and walking in selected individuals with SCI, whereas evidence in TBI remains concentrated on brain-state assessment and low-bandwidth communication.

CONCLUSION: Clinical translation will require careful candidate selection, stable long-term recordings, effective bidirectional feedback, clinically meaningful real-world outcomes, ethical oversight, and sustained technical support. Disease-specific translational pathways, rather than a universal BCI model, are likely to provide the most practical route to routine clinical use after central nervous system injury.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are increasingly being developed for clinically relevant assessment, communication, rehabilitation, and functional restoration after central nervous system injury. However, their clinical roles differ substantially across injury types. This narrative review examines BCI applications in traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) using an injury-pattern-guided framework that links residual neural architecture with clinical tasks, interface selection, and outcome assessment.

title: Sex-specific differences in patient-prosthesis mismatch following valve-in-valve transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
abstract: Female sex is associated with increased rates of mortality and readmission following transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and is a risk factor for patient-prosthesis mismatch (PPM). Valve-in-valve (ViV) TAVI for treatment of degenerated bioprosthetic valves has a greater risk of PPM. We sought to determine if sex-specific differences exist in rates of PPM following ViV-TAVI. This retrospective study analyzed 77 patients who underwent ViV-TAVI at Kettering Health from 2015 to 2021, evaluating PPM incidence and bioprosthetic valve fracture (BVF) utilization. Indexed effective orifice area following ViV-TAVI was compared between females and males using an unpaired t test. Fisher exact test assessed the association between BVF and PPM for the overall cohort and within each sex. Statistical analyses were performed using R software. Males represented 57% of patients (body mass index = 28.8 kg/m2), while females comprised 43% (body mass index = 29.1 kg/m2). There was no significant difference in average indexed effective orifice area between females and males (P = .370). BVF rates were similar between sexes (33.3% in females; 29.6% in males), with an overall reduction in PPM (P = .028) and in females (P = .029). Cramér's V showed a moderate association between BVF and PPM in the overall cohort (0.305) and females (0.475), with a weaker association in males (0.183). Similar rates of PPM between sexes suggest that appropriate patient selection and valve sizing are crucial in PPM prevention. The significant reduction of PPM with BVF in females calls for further research into sex-specific outcomes and optimization of ViV-TAVI results.

Valve-in-valve (ViV) TAVI for treatment of degenerated bioprosthetic valves has a greater risk of PPM. We sought to determine if sex-specific differences exist in rates of PPM following ViV-TAVI.

title: Compared strategies of carotid revascularization periprocedural risks and long-term outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials of stenting versus endarterectomy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) remains the benchmark open revascularization strategy for appropriately selected patients with extracranial carotid stenosis, whereas carotid artery stenting (CAS) provides an endovascular alternative when cervical exposure, medical comorbidity, or anatomic factors make open surgery less favorable. Balancing periprocedural stroke, myocardial infarction, cranial nerve injury, and long-term stroke risk remains central to contemporary cerebrovascular decision-making. This study compared periprocedural and exploratory long-term outcomes after CAS versus CEA using randomized head-to-head trial evidence across trial eras.

METHODS: PubMed, EMBASE, CENTRAL, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through April 2026. Eligible studies were randomized trials directly comparing CAS with CEA in adults with extracranial carotid stenosis. Arm-level event counts were extracted. Random-effects risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated using inverse-variance models with DerSimonian-Laird estimation. Hartung-Knapp intervals and absolute risk differences were added to support sensitivity analysis and clinical interpretation. The primary endpoint was 30-day stroke or death. Secondary endpoints included periprocedural stroke, death, myocardial infarction (MI), cranial nerve injury, disabling stroke or death, and exploratory long-term stroke-related outcomes.

RESULTS: Six randomized cohorts contributed to the primary endpoint; up to eight contributed to secondary analyses. Thirty-day stroke or death occurred in 244 of 5285 patients assigned to CAS (4.6%) and 156 of 4522 assigned to CEA (3.4%), corresponding to an absolute excess of 1.2 percentage points with CAS and a pooled RR of 1.42 (95% CI, 1.12-1.81; I²=27.9%). Periprocedural stroke was also more common after CAS (291/6305 [4.6%] vs. 186/5546 [3.4%]; RR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.18-1.75; I²=9.1%). Periprocedural death did not differ significantly (RR, 1.30; 95% CI, 0.77-2.19). MI (RR, 0.45; 95% CI, 0.29-0.71) and cranial nerve injury (RR, 0.05; 95% CI, 0.02-0.11) favored CAS. In a prespecified sensitivity analysis excluding CAVATAS-because most patients in its endovascular arm underwent balloon angioplasty rather than stenting-the primary result was unchanged (RR, 1.51; 95% CI, 1.17-1.95). Exploratory long-term stroke-related outcomes did not differ significantly (RR, 1.05; 95% CI, 0.87-1.26), although endpoint definitions and follow-up windows varied substantially.

CONCLUSIONS: In randomized head-to-head trials, CAS was associated with higher early stroke and stroke-or-death risk than CEA, whereas MI and cranial nerve injury were reported less often after CAS. Selection of open versus endovascular carotid revascularization should be guided by symptom status, age, lesion morphology, cervical and arch anatomy, perioperative cardiac risk, and operator outcomes.

Balancing periprocedural stroke, myocardial infarction, cranial nerve injury, and long-term stroke risk remains central to contemporary cerebrovascular decision-making. This study compared periprocedural and exploratory long-term outcomes after CAS versus CEA using randomized head-to-head trial evidence across trial eras.

title: Comparison of conventional logistic, random forest, and random forest-assisted models for 1-year primary patency after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula creation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We compared three strategies for predicting 1-year primary patency after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) creation.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 274 patients. Models A, B, and C were a 5-predictor logistic model, a 31-predictor random forest, and a 9-predictor random forest-assisted logistic model. The three models were compared in 251 patients with complete Model C predictors using 20 repeats of stratified 5-fold cross-validation.

RESULTS: Mean AUCs (SD) were 0.9361 (0.0045), 0.8843 (0.0095), and 0.9301 (0.0089) for Models A, B, and C; corresponding Brier scores were 0.0886 (0.0033), 0.1246 (0.0026), and 0.0933 (0.0060). Model A showed slightly better average cross-validated discrimination and prediction error than Model C, whereas Model C performed better than Model B.

CONCLUSIONS: Random forest-assisted modeling did not improve cross-validated predictive performance over the simpler logistic model. External validation is required before clinical implementation.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: We compared three strategies for predicting 1-year primary patency after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) creation. METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 274 patients. Models A, B, and C were a 5-predictor logistic model, a 31-predictor random forest, and a 9-predictor random forest-assisted logistic model.

title: Systemic immune-inflammation index for predicting pre-operative deep vein thrombosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) is a composite biomarker reflecting thrombo-inflammatory status. Its diagnostic performance for preoperative deep vein thrombosis (DVT) remains unclear. This meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic performance of SII for identifying preoperative DVT.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched up to October 16, 2025, for observational studies examining SII and preoperative DVT. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality. Pooled diagnostic accuracy measures, including area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity, were calculated using random-effects models. Meta-regression, sensitivity analyses, and publication bias assessments were performed.

RESULTS: Five retrospective cohort studies involving 4,097 patients were included. The pooled AUC of SII for predicting preoperative DVT was 0.671 (95% CI: 0.595-0.748). The pooled sensitivity was 0.591 (95% CI: 0.487-0.688), and pooled specificity was 0.780 (95% CI: 0.682-0.854). Formal tests did not suggest substantial publication bias, although their power was limited by the small number of studies. Exploratory meta-regression suggested that mean age may influence diagnostic performance, with higher accuracy observed in older populations. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the results, and no substantial publication bias was detected.

CONCLUSION: SII may be a potential adjunctive biomarker for preoperative DVT in selected orthopedic populations, but evidence is limited by retrospective designs, geographic restriction, clinical heterogeneity, and variable cutoffs. Prospective multicenter validation is warranted.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: The systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) is a composite biomarker reflecting thrombo-inflammatory status. Its diagnostic performance for preoperative deep vein thrombosis (DVT) remains unclear. This meta-analysis evaluated the diagnostic performance of SII for identifying preoperative DVT.

title: Real-World Use and Clinical Outcomes of Jetstream Atherectomy Extending to the P2/P3 Popliteal Artery Segments: Results of the PULSAR Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular treatment of mid- and distal popliteal artery (P2/P3) lesions remains challenging owing to repetitive mechanical deformation and concerns regarding permanent stent implantation. In this setting, Jetstream atherectomy may facilitate lesion preparation; however, data on its use in the P2/P3 segments, procedural safety, and clinical outcomes remain limited.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 443 limbs of 381 patients who underwent Jetstream atherectomy for femoropopliteal artery lesions in a multicenter registry. Limbs were classified by the most distal segment treated with Jetstream into the SFA/P1 and P2/P3 groups. The primary outcomes were procedural characteristics and periprocedural safety, including distal embolization (DE). Secondary outcomes were 1-year primary patency (PP) and freedom from clinically driven target-lesion revascularization (CD-TLR).

RESULTS: The Jetstream atherectomy was extended to the P2/P3 segments in 94 limbs (21.2%). Distal protection was more frequently used in the P2/P3 group (90.4% vs. 80.8%, p = 0.035). Overall DE occurred in 37.2% of the P2/P3 group and 33.8% of the SFA/P1 group (p = 0.51), whereas DE requiring endovascular intervention was numerically more frequent in the P2/P3 group (9.6% vs. 4.6%, p = 0.067). Jetstream use extending to the P2/P3 segments was not independently associated with overall DE (adjusted odds ratio 1.22, 95% CI 0.72-2.07; p = 0.47). At 1 year, PP was 84.4% in the P2/P3 group and 85.0% in the SFA/P1 group (p = 0.74), whereas freedom from CD-TLR was 89.9% and 90.8%, respectively (p = 0.50).

CONCLUSIONS: Jetstream atherectomy extended to the P2/P3 segments in approximately one-fifth of the treated limbs, with more frequent use of distal protection. Although no clear differences in periprocedural complications or 1-year clinical outcomes were observed, careful attention to DE is warranted.

In this setting, Jetstream atherectomy may facilitate lesion preparation; however, data on its use in the P2/P3 segments, procedural safety, and clinical outcomes remain limited. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 443 limbs of 381 patients who underwent Jetstream atherectomy for femoropopliteal artery lesions in a multicenter registry.

title: Lorlatinib-Associated Dyslipidemia in ALK-Positive NSCLC: Atherosclerotic Risk and the Unresolved Question of Venous Thromboembolism.
abstract: Lorlatinib, a brain-penetrant third-generation anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) tyrosine kinase inhibitor, has markedly improved outcomes in ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In the CROWN trial, median progression-free survival had not been reached with first-line lorlatinib after 7 years of follow-up, compared with 9.1 months for crizotinib, with 7-year progression-free survival of 55% versus 3%. Median treatment duration was 62.6 months versus 9.6 months. This duration extends cumulative exposure to lorlatinib's characteristic metabolic toxicity: hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia. At 7 years, these occurred in 73% and 71% of patients receiving lorlatinib, with grade 3 or 4 events in 22% and 26%. Onset is rapid, at a median of about 2 weeks. At 5 years, any-grade elevations had persisted for a median of 36 to 38 months; 71% of events were managed with lipid-lowering agents. ALK-positive NSCLC carries a high risk of venous thromboembolism across observational cohorts and a meta-analysis, more so for venous than arterial events. Laboratory evidence suggests the EML4-ALK fusion raises tissue factor through the pERK1/2-AP-1 pathway. At 7 years, aggregate cardiovascular adverse events were similar between treatment groups, and venous events were not more frequent with lorlatinib; small event counts and differing treatment exposure limit comparison of individual events. Statin choice is limited because lorlatinib is a moderate cytochrome P450 3A inducer; rosuvastatin and pravastatin are preferred. We review lorlatinib-associated dyslipidemia and its management and separate two claims: prompt, guideline-concordant lipid management is supported by established atherosclerotic prevention principles, whereas any effect on venous thromboembolism remains untested.

title: Real-World Risk of Venous Thromboembolism with Bevacizumab Biosimilar versus Reference Biologic in Japanese Patients with Cancer: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Large-scale safety data for newly introduced bevacizumab biosimilars in routine oncology practice remain limited. As part of post-marketing safety evaluations under the Risk Management Plan in Japan, we evaluated the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) associated with a bevacizumab biosimilar (CTNK) and compared the findings with those for a reference biologic (Avastin®) in Japanese patients with cancer.

METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study using a large-scale hospital-based claims database (Medical Data Vision) in Japan, we identified new users of bevacizumab diagnosed with colorectal, breast, or ovarian cancer or glioblastoma between November 2020 and February 2025. Patients were classified into the biosimilar group or the reference biologic group. The primary outcome was the incidence of VTE, evaluated using a multivariable Cox proportional hazards model. Exploratory safety outcomes, including bleeding/hemorrhage and infections, were also assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 8599 eligible patients (1967 in the biosimilar group and 6632 in the reference biologic group; male versus female patients, 45.60% and 41.74% versus 54.40% and 58.26%, respectively; median age, 69.0 years in both groups) were included in the primary analysis. The overall incidence of VTE was 2.36%. The adjusted hazard ratio for VTE in the biosimilar group compared with that in the reference biologic group was 0.82 (95% confidence interval, 0.57-1.19; P = 0.30), indicating no significant difference. This finding was consistent across subgroups stratified by target cancer type or by VTE history. Furthermore, the incidence of exploratory safety events was comparable between the two treatment groups.

CONCLUSIONS: This retrospective cohort study showed no evidence of increased VTE risk with the bevacizumab biosimilar or major safety differences between the bevacizumab biosimilar and the reference biologic in Japanese patients with cancer, providing reassuring real-world evidence supporting the safe use of the bevacizumab biosimilar in routine clinical practice. title: The Case for Interpretable Geometry: Statistical Shape Models vs. Curvature-Based Descriptors in Aortic Disease Classification.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Quantifying aortic morphology is central to surgical planning for thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR), yet no consensus exists on how best to represent three-dimensional aortic shape for outcome prediction. Two broad strategies have emerged: statistical shape analysis (SSA), which relies on statistical methods and dimensionality reduction to capture the most significant shape modes, and geometrically-informed approaches that extract descriptors grounded in differential geometry. Here, we directly compare these paradigms on a cohort of 290 CTA scans classified by surgical outcome (non-pathological, successful TEVAR, failed TEVAR).

METHODS: For the geometrically-informed approach, we use a two-dimensional feature space using fluctuation in integrated Gaussian curvature δ K and mean aortic radius R. For SSA, we construct a point-cloud shape model with dimensionality reduction using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and evaluate classification performance as a function of the number of retained principal components. Both approaches are evaluated by repeated cross-validation grouped by patient, with all scaling, PCA, and hyperparameter selection performed within the training folds, and by external testing on scans from the GORE TAG 08-01 trial.

RESULTS: SSA's leading principal components encode variations in global aortic size and shape and are statistically redundant with (R, δ K ), yet they lack a one-to-one correspondence with interpretable anatomical quantities. With the same number of dimensions, the geometric descriptors classified at least as well as SSA (Gaussian process classification, cross-validated weighted F 1 of 85.8% versus 84.9%). SSA's cross-validated F 1 peaked with two principal components (83.1%) and declined as more were added, although its training-set accuracy rose above 90%, which indicates overfitting. On the independent trial cohort, in which every patient required TEVAR, SSA classified 50.7% of scans as non-pathological, compared with 21.2% for the geometric approach, suggesting better generalizability.

CONCLUSION: Two physically defined descriptors classified aortic disease at least as well as the leading SSA modes and transferred better to an independent cohort. SSA modes offer an intuitive visualization of how shape varies across a cohort, but geometric descriptors, which are measured identically for any patient and do not depend on the cohort used to build a model, provide a more robust basis for patient-level classification.

title: Outcomes of Endovascular Repair for Stanford Type B Aortic Dissection with Concurrent Retrograde Intramural Hematoma Involving the Aortic Arch and/or Ascending Aorta (Zone 0-2) in a Chinese Population: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the outcomes of thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for type B aortic dissection (TBAD) with concurrent retrograde intramural hematoma (RTIMH) involving the aortic arch, with or without further extension into the ascending aorta.

METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE and EMBASE to June 2026 was performed. Studies reporting TEVAR outcomes in adults with TBAD-associated RTIMH, defined as a primary intimal tear at or distal to Ishimaru zone 3 with retrograde intramural hematoma extension into zones 0-2, were included. Co-primary outcomes were technical success and post-TEVAR retrograde type A aortic dissection (RTAD), defined as the new development of a communicating dissection flap within the previously non-flow intramural hematoma. Secondary outcomes included early mortality, stroke, type I endoleak, reintervention, survival, aortic rupture, and aortic remodelling. Proportions were pooled using single-arm random-effects meta-analysis following logit transformation; remaining findings were synthesised narratively.

RESULTS: Seven retrospective cohort studies comprising 342 patients, all from mainland Chinese institutions, were included. The pooled technical success rate was 99% (95% CI 97-99%; I2 = 0.0%). The pooled post-TEVAR RTAD rate was 3% (95% CI 1-8%; I2 = 7.6%), with all events preceded by proximal stent-graft-induced new entry. Secondary outcomes included pooled 30-day mortality of 2% (95% CI 1-4%; I2 = 0.0%), aortic rupture of 2% (95% CI 1-4%; I2 = 0.0%), reintervention of 7% (95% CI 5-11%; I2 = 0.0%), late all-cause mortality of 4% (95% CI 3-6%; I2 = 0.0%), and type I endoleak of 4% (95% CI 2-7%; I2 = 0.0%). All studies reporting pre- and post-procedural imaging demonstrated reductions in ascending aortic diameter and hematoma thickness, with complete ascending IMH resolution in 52.5-100% of patients.

CONCLUSIONS: TEVAR is technically feasible with low perioperative mortality and consistent aortic remodelling in selected patients with TBAD-associated RTIMH. Post-TEVAR RTAD and type I endoleak represent the principal procedure-specific risks. Contemporary evidence remains limited to small retrospective cohorts from a single geographic region.

METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE and EMBASE to June 2026 was performed. Studies reporting TEVAR outcomes in adults with TBAD-associated RTIMH, defined as a primary intimal tear at or distal to Ishimaru zone 3 with retrograde intramural hematoma extension into zones 0-2, were included.

title: One-Year Outcomes of Surgical Versus Endovascular Revascularization for Acute Limb Ischemia in the SAPLING-ALI Registry.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Despite the increasing use of endovascular therapy as an alternative to surgery for acute limb ischemia, individualized treatment selection remains challenging. We compared outcomes of endovascular therapy versus surgery and sought to identify patient characteristics favoring either strategy.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included consecutive patients with acute limb ischemia (Rutherford category 1-2b) who underwent revascularization at 13 Japanese institutions between July 2011 and March 2025; patients with thrombosed popliteal artery aneurysm were excluded. The primary outcome was amputation-free survival, defined as freedom from major amputation or death from any cause. The primary analysis was a Cox model adjusted for 13 baseline covariates with hospital as a categorical covariate; propensity score weighting was used as a sensitivity analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed to identify characteristics favoring either strategy.

RESULTS: Of 978 patients (endovascular therapy, n = 607; surgery, n = 371), those treated with endovascular therapy more often had diabetes, hemodialysis, dementia, and non-ambulatory status. Unadjusted 1-year amputation-free survival was lower with endovascular therapy than with surgery (68.7% vs 76.3%; log-rank P = .001), but the adjusted hazard ratio for death or major amputation was 1.03 (95% confidence interval, 0.77-1.38; P = .84). Results were consistent with overlap weighting (hazard ratio 1.15; 95% confidence interval, 0.93-1.42) and across other sensitivity analyses. Thirty-day mortality was 13.1% after endovascular therapy and 8.9% after surgery (P = .05), and the difference was attenuated after weighting. No subgroup favoring either strategy was identified (all P for interaction ≥ .18).

CONCLUSIONS: Unadjusted amputation-free survival was lower after endovascular therapy than after surgery, but the difference disappeared after adjustment for patient characteristics and hospital, and no subgroup favoring either strategy was identified. Endovascular therapy, being less invasive, may be a reasonable alternative to surgery for acute limb ischemia.

We compared outcomes of endovascular therapy versus surgery and sought to identify patient characteristics favoring either strategy. title: Assessment of aspirin response in patients undergoing neuroendovascular treatments: A comparison of five platelet function tests across two platforms.
abstract: Aspirin is widely used for periprocedural antiplatelet therapy in neuroendovascular procedures; however, variability in patient response poses clinical challenges. This study aimed to assess five platelet function tests on two different platforms: light transmission aggregometry (LTA) using the CN-6000 device and the VerifyNow system, which were utilized to assess patients undergoing neuroendovascular procedures. A total of 124 patients who underwent elective neuroendovascular procedures and received perioperative aspirin-based antiplatelet therapy between September 2020 and December 2023 were retrospectively reviewed. Platelet function was assessed at three time points: before surgery, 1-3 days after surgery, and 1 month following the procedure. The assessments included maximum aggregation (MA) induced by 1 mM arachidonic acid (AA), 10 μM ADP, and 1 μg/mL collagen, as well as collagen-induced platelet aggregation level (CPAL) and aspirin reaction units (ARU). Significant perioperative changes were observed only with 1 mM AA MA, which increased immediately after surgery (p < 0.001) and decreased at 1 month (p = 0.013), while other tests showed no significant differences. Correlation analysis revealed the strongest association between 1 mM AA MA and 1 μg/mL collagen MA (r = 0.65), followed by CPAL (r = 0.62). ARU correlated modestly with LTA-based measures (r ≤ 0.34). Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified CPAL >6.0 and collagen MA > 43.2% as equivalent to AA MA > 20%. In this cohort, perioperative changes were detected by 1 mM AA MA but not by the other platelet function tests, and correlations between VerifyNow ARU and LTA-based measurements were modest. However, the clinical significance of these differences remains to be established. Automated LTA using CN-6000 may offer a practical option for aspirin monitoring in patients undergoing neuroendovascular procedures. Further prospective studies are warranted to validate its clinical utility.

A total of 124 patients who underwent elective neuroendovascular procedures and received perioperative aspirin-based antiplatelet therapy between September 2020 and December 2023 were retrospectively reviewed.

title: Risk factors for venous thromboembolism in adults with sepsis: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Adults with sepsis are at increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), encompassing deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), because of sepsis-related inflammation, endothelial injury, coagulation activation and treatment-related exposures. Although several potential risk factors have been reported, the evidence remains fragmented and findings are inconsistent across populations, VTE subtypes and diagnostic approaches. This protocol aims to prespecify transparent and reproducible methods for a systematic review and meta-analysis of factors associated with incident VTE in adults with sepsis.

METHODS AND ANALYSIS: Prospective and retrospective cohort studies and case-control studies involving adults with sepsis or septic shock will be included. Studies evaluating potential risk factors for incident VTE after sepsis onset or diagnosis will be eligible. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science Core Collection, CINAHL and the Cochrane Library will be searched from inception to the final search date, supplemented by grey-literature searching and citation screening. Two reviewers will independently perform study selection, data extraction and risk-of-bias assessment. Where sufficient comparable data are available, random-effects meta-analysis will be conducted, with adjusted estimates prioritised. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses will be performed to explore heterogeneity, and certainty of evidence will be assessed using the GRADE approach adapted for prognostic-factor evidence.

title: Median arcuate ligament syndrome: Current evidence and controversies-A narrative review.
abstract: Median arcuate ligament syndrome is a rare and controversial cause of chronic abdominal pain, attributed to extrinsic compression of the celiac artery by the median arcuate ligament. The 2025 European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines consider median arcuate ligament syndrome a diagnosis of exclusion and recommend management in specialized multidisciplinary centers. Anatomical compression of the celiac artery has been recognized for over a century, but a clear clinicopathological entity remains disputed. Median arcuate ligament syndrome is rare, with an estimated incidence of about 1.3 (0.5-3.6) per 100,000 inhabitants in a recent Dutch population study. Patients, predominantly women, typically present with long-standing postprandial epigastric pain and, in most cases, weight loss, often after years of extensive investigations for more common gastrointestinal disorders. Both ischemic and neurogenic mechanisms have been proposed, and data support elements of each. Diagnostic work-up relies on exclusion of differential diagnoses and imaging evidence of ⩾70% celiac artery stenosis, often with dynamic testing. Laparoscopic or robot-assisted laparoscopic decompression and video-assisted retroperitoneal decompression of the celiac artery are now the preferred approaches. Clinically significant symptom improvement is reported in up to 80% of operated patients, although treatment failure rates close to 50% have also been reported in large multicenter cohorts. Median arcuate ligament syndrome remains a challenging and controversial diagnosis with limited high-quality evidence. Careful patient selection, multidisciplinary evaluation, and realistic expectations regarding prognosis are essential. Ongoing randomized controlled trials and studies on objective ischemia biomarkers and quality of life may help refine indications and improve outcomes.

The 2025 European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines consider median arcuate ligament syndrome a diagnosis of exclusion and recommend management in specialized multidisciplinary centers. Anatomical compression of the celiac artery has been recognized for over a century, but a clear clinicopathological entity remains disputed.

title: Three-Year Outcomes of Endovascular Therapy Using Covered Stent-Grafts Versus Interwoven Nitinol Stents in Severely Calcified Femoropopliteal Artery Disease From a Retrospective Multicenter Registry.
abstract:
PURPOSE: This study aimed to compare the long-term safety and efficacy of Viabahn covered stent-grafts (CSG) and Supera peripheral stents (SPS) in calcified femoropopliteal artery lesions.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 341 cases who had Rutherford class 2 to 6 peripheral artery disease and underwent endovascular therapy (EVT) with either CSG (n = 137) or SPS (n = 204) for femoropopliteal lesions with bilateral calcification assessed by fluoroscopic image based on Peripheral Arterial Calcium Scoring System classification, between April 2017 and February 2021 at 7 cardiovascular centers in our country.

RESULTS: Following propensity score (PS) matching, the final study population comprised 142 matched patients with no remarkable intergroup difference in baseline characteristics. The 3-year primary patency was 70.9% in the CSG group and 56.2% in the SPS group, respectively, and was not statistically different (P = .083). Moreover, no significant difference was noted in freedom from target lesion revascularization (72.8% vs 63.5%, P = .16), limb salvage rate (100.0% vs 96.2%, P = .32), and overall survival rate (67.6% vs 66.6%, P = .61). Stratification analysis revealed that advanced age and current smoking had a significant interaction on the association of CSG versus SPS implantation with restenosis (interaction P < .05).

CONCLUSION: In patients with severely calcified femoropopliteal lesions, the 3-year primary patency was not significantly different between EVT using CSG and SPS following PS matching.Clinical ImpactSevere calcification in femoropopliteal disease remains a challenge for EVT. Covered stent-graft and SPS are reliable devices for calcified femoropopliteal lesions. We compared the 3-year outcomes in patients undergoing EVT using either CSG or SPS. Following the propensity matching, the 3-year primary patency was not different at 70.0% and 56.2% (P = .083) in the CSG (n = 71) and SPS (n = 71) groups, respectively. Moreover, no significant difference was noted in freedom from target lesion revascularization and limb salvage rate.

title: Endovascular Recanalization of Chronically Occluded Femoropopliteal Bypass Grafts: Feasibility and Early Clinical Outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic occlusion of femoropopliteal bypass grafts remains a complex clinical challenge, particularly in patients with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) who have limited surgical options and high operative risk. Although redo bypass surgery has traditionally been considered the standard treatment, it is associated with increased morbidity. Advances in endovascular techniques have expanded revascularization strategies; however, data on graft-directed endovascular recanalization remain limited.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 32 consecutive patients who underwent endovascular recanalization for chronically occluded femoropopliteal bypass grafts between January 2018 and December 2024. A stepwise graft-directed technique was applied, consisting of intraluminal guidewire crossing, sequential balloon predilatation, and stent implantation along the graft body and anastomotic segments when necessary. Technical success, procedural safety, and changes in ankle-brachial index (ABI) were evaluated.

RESULTS: The mean age of the patients was 69.8 ± 9.6 years, and 68.8% were male. Technical success was achieved in 30 patients (93.8%). Median ABI improved significantly from 0.34 (interquartile range [IQR]: 0.22-0.48) before intervention to 0.71 (IQR: 0.58-0.84) after revascularization. Stent implantation was performed in all patients, with a median of 3 stents per case. Periprocedural complications occurred in 2 patients (6.3%) and were managed conservatively or by endovascular means. No procedure-related mortality or major limb loss was observed during hospitalization.

CONCLUSION: Stepwise endovascular recanalization of chronically occluded femoropopliteal bypass grafts is feasible and safe, providing favorable early technical and clinical outcomes. This graft-targeted approach may expand the endovascular treatment spectrum for PAD patients who are poor candidates for surgical reintervention and should be regarded as a procedural optimization strategy rather than a replacement for redo bypass surgery.Clinical ImpactGraft-directed endovascular recanalization of chronically occluded femoropopliteal bypass grafts demonstrated high technical success (93.8%), improved limb perfusion, and low periprocedural complication rates. This minimally invasive approach may represent a feasible revascularization option for selected high-risk patients with limited surgical alternatives. Further studies are warranted to establish its long-term durability.

Although redo bypass surgery has traditionally been considered the standard treatment, it is associated with increased morbidity. Advances in endovascular techniques have expanded revascularization strategies; however, data on graft-directed endovascular recanalization remain limited.

title: Percutaneous Local Antibiotic Irrigation for Aortic Graft Infection After Endovascular Repair: A Single-Center Experience and Systematic Literature Review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortic graft infections (AGIs) are a severe complication following open aortic surgical repair (OSR) and endovascular aortic repair (EVAR). Endograft extirpation and aortic reconstruction remain the gold standard treatment according to European guidelines. The aim is to present a single-center experience using a percutaneous local antibiotic irrigation strategy in selected patients with AGI after EVAR, with a systematic literature review.

METHODS: Patients with AGI after endovascular aortic repair treated with computed tomography (CT)-guided local antibiotic irrigation (2011-2023) were included. Outcomes were assessed using clinical, microbiological, and radiological follow-up, with mortality and reinfection evaluated up to 3 years. A systematic search of PubMed and Cochrane was conducted. The review was not registered, and formal bias assessment was not performed.

RESULTS: Among 665 endovascular repairs, 14 patients developed AGI. Eight patients were treated with CT-guided antibiotic irrigation. Infection resolved in 4 patients (n = 4/8), and 1 patient (n = 1/8) was treated as a bridge to open aortic surgical repair OSR. Persistent infection was observed in 3 patients (3/8). Cumulative mortality was 0% at 30 days (n = 0/8), 13% at 90 days (n = 1/8), and 50% (n = 4/8) at 1 to 3 years. Three patients (n = 3/8) died from recurrent infection. The literature review identified 6 studies, adding 28 cases. All patients were treated with antibiotic irrigation either as primary therapy or as a bridge to OSR. Short-term/30-day mortality ranged from 0% to 22%, except for 1 study, with mortality of 50%. Most studies achieved effective infection control in high-risk surgical candidates.

CONCLUSION: In highly selected groups of patients who are not candidates for extensive surgery such as aortic reconstruction, percutaneous local antibiotic irrigation may be an alternative treatment method.Clinical ImpactAGI after endovascular repair carries high mortality, current guidelines recommendation is endograft extirpation and aortic reconstruction. This may not be feasible for frail patients. This single-center case series along with literature review of 6 studies suggest it may be feasible with minimally invasive CT-guided percutaneous drainage with local antibiotic irrigation in carefully selected patients who are unfit for major surgery.

Endograft extirpation and aortic reconstruction remain the gold standard treatment according to European guidelines. The aim is to present a single-center experience using a percutaneous local antibiotic irrigation strategy in selected patients with AGI after EVAR, with a systematic literature review.

title: Real-world pharmacovigilance of thromboembolic adverse events associated with osimertinib using the Japanese adverse drug event report database.
abstract: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the disproportionality, times to onset, and outcomes of thromboembolic adverse events (AEs) associated with osimertinib using data from the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report database (JADER), with a specific focus on real-world evidence from Japan, an East Asian country with high EGFR mutation prevalence. We analyzed JADER data from April 2004 to December 2024. Disproportionality was assessed by calculating reporting odds ratios (RORs). Time-to-onset was evaluated, and Weibull distribution parameters were calculated for major AEs with detected signals, while rare AEs were summarized descriptively. Among 3,221,393 reports, 7134 AEs were associated with osimertinib, including 153 thromboembolic AEs. Significant disproportionality signals were detected for six thromboembolic AEs: deep vein thrombosis (ROR = 2.89), pulmonary embolism (ROR = 2.78), embolism venous (ROR = 6.64), peripheral vein thrombosis (ROR = 3.16), pulmonary artery thrombosis (ROR = 2.93), and thrombophlebitis migrans (ROR = 7.49). Median onset times ranged from 28 to 85 days after osimertinib initiation. Weibull analysis of major thromboembolic AEs suggested no clear time-dependent increase in reporting frequency over time (random failure type). Fatal outcomes were observed for several thromboembolic AEs, particularly pulmonary embolism and pulmonary artery thrombosis. Several thromboembolic AEs associated with osimertinib were identified, including potentially fatal events. These findings suggest that thromboembolic events may be reported relatively early after the initiation of osimertinib treatment and highlight the importance of clinical awareness and appropriate monitoring during treatment. However, these findings do not establish a causal relationship between osimertinib and thromboembolic events.

We analyzed JADER data from April 2004 to December 2024. Disproportionality was assessed by calculating reporting odds ratios (RORs).

title: Temporal Trend and Geographic Variation in Anticoagulation of Patients Hospitalized with Acute Pulmonary Embolism: the RIETE Registry from 2013 to 2024.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: A recent U.S. study of initial anticoagulation in adults with acute pulmonary embolism (PE) requiring hospitalization found intravenous unfractionated heparin (UFH) use exceeded 50%. Guidelines, however, recommend low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) over UFH for most patients requiring parenteral anticoagulation. Use patterns in other geographic regions are unclear.

METHODS: We analyzed data from Registro Informatizado de la Enfermedad TromboEmbólica, a prospective multinational registry of consecutive patients with venous thromboembolism. We included adults hospitalized for acute PE from 2013 through 2024 in 273 hospitals across 31 countries. We assessed temporal trend and regional variation in initial anticoagulation. Using multivariable regression, we identified variables independently associated with UFH.

RESULTS: Among 36,210 adults, 83.2% received subcutaneous LMWH, 7.1% UFH, and 6.8% direct oral anticoagulants. LMWH use decreased slightly from 2013 to 2024 (85.8-79.2%; unadjusted), while UFH increased (8.9-10.4%). Wide geographic variation was observed in overall use of LMWH (37-95%) and UFH (2-39%). When adjusted for demographic and clinical covariates, increased weight, recent surgery, recent major bleeding, severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, severe renal dysfunction, abnormal vital signs, and early reperfusion therapy were positively associated, whereas age > 80 years, active cancer, chronic lung disease, prior ischemic stroke, and year were negatively associated with UFH. Compared with Spanish hospitals, hospitals in other European countries, the United States, and Asia were independently associated with UFH use.

CONCLUSION: Results highlight opportunities for some geographic regions to align anticoagulation practices more closely with evidence-based guidelines recommending LMWH as the preferred parenteral agent in most patients with PE requiring hospitalization.

title: The 2026 American Heart Association/American Stroke Association Guideline Updates to Management of Patients with Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Guide for Radiologists.
abstract: The 2026 guideline for early management of acute ischemic stroke retains many foundational recommendations while introducing clinically meaningful updates spanning imaging, broader inpatient management, and reperfusion strategies including IV thrombolysis and endovascular thrombectomy. Notably, it provides expanded guidance for medium vessel occlusions and introduces pediatric recommendations that were largely absent from prior iterations. Given their impact on imaging workflows in acute ischemic stroke, the authors present a focused review of the updated guidelines for the radiologist.

title: Automated Quantitative Assessment of Recanalization in Endovascular Thrombectomy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains a major cause of death and disability worldwide. Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) has substantially improved outcomes by restoring cerebral blood flow. The TICI score, the current standard for recanalization assessment, is a semiquantitative grading system that is commonly used to evaluate the effectiveness of thrombectomy, but it suffers from interrater variability and is poorly correlated with clinical outcomes. Here, we propose a novel and fully automated quantitative TICI (qTICI) score derived from DSA during EVT that integrates morphologic descriptors, vascular network topology, and perfusion dynamics to provide a numeric quantitative reperfusion metric.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Using a prospectively collected cohort of 295 patients with AIS who underwent EVT, we developed an automated pipeline to extract vascular morphology and perfusion metrics from postrecanalization DSA images. We integrated selected features to compute qTICI and evaluated its performance against adjudicated extended TICI (eTICI) grades, provided by expert interventional neuroradiologists, to predict clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: Although the qTICI score demonstrated moderate agreement with the eTICI grades (micro-average area under the curve [AUC] 0.70), it outperformed eTICI in predicting both early and long-term outcomes among successfully recanalized patients (72-hour NIHSS: AUC = 0.60 vs 0.47; 90-day mRS: AUC = 0.55 vs 0.46). Combining qTICI with additional clinical variables further enhanced its predictive performance. Multivariable analyses showed a greater contribution of qTICI to outcome predictions compared with eTICI.

CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that automated qTICI offers an objective and enhanced alternative to visual grading with modest improvements in prognostic accuracy for AIS outcomes. Prospective, multicenter validation is warranted to standardize reperfusion assessment and support integration of qTICI into clinical trials and stroke care.

title: Age-stratified sex differences in outcomes after lower extremity fracture fixation: A propensity-matched cohort study.
abstract: BackgroundOutcomes of open reduction internal fixation (ORIF) of lower extremity fractures vary based on patient sex and age.MethodsWe performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX national research database. Adult patients (≥18 years) who underwent ORIF of lower extremity fractures, including pelvis and acetabulum, between 2003 and 2023 were identified. We conducted 1:1 propensity score matching (male vs. female) to balance comorbidities, including age, race, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, BMI, osteoporosis, and smoking status. Patients were stratified into age groups (18-39, 40-64, ≥ 65 years). Postoperative outcomes at 90 days and two years were compared using risk ratios (RR) and 95% confidence intervals.ResultsOf 204,152 patients, 147,518 remained after matching. Males had significantly higher complication rates than females: deep vein thrombosis, 2.1% vs. 1.5%; pneumonia, 1.5% vs. 1.0%; nonunion requiring surgical treatment, 4.8% vs. 3.5%; and amputation, 1.1% vs. 0.5% (all p<0.001). Males also had higher rates of 90-day emergency department visits (4.6% vs. 3.8%) and readmissions (6.7% vs. 4.6%, p<0.001). These sex disparities were most pronounced in midlife (40-64 years). Conversely, females had higher rates of complex regional pain syndrome across all ages.ConclusionBoth sex and age are predictors of postoperative outcomes following lower extremity ORIF, with the largest sex disparities in patients aged 40-64 and higher CRPS rates in females across all age groups.

title: Cost-consequence analysis of long peripheral catheters versus midline catheters: a post-hoc model-based analysis of published systematic review data.
abstract:
AIM: To compare expected hospital costs and catheter-related outcomes of midline catheters (MCs) and long peripheral catheters (LPCs) for intravenous therapy lasting more than seven days.

METHODS: A 7-28-day competing-risks renewal model assumed management and replacement after each failure. Inputs were pooled cause-specific complication rates from a systematic review of 5,023 MCs (129,179 catheter-days) and 962 LPCs (11,147 catheter-days). Uncertainty was quantified with 50,000 second-order probabilistic draws (95% credible intervals, CrI). Scenarios addressed between-study heterogeneity, outcome-specific denominators, and confounding by indication. Sensitivity analyses used re-extracted all-cause failure rates and four direct comparisons.

RESULTS: At 14 and 28 days, incremental costs (MC minus LPC) were -€97.9 (95% CrI, -264 to + 21) and -€218.3 (95% CrI, -547 to +14) per patient, respectively. MCs were cost-saving in 93.9% and 96.6% of simulations, respectively. The higher MC insertion cost was offset after 2.6 days. At 14 days, expected failures per patient were 0.064 versus 0.246, and first-device therapy completion was 93.8% versus 78.2% (MC versus LPC). Bloodstream infection and symptomatic thrombosis accounted for 68.2% of the cost difference and 7.9% of the failure difference. All-cause failure rates yielded a 14-day cost difference of -€104.9. With head-to-head evidence, the LPC-to-MC failure rate ratio was 1.97 versus 4.89 using pooled rates, and the 14-day cost difference was -€60.9 (95% CrI, -226 to +54). Without the modeled excess of these complications with LPCs, MCs cost €17.6 more per patient.

LIMITATIONS: Pooled observational data had unequal exposure across devices and were susceptible to confounding by indication. Costs reflected one national setting. The model excluded indirect costs, quality of life, and patient heterogeneity.

CONCLUSIONS: MCs had fewer modeled failures across analyses. Estimated savings diminished with head-to-head evidence and depended on unconfirmed differences in major complications. Adjusted head-to-head studies are needed to confirm these findings.

Inputs were pooled cause-specific complication rates from a systematic review of 5,023 MCs (129,179 catheter-days) and 962 LPCs (11,147 catheter-days).

title: Emergency department ultrasound-guided peripheral intravenous catheter insertion training with virtual reality.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ultrasound-guided peripheral intravenous catheter (USG-PIVC) insertion is a challenging skill for emergency department (ED) clinicians to master. Virtual reality (VR) is a promising, cost-effective tool for procedural training. Unlike manikins or phantoms, VR enables immersive, repeatable and scalable training with real-time feedback, simulating real ED conditions to improve skill transfer and learner engagement. However, its use in USG-PIVC education within EDs has not been evaluated despite persistent training barriers to USG-PIVC insertion in this setting.

AIMS: To assess the feasibility of conducting a large-scale randomised controlled trial (RCT) that integrates a VR intervention into USG-PIVC training, addressing these challenges before evaluating effectiveness.

METHODS: A single-site feasibility RCT will be conducted in an Australian ED. Twenty ED doctors will be randomly assigned to either standard training or standard training plus VR simulation. In addition to feasibility outcomes, the study will assess clinical metrics including first-attempt success rate, number of attempts, time to insertion, vein difficulty, completion of procedural steps, immediate complications, time spent practising, and clinician confidence and satisfaction.

EXPECTED OUTCOMES: Although limited by a small sample size and single-site design, the findings from this pilot trial will provide valuable insights into the feasibility of integrating VR into USG-PIVC training. These results will help inform the design and implementation of a larger-scale, multi-site trial to evaluate effectiveness and broader applicability.
