title: AI-Driven CT Analysis for Aortic Disease: A Task-Based Systematic Review of Segmentation, Measurement, and Detection Applications.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Computed tomography (CT) and CT angiography (CTA) are central to assessing aortic aneurysm and dissection, but manual segmentation and geometric analysis remain time-consuming and operator-dependent, while evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) is fragmented. This task-based systematic review synthesised AI applications to CT/CTA of the thoracic and abdominal aorta by primary task: segmentation, measurement, or detection and classification. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE and Europe PMC were searched from 2015 to September 2026 following PRISMA 2020; the protocol was registered retrospectively (INPLASY2026110004). Segmentation and measurement studies were appraised with CLAIM and detection studies with QUADAS-2/QUADAS-AI, and results were synthesised without meta-analysis. Results: Of 118 included studies (42 segmentation, 38 measurement, 38 detection), half were published since 2024. Median Dice similarity coefficient was 0.90 or higher for the outer wall, lumen and true and false lumina, but 0.86 for intraluminal thrombus and 0.63 for false lumen thrombus. Automated maximum diameter showed a median absolute bias of 0.26 mm (95% limits of agreement about ±5 mm). Detection of aortic dissection reached a median AUC of 0.96-0.97, mostly in enriched samples. External validation was reported in 14%, 34% and 55% of segmentation, measurement and detection studies, 33 of 38 detection studies were at high risk of bias, and only two systems were evaluated prospectively. Conclusions: AI supports technical automation of aortic CT/CTA segmentation and measurement and is progressing toward multistructure geometric phenotyping and clinical decision support, but independent multicentre validation, consecutive cohorts and prospective reader-in-the-loop studies are required before clinical integration. Detection/classification tools require independent diagnostic and workflow validation.

title: Teaching the bigger picture - student perceptions on interprofessional teaching on the patient journey in vascular surgery.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ensuring drug safety is critical in comorbid vascular surgery patients and can be supported by interprofessional collaboration with clinical pharmacists. Thus, this project aimed to create an interprofessional seminar for medical students using real-life vascular surgery cases, highlighting medication risks and the value of interprofessional collaboration during the cross-sectoral medication process.

METHODS: A six-step model (Kern cycle) was used to develop a seminar integrating vascular surgery cases with the medication process from admission to discharge. The implementation was guided by a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT)-analysis to identify challenges and opportunities. After piloting the seminar, self-reported evaluation data were used to describe students' perception of acceptance, perceived learning, and practical relevance. A 14-item questionnaire and qualitative content analysis of free-text responses were used to analyze students' perceptions on the course.

RESULTS: Learning objectives included identifying medication risks, applying literature to solve drug-related problems, and developing interprofessional strategies to improve medication safety. The seminar, led by vascular surgeons and clinical pharmacists, employed various didactic methods (e.g., inverted classroom, small group learning). The seminar was evaluated by 142 of 240 students involved in the pilot phase (response rate 59.1%). Respondents rated the practical relevance, interprofessional approach, and interactive learning methods positively and reported perceived learning progress. The seminar is now part of the vascular surgery curriculum.

CONCLUSIONS: The seminar provides a practical framework for integrating cross-sectoral medication management into medical education. By linking clinical practice with collaborative patient care, it offers an opportunity for enhancing students' understanding of collaborative patient care and drug safety in the surgical patient journey. The seminar was successfully integrated into the vascular surgery curriculum and was positively perceived by participating students. This model may be adaptable to other medical specialties to promote interprofessional teaching in the medical curriculum.

title: Public real-world data decision thresholds for hybrid vascular control in complex robot-assisted partial nephrectomy.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Hybrid endovascular balloon occlusion has been described during complex robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN), but no reproducible public-data phenotype or access-risk-adjusted threshold has been validated. The selected public evidence was audited, and a hypothesis was formulated for future testing.

METHODS: A public-data quantitative evidence synthesis was combined with a conceptual decision model. ​Six selected reports of hybrid partial nephrectomy were rechecked. Possible patient overlap and incomplete reporting meant that the reported procedures could not be treated as a cohort of independent patients. A 20-patient branch-occlusion study provided a numerical illustration using Jeffreys-prior beta-binomial models and an additive expected-loss equation. KiTS23, C4KC-KiTS, TCGA-KIRC and MAUDE were mapped for possible future research; their individual patient or event records were not analysed.​ RESULTS: The illustrative cohort reported no conversion, one escalation from branch to main-artery balloon occlusion and one minor puncture-site bruise. The posterior median conversion probability was 1.1% (95% credible interval [CrI] < 0.1-11.7%). For each outcome with one reported event, the posterior median probability was 5.8% (95% CrI 0.5-21.1%). The median loss-equivalence boundary increased from 8.2% to 37.4% when the hypothetical access-harm weight increased from one to six. These values are not clinical thresholds. No anatomical model was trained or validated.

CONCLUSION: Hybrid vascular control in complex RAPN is best framed as a hypothesis for future testing, not as a patient-selection rule. Prospective outcome-labelled data and comparative clinical evaluation are required before performance, safety or utility can be assessed.

title: ASFNR Clinical State-of-Practice in Neuroimaging of Minor Large Vessel Occlusion Stroke.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minor ischemic stroke (MIS) with anterior large vessel occlusion (LVO) is a distinct stroke subtype in which mild neurological deficits may mask a substantial volume of threatened but salvageable brain tissue. Despite a baseline NIHSS≤5, nearly one-third of patients experience poor functional outcomes, often due to early neurological deterioration (END).

CURRENT EVIDENCE AND ONGOING TRIALS: Patients with LVO-MIS were markedly underrepresented in landmark thrombectomy trials, resulting in limited evidence to guide treatment. Retrospective studies have identified imaging biomarkers of END, including proximal occlusion, clot length, collateral status, and perfusion mismatch, but the benefit of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remains uncertain. Ongoing randomized controlled trials, including STEP and MOSTE, are expected to define the role of EVT and imaging-based patient selection in this population.

PURPOSE: To summarize the current state of neuroimaging in anterior circulation LVO-MIS and provide a practical imaging workflow and reporting checklist for diagnosis, prognostication, and treatment selection.

KEY POINTS: CTA remains the primary modality for LVO detection and collateral assessment, while CT and MR perfusion identify salvageable tissue and predict END beyond baseline NIHSS. MRI further refines infarct core, perfusion deficit, and thrombus characterization. Current AI-based LVO detection tools improve stroke triage but require careful human oversight because proximal M2 and non-terminus ICA occlusions may be missed.

CONCLUSION: Pending results from ongoing trials, tissue-based imaging with CTA, CT perfusion, and MR perfusion can complement clinical assessment to improve risk stratification and individualized treatment decisions. Advances in quantitative imaging and artificial intelligence are expected to further enable precision imaging-guided management of LVO-MIS.

title: Evaluating an Estimated Blood Volume-Based Enoxaparin Dosing Protocol in Emergency General Surgery Patients.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Low antifactor Xa (AFXa) levels are associated with venous thromboembolism (VTE), and prior research has shown that emergency general surgery (EGS) patients may be underdosed with enoxaparin for VTE prophylaxis. The objective of this study was to describe our experience with utilizing an estimated blood volume (EBV)-based enoxaparin dosing protocol in EGS patients.

METHODS: This was a prospective cohort study of adult EGS patients. Patients eligible for VTE prophylaxis with enoxaparin were dosed using an EBV-based protocol. The primary outcome was peak AFXa level obtained 2.5-6 h after the third dose of enoxaparin. The goal AFXa range was 0.2-0.4 IU/mL. Bleeding complications and in-hospital VTE events were assessed.

RESULTS: There were 121 patients in total, and 62% (n = 75) required an operation. The initial proportion of in-range AFXa levels was 61% (n = 74), and there were no differences between those in the operative versus nonoperative groups (operative in-range: 64%, n = 48, nonoperative: 57%, n = 26, P = 0.17). Bleeding complications occurred in 4.96% of patients, all of which were in the operative group. There were no VTE events.

CONCLUSIONS: An EBV-based enoxaparin dosing protocol led to over half of EGS patients having in-range AFXa levels, and there were no differences between those who required an operation and those who did not. A major barrier to protocol implementation included appropriate timing of lab collection. Further research is needed to directly compare EBV-based protocols to other dosing protocols in EGS patients to improve VTE prophylaxis protocols.

The objective of this study was to describe our experience with utilizing an estimated blood volume (EBV)-based enoxaparin dosing protocol in EGS patients. METHODS: This was a prospective cohort study of adult EGS patients.

title: Clinical evaluation of a novel artificial intelligence-based image processing algorithm for two-dimensional angiography.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To evaluate the clinical performance of a novel artificial intelligence (AI)-based image processing algorithm for two-dimensional angiographic imaging compared with its predecessor across multiple imaging modes, anatomic regions, and endovascular specialties.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, comparative, randomized, paired, and blinded multicenter reader study included anonymized images acquired during clinically indicated endovascular interventions at 11 institutions in the United States and Europe. A total of 553 image series from 182 patients representing 51 procedure types across interventional radiology, neurointervention, cardiology, and pediatric cardiology were processed using both the AI-based and predecessor image processing algorithms. Thirteen board-certified physicians independently evaluated paired images using five-point Likert scales for overall image quality, contrast of clinically relevant details, noise reduction, and confidence in assessing device and vessel details. The primary endpoint was non-inferiority of overall image quality. Secondary endpoints evaluated superiority across image quality metrics using a predefined hierarchical testing strategy.

RESULTS: The AI-based image processing algorithm demonstrated non-inferior overall image quality in 98.9% of all evaluations (95% confidence interval [CI], 98%-100%), meeting the primary endpoint across all imaging modes, anatomic regions, and predefined subgroups. Superiority of the AI-based algorithm was demonstrated for overall image quality, contrast of clinically relevant details, noise reduction, and confidence in assessing device and vessel details across fluoroscopy, roadmap, overlay reference, and native acquisition imaging. Overall image quality superiority was not demonstrated for digital subtraction angiography, likely reflecting the intrinsically higher signal-to-noise characteristics of these acquisitions. Inter-reader agreement analysis demonstrated identical ratings in 49.3% of evaluations, with 94.7% of paired ratings differing by no more than one Likert category.

CONCLUSIONS: In this multicenter blinded reader study, AI-based image processing demonstrated non-inferior overall image quality compared with its predecessor across all evaluated imaging modes and patient subgroups, with superior performance for multiple image quality metrics in fluoroscopy, roadmap, overlay reference, and native acquisition imaging. These findings support the clinical utility of AI-based image processing for endovascular imaging and provide a foundation for future studies evaluating its impact on radiation dose and procedural outcomes.

title: Limited arch repair versus extended arch repair for acute type A aortic dissection: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE(S): To compare early and long-term outcomes of limited arch repair versus extended arch repair for acute type A aortic dissection.

METHODS: Comparative studies evaluating limited (proximal) arch repair and extended arch repair were included. Studies with mixed isolated ascending or nonseparable proximal comparators were excluded from the primary synthesis. Random-effects meta-analyses using restricted maximum likelihood with Hartung-Knapp adjustment were performed to pool risk ratios for early binary outcomes and hazard ratios for long-term outcomes.

RESULTS: Twenty-five reports were included in the updated systematic review. After endpoint-specific adjudication of potentially overlapping institutional cohorts, the number of reports contributing to each pooled analysis varied by outcome. EAR was associated with a higher risk of early mortality (RR 1.31, 95% CI 1.01-1.70) and re-exploration for bleeding (RR 1.23, 95% CI 1.04-1.45). No statistically significant associations were detected for postoperative stroke (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.96-1.20) or dialysis (RR 1.21, 95% CI 0.99-1.49). HR-based analyses showed no statistically significant association with overall survival (HR 1.32, 95% CI 0.91-1.92) or distal aortic reintervention (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.07-13.78).

CONCLUSIONS: In retrospective observational comparisons, EAR was associated with higher early mortality and re-exploration for bleeding, whereas no statistically significant associations were detected for postoperative stroke or dialysis. No statistically significant associations were detected for overall survival or distal aortic reintervention. These findings do not establish causal effects of repair extent and remain limited by confounding by indication.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE(S): To compare early and long-term outcomes of limited arch repair versus extended arch repair for acute type A aortic dissection. METHODS: Comparative studies evaluating limited (proximal) arch repair and extended arch repair were included. Studies with mixed isolated ascending or nonseparable proximal comparators were excluded from the primary synthesis.

title: Effect of multivitamin-mineral supplementation on cardiovascular-related functional health status in older adults: secondary findings from the COSMOS randomized clinical trial.
abstract: Declines in cardiovascular-related functional health status are common with aging, yet the long-term effects of multivitamin-mineral (MVM) and cocoa extract (CE) supplementation on patient-reported outcomes remain unclear in older adults. This prespecified secondary analysis of the COcoa Supplement and Multivitamin Outcomes Study (COSMOS) examined whether daily MVM or CE influenced Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) scores in generally healthy older adults and those with pre-existing heart conditions. COSMOS was a 2 × 2 factorial, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 21,442 US adults (men ≥ 60, women ≥ 65 years) without major cardiovascular disease at baseline. All participants were included in intention-to-treat (ITT) analyses of physical ability score (PAS), symptom burden (SB), and clinical summary score (CSS), representing KCCQ outcomes over 3 years. Linear mixed-effects models estimated treatment effects, with prespecified subgroup analyses among participants with cardiac conditions. Among a total cohort of over 21,000 participants, those taking a daily MVM versus placebo had small but statistically significant improvements in SB (MD 0.44, 95% CI 0.13-0.74) and CSS (MD 0.33, 95% CI 0.09-0.57) (both P < 0.05), with no significant effect on PAS, compared to placebo. CE supplementation had no overall effect. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested heterogeneity in MVM effects according to carotid stenosis status, with year 3 ITT differences of 5.13 points for PAS and 4.95 points for CSS (P-interaction = 0.012 and 0.009, respectively). For CE, the primary ITT analysis provided limited evidence of subgroup benefit. This is the first large randomized clinical trial to evaluate the long-term effects of MVM and CE supplementation on KCCQ-assessed cardiovascular functional health in older adults. Our findings provide new evidence that daily MVM supplementation, but not CE, is associated with small improvements in cardiovascular-related functional health status among older adults, warranting further investigation. The trial was registered at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT02422745 ; unique identifier: NCT02422745.

This prespecified secondary analysis of the COcoa Supplement and Multivitamin Outcomes Study (COSMOS) examined whether daily MVM or CE influenced Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire (KCCQ) scores in generally healthy older adults and those with pre-existing heart conditions. COSMOS was a 2 × 2 factorial, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of 21,442 US adults (men ≥ 60, women ≥ 65 years) without major cardiovascular disease at baseline.

title: Hospital Volume, Stroke Severity, and In-Hospital Mortality after Basilar Artery Thrombectomy in the United States.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Hospital volume is associated with outcomes after anterior-circulation thrombectomy, but its relationship with mortality after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for basilar artery occlusion (BAO) is uncertain. We examined trends, hospital volume, and the influence of coded stroke severity on mortality after BAO thrombectomy.

METHODS: Serial cross-sectional analysis of the National Inpatient Sample, 2016-2023. Adults with a principal ischemic stroke diagnosis and a basilar artery infarction code (ICD-10-CM I63.02, I63.12, I63.22) were included; the National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) was derived from R29.7xx codes. Hospital volume was measured within each year as BAO-specific and all-stroke EVT volume. Analyses used survey-weighted regression, interrupted time series, and propensity matching with and without NIHSS.

RESULTS: Among 9,049 BAO admissions (weighted 45,245), 2,335 (25.8%) received EVT. EVT use rose from 16.4% to 32.0%, and EVT-recipient mortality declined from 33.3% to 27.2%, without a robust change at trial publication. Highest-volume centers treated more severe and more often transferred patients and had lower NIHSS-adjusted mortality (BAO-specific volume: odds ratio [OR] 0.76, 95% CI 0.56-1.02; all-stroke volume: OR 0.82, 0.61-1.10; sensitivity analyses 0.73-0.83), without a monotonic gradient. NIHSS adjustment attenuated the matched mortality OR for EVT from 2.46 (2.16-2.80) to 1.31 (1.12-1.53); by severity stratum, ORs ranged from 7.74 (NIHSS 0-4) to 0.80 (NIHSS 21-42).

CONCLUSION: US basilar thrombectomy use doubled across the trial era while in-hospital mortality declined gradually. Highest-volume centers had consistently but imprecisely lower severity-adjusted mortality. Coded NIHSS materially changes treatment associations and should be standard in administrative stroke research.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Hospital volume is associated with outcomes after anterior-circulation thrombectomy, but its relationship with mortality after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for basilar artery occlusion (BAO) is uncertain. We examined trends, hospital volume, and the influence of coded stroke severity on mortality after BAO thrombectomy. METHODS: Serial cross-sectional analysis of the National Inpatient Sample, 2016-2023.

title: Longitudinal Trends of Intact and Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repairs in the United States: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted access to elective procedures and routine care. Given the risk of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture, understanding repair trends is important to assess the impact of the pandemic on vascular outcomes.

METHODS: This repeated cross-sectional analysis used the TriNetX network, a multicenter US electronic health records database. We included 423 874 patients diagnosed with AAA from 2016 to 2024. Patients were categorized by clinical presentation-intact AAA and ruptured AAA-and stratified by surgical approach: endovascular aneurysm repair or open aneurysm repair. Annual trends in AAA repair rates were assessed using joinpoint regression to calculate annual percentage change.

RESULTS: Among 19 330 AAA repairs, 3791 (19.6%) were open aneurysm repair, and 15 539 (80.4%) were endovascular aneurysm repair. From 2018 to 2024, 1623 repairs (9.9%) were for ruptured AAA and 14 835 (90.1%) were for intact AAA. The rate of intact AAA repairs initially remained stable from 2018 to 2022 but significantly decreased after the pandemic from 2022 to 2024 (annual percentage change, -2.87% [95% CI, -10.95 to -1.00]). In contrast, ruptured AAA repairs rates shifted sharply during the pandemic, with an established prepandemic decline in ruptured repairs from 2018 to 2020 (annual percentage change, -11.48%) reversed, with an increase from 2020 to 2022 (annual percentage change +12.01%), before declining from 2022 to 2024 (annual percentage change, -11.00%).

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, repairs for intact AAA declined, while repairs for ruptured AAA increased during the pandemic period. These trends suggest that potential delays in routine surveillance and elective surgery during the pandemic may have increased acute presentations.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted access to elective procedures and routine care. Given the risk of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture, understanding repair trends is important to assess the impact of the pandemic on vascular outcomes. METHODS: This repeated cross-sectional analysis used the TriNetX network, a multicenter US electronic health records database.

title: Cardiovascular morbidity and mortality in acromegaly-associated diabetes: a Swedish nationwide study.
abstract:
CONTEXT: Secondary diabetes mellitus occurs in 30% to 50% of patients with acromegaly despite a lean phenotype, whereas type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with adiposity.

OBJECTIVE: We compared mortality, morbidity, and treatment patterns between patients with acromegaly-associated diabetes (ACRO-DM) and T2DM.

DESIGN: Nationwide, retrospective, matched-cohort study in Sweden.

METHODS: The ACRO-DM group included patients with an acromegaly diagnosis in the Patient Register, with diabetes registered in the National Diabetes Register (NDR) or a dispensed glucose-lowering drug in the Prescribed Drug Register. Controls with T2DM from the NDR were matched 10:1 for sex, age, calendar year, and diabetes duration. We derived mortality and morbidity outcomes from the Death and Patient Registers.

RESULTS: We included 348 patients with ACRO-DM and 3480 with T2DM. Mean (SD) age was 60.3 (13.2) and 59.5 (15.6) years, whereas diabetes duration was 2.8 (5.8) and 3.0 (7.1) years in ACRO-DM and T2DM, respectively. Baseline cardiovascular morbidity was more common in ACRO-DM than T2DM group (61% vs 43%), including hypertension (48% vs 29%), heart failure (11% vs 5%), arrhythmia (13% vs 9%), and stroke (8% vs 5%).The hazard ratio (HR) for overall mortality was 1.18 (95% CI, 0.96-1.46) in ACRO-DM compared with T2DM group. The ACRO-DM group had a higher risk of cardiovascular morbidity (HR = 1.55; 95% CI, 1.24-1.94), with increased hazards for venous thromboembolism, specifically pulmonary, and arrhythmia, whereas cardiovascular mortality was not increased (HR = 1.12; 95% CI, 0.78-1.60).

CONCLUSION: The risk of cardiovascular morbidity was increased in patients with ACRO-DM compared to T2DM.

title: Mortality After Emergency versus Elective Ventral Hernia Repair: A Propensity-Matched ACHQC Study.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Outcomes of ventral hernia repair (VHR) differ substantially between elective and emergency settings. Prior population-based studies have demonstrated increased morbidity and mortality with emergency repair, but limited data exist from disease-specific hernia registries incorporating detailed anatomical and operative variables.

METHODS: Records from the Abdominal Core Health Quality Collaborative (ACHQC) registry spanning 2013 through 2023 were reviewed retrospectively. Adult patients undergoing VHR were identified. Emergency cases were paired with elective cases in a 1:2 ratio through propensity score matching built on demographics, comorbidities, and hernia characteristics. We judged the groups balanced when the standardized mean difference (SMD) for every covariate fell below 0.1. Death within 90 days was the primary endpoint. Length of stay (LOS), surgical site infection (SSI), and systemic complications were examined as secondary endpoints.

RESULTS: Among 36,788 patients, 965 (2.6%) underwent emergency repair. After matching, 955 emergency and 1,906 elective patients were analyzed with excellent covariate balance (SMD < 0.1). Within 90 days, 1.6% of emergency patients had died versus 0.3% of elective patients (P < .001). Emergency patients stayed a median of 4 days (interquartile range [IQR] 1-6), 4 times the 1 day (IQR 0-5) recorded for elective patients (P < .001). SSI developed in 9% of emergency and 6% of elective patients (P = .02), and surgical site occurrence requiring procedural intervention in 11% and 8%, respectively (P = .003). The emergency group also had more deep vein thrombosis (1% vs 0.2%, P < .001), postoperative respiratory failure (1% vs 0.4%, P = .01), and septic shock (0.4% vs 0.1%, P = .03).

CONCLUSION: In this registry-based propensity-matched analysis, 90-day mortality and postoperative morbidity were both higher after emergency than after elective VHR. These findings highlight the association between emergency presentation and adverse outcomes and underscore the potential importance of timely elective evaluation and preoperative optimization in appropriately selected patients.

Prior population-based studies have demonstrated increased morbidity and mortality with emergency repair, but limited data exist from disease-specific hernia registries incorporating detailed anatomical and operative variables. METHODS: Records from the Abdominal Core Health Quality Collaborative (ACHQC) registry spanning 2013 through 2023 were reviewed retrospectively.

title: Safety of home treatment for incidental pulmonary embolism in cancer patients.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Incidental pulmonary embolism (iPE) is increasingly detected in computed tomography (CT) scans for scheduled cancer staging, but the safety of outpatient management in these patients with active cancer remains uncertain, as current guidelines usually do not define patients with pulmonary embolism and cancer as low risk.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included adults with active cancer and iPE diagnosed on a scheduled staging CT scan at a tertiary hospital in Germany between January 2020 and June 2024, excluding patients who were hospitalized at the time of the scan. The primary outcome was 90-day event-free survival. Events were unscheduled consultations or emergency department presentations, progression of venous thromboembolism, clinically relevant bleeding or death.

RESULTS: Of 212 patients included, 89.2% were managed as outpatients. Patients treated at home were less likely to have bilateral pulmonary embolism, evidence of right ventricular dysfunction, an elevated troponin or hypoxemia. 90-day all-cause mortality was 5.2%, deaths occurred usually while the patient was receiving hospice care. For patients treated at home clinically relevant bleeding occurred in 1.6% and progression of thromboembolism in 2.1%.

CONCLUSION: In this cohort of patients diagnosed with iPE, most patients were treated at home. With 90-day mortality likely being mainly caused by the malignancy, home treatment appears safe if cancer is the only risk factor present.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included adults with active cancer and iPE diagnosed on a scheduled staging CT scan at a tertiary hospital in Germany between January 2020 and June 2024, excluding patients who were hospitalized at the time of the scan. The primary outcome was 90-day event-free survival.

title: Post-Traumatic Abdominal Aortic Dissection Associating Solid Organ Injury in a Child.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Handlebar injuries are frequent events in children, often perceived as minor, but may result in severe intra-abdominal damage.

CASE PRESENTATION: We report the case of a 13-year-old boy who sustained a blunt abdominal trauma following impact against a bicycle handlebar. In this case, the trauma produced an unusual and potentially life-threatening combination of lesions, including massive hemoperitoneum, a deep hepatic laceration, a severe pancreatic injury with disruption of the main pancreatic duct, and a post-traumatic dissection of the infrarenal abdominal aorta.

RESULTS: The patient was admitted in critical condition and underwent prompt clinical, laboratory, and radiological evaluation. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography revealed the extent of the abdominal injuries and confirmed the vascular involvement. Given the complexity and severity of the findings, management required a rapid multidisciplinary approach involving pediatric surgeons, interventional radiologists, vascular surgeons, and gastroenterologists. The infrarenal aortic dissection was treated urgently with an endovascular approach using the placement of a covered stent, allowing successful exclusion of the lesion and stabilization of the vascular injury while avoiding open surgery. The hepatic injury was managed conservatively with close hemodynamic and radiological monitoring. During the subsequent clinical course, the patient developed a large post-traumatic pancreatic pseudocyst related to the pancreatic duct disruption. This complication was successfully treated with endoscopic ultrasound-guided drainage using a lumen-apposing metal stent (LAMS), which allowed effective internal drainage and progressive resolution of the collection.

CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the potentially severe nature of bicycle handlebar injuries in children and emphasizes the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion for occult intra-abdominal and vascular injuries. Early diagnosis and timely multimodal management are crucial to optimize outcomes in these complex traumatic scenarios.

In this case, the trauma produced an unusual and potentially life-threatening combination of lesions, including massive hemoperitoneum, a deep hepatic laceration, a severe pancreatic injury with disruption of the main pancreatic duct, and a post-traumatic dissection of the infrarenal abdominal aorta.

title: Risk of Venous Thromboembolism in Patients with Resectable Colorectal Cancer According to Stage.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a significant source of morbidity in patients undergoing colectomy and proctectomy for colorectal adenocarcinoma. However, the association between cancer stage and VTE risk is unclear. We aimed to describe the association between colorectal cancer stage and post-operative VTE among patients undergoing resection for colorectal cancer.

METHODS: Utilizing the 2022-2023 American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program database, a retrospective cohort study was conducted. A multivariable logistic regression analyzed the association between VTE and cancer stage with adjustments for covariates.

RESULTS: Of 18,830 patients fitting inclusion criteria, 4,418 (23%) had stage I adenocarcinoma, 6,509 (35%) had stage II, 6,402 (34%) had stage III and 1,501 (8%) had stage IV; while 302 (2%) experienced postoperative VTE. On univariate analysis, patients with stage II, III and IV cancers had higher VTE rates than patients with stage I (stage I: 0.9%, stage II: 1.7%, stage III: 1.8%: stage IV 2.5%; p < 0.001). In the multivariable analysis of VTE risk, patients with stage II, III and IV cancer had higher odds of VTE relative to patients with stage I cancer (OR for stage II vs. I: 1.57; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.08, 2.27; p = 0.017; OR for stage III vs. I: 1.77; 95% CI: 1.22, 2.55; p = 0.002; OR for stage IV vs. I: 1.73, 95% CI:1.07, 2.79; p = 0.025).

CONCLUSION: Resectable colorectal cancers at higher stages are associated with increased risk of VTE. Understanding the differences in risk can help clinicians make more informed and targeted treatment plans for patients undergoing colectomy or proctectomy for locoregional adenocarcinoma.

However, the association between cancer stage and VTE risk is unclear. We aimed to describe the association between colorectal cancer stage and post-operative VTE among patients undergoing resection for colorectal cancer.

title: Robot-assisted partial nephrectomy with venous tumor thrombectomy for classic renal angiomyolipoma: standardized technique and short-term outcomes.
abstract:
PURPOSE: To achieve the dual goals of effective tumor control and maximal renal function preservation, we have proposed a standardized robot-assisted nephron-sparing surgery combined with venous thrombectomy for classic renal angiomyolipoma (AML) with venous tumor thrombus (VTT). This study aimed to evaluate the technical feasibility and clinical rationality of this innovative surgical technique.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 17 patients who underwent robot-assisted partial nephrectomy (RAPN) with venous tumor thrombectomy and 16 patients who underwent robot-assisted radical nephrectomy with venous tumor thrombectomy. The radical-nephrectomy cohort served as a historical clinical comparator. The modified thrombectomy strategy followed the proposed "NSS" technical principles. Functional and oncological outcomes were analyzed.

RESULTS: All procedures were completed without open conversion or intraoperative tumor-thrombus dislodgement, and no RAPN case required conversion to radical nephrectomy. The RAPN group had shorter operative time (160.0 vs. 232.5 min, p=0.021), shorter left renal vein clamping (3.0 vs. 16.5 min, p<0.001) and IVC clamping time (3.0 vs. 16.0 min, p<0.001), and better renal function preservation (p<0.001). Renal function was better preserved in RAPN group, primarily reflecting retention of the affected kidney. During the available follow-up (median 9 months in the RAPN group and 55 months in the Control group), no recurrence was detected; however, follow-up was insufficient for comparative or long-term oncological conclusions.

CONCLUSIONS: RAPN with venous tumor thrombectomy appears technically feasible in patients with classic renal AML with VTT. This surgical approach could better preserve renal function, but the long-term outcomes require confirmation in larger series with longer follow-up.

title: Pharmacological strategies for hemodialysis arteriovenous fistula and graft patency: an access-stratified systematic review and network meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pharmacological therapies target different stages of hemodialysis access failure. We compared treatments separately in arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) and grafts (AVGs), accounting for differences in outcomes and follow-up.

METHODS: This PROSPERO-registered review (CRD420261411441) followed PRISMA 2020 and PRISMA-NMA guidance. PubMed, Embase, CENTRAL/Cochrane records, and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched through May 31, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed RoB 2. Separate random-effects frequentist network meta-analyses were supplemented by time-restricted analyses and exploratory follow-up meta-regression.

RESULTS: Among 1,557 records, 31 reports were included; 23 trial datasets contributed to the primary analyses (15 AVF and 8 AVG). In AVFs, ticlopidine (OR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.18-0.76) and clopidogrel (0.49; 0.24-0.97) may reduce predominantly early access failure (low certainty); estimates remained favorable at follow-up of 8 weeks or less. Larger single-trial effects for heparin plus anisodamine and clopidogrel plus a prostacyclin analog were very uncertain. Fish oil showed no clear AVF benefit. In AVGs, apixaban may reduce thrombosis (0.12; 0.03-0.41; low certainty), but its interval widened to 0.007-1.94 in the approximately 12-month subset. The aspirin estimate (3.35; 1.21-9.27) was very uncertain and imprecise under timing restrictions.

CONCLUSIONS: Ticlopidine and clopidogrel may reduce early AVF failure without established improvement in functional maturation. AVG apixaban findings require confirmation, and the effect of aspirin remains very uncertain. Interpretation depends on the clinical outcome, follow-up, and bleeding risk.

We compared treatments separately in arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) and grafts (AVGs), accounting for differences in outcomes and follow-up. title: Comparative real-world outcomes of LifeStream and Viabahn VBX balloon-expandable covered stents for iliac artery occlusive disease.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Balloon-expandable covered stents (CSs) are increasingly used for complex iliac artery occlusive disease, but direct comparative data among CS platforms remain limited. This study compared 1-year restenosis and clinical outcomes between the LifeStream and Viabahn VBX CSs in patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT).

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 226 patients who underwent EVT for symptomatic iliac artery occlusive disease using either the LifeStream CS (n = 95) or Viabahn VBX CS (n = 131). Outcomes included restenosis, clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR), re-occlusion, conversion to bypass surgery, and perioperative complications (POCs). Between-group comparisons were performed using inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) based on propensity scores.

RESULTS: One-year follow-up data were available for 163 of 226 patients (72.1%), and 10 restenosis events occurred during follow-up. After IPTW adjustment, the balance of measured covariates was substantially improved. The estimated 1-year freedom from restenosis was 95.8% (95% confidence interval [CI], 93.1-98.6%) in the LifeStream group and 95.8% (95% CI, 93.1-98.6%) in the Viabahn VBX group, with no statistically significant between-group difference (p = 0.99). No significant differences were detected in freedom from CD-TLR (99.2% [95% CI, 98.0-100.0%] vs. 96.7% [95% CI, 94.3-99.2%]; p = 0.13), re-occlusion (100.0% [95% CI, 100.0-100.0%] vs. 98.1% [95% CI, 96.3-99.9%]; p = 0.091), conversion to bypass surgery (100.0% [95% CI, 100.0-100.0%] vs. 98.2% [95% CI, 96.4-100.0%]; p = 0.083), or POCs.

CONCLUSION: In this IPTW-adjusted multicenter retrospective study, no statistically significant differences in 1-year restenosis or other clinical outcomes were detected between the LifeStream and Viabahn VBX balloon-expandable CSs. These findings should be considered hypothesis-generating because of the small number of events, incomplete follow-up, and potential residual confounding.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included 226 patients who underwent EVT for symptomatic iliac artery occlusive disease using either the LifeStream CS (n = 95) or Viabahn VBX CS (n = 131).

title: Heat-Based Therapies in Hypertension Management: A Systematic Review of Physiological Mechanisms.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for several cardiovascular diseases, leading to the need for investigations of user-friendly and less costly nonpharmacological interventions, including passive heat therapies. This study synthesized information on heat-based therapies used in prehypertension and hypertension management, as well as their clinical efficacy, physiological mechanisms, and translational potential.

METHODS: We systematically reviewed 13 eligible human studies published between 2000 and 2025 per the PRISMA 2020 checklist, assessed randomized studies with RoB 2 and nonrandomized studies with ROBINS-I, and used SWiM-guided narrative synthesis because interventions, populations, comparators, and outcomes were heterogeneous. Certainty was assessed using GRADE. The review protocol was not preregistered.

RESULTS: Acute blood-pressure reductions and changes in vascular or autonomic markers were reported in some populations, but sustained comparative effects in hypertension remain uncertain. In hypertensive participants, both hot and thermoneutral immersion were associated with reductions in 24-h blood pressure (BP), limiting heat-specific attribution. A single pooled effect estimate and corresponding 95% confidence interval were not calculated. The benefits were linked to lower sympathetic activity, more nitric oxide availability, lower endothelin-1 levels, and less oxidative stress. Outcome-specific GRADE certainty was very low for SBP and DBP and the assessed mechanistic domains.

CONCLUSION: Passive heat exposure can produce short-term reductions in BP and changes in vascular function, but sustained antihypertensive efficacy, particularly when evaluated with 24-h ambulatory BP in patients with established hypertension, remains uncertain. Mechanistic findings from heart-failure and peripheral artery disease (PAD) cohorts are indirect evidence for uncomplicated hypertension. Passive heat should not replace established antihypertensive treatment. Safety evidence is limited to selected, often supervised populations, and larger trials with ambulatory BP and systematic adverse-event assessment are needed.

METHODS: We systematically reviewed 13 eligible human studies published between 2000 and 2025 per the PRISMA 2020 checklist, assessed randomized studies with RoB 2 and nonrandomized studies with ROBINS-I, and used SWiM-guided narrative synthesis because interventions, populations, comparators, and outcomes were heterogeneous.

title: Anterior mitral leaflet modification to prevent left ventricular outflow tract obstruction during transcatheter mitral valve replacement: the PROTECT-LVOT registry.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction remains the major limitation of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Anterior mitral leaflet (AML) modification has emerged as a key preventive strategy, yet real-world data remain limited and residual risk is still unknown.

AIMS: We sought to evaluate the outcomes of TMVR with concomitant AML modification across valve-in-mitral annular calcification (ViMAC), valve-in-ring (ViR), and valve-in-valve (ViV) substrates.

METHODS: We established a multicentre retrospective registry of consecutive patients undergoing TMVR with AML modification between 2017 and 2025. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, stroke/transient ischaemic attack, and major bleeding.

RESULTS: A total of 55 patients were included (67% females). The median age was 78 years (interquartile range [IQR] 73-81); the median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality was 6.7% (IQR 4.8-9.5). AML modification was performed in 65.5% of cases with the Laceration of the Anterior Mitral leaflet to Prevent Outflow ObstructioN technique and in 34.5% with the Balloon-Assisted Translocation of the Mitral Anterior Leaflet technique. AML modification was successful in 96.4% of cases. Despite successful AML modification, haemodynamically significant LVOT obstruction occurred in 12.7% of cases. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint occurred in 20.0% of patients, driven by cardiovascular death in 14.5% of patients. Overall in-hospital mortality was 16.4%. The ViMAC substrate was associated with the numerically highest LVOT obstruction rate (ViMAC 20.7%, ViR 0.0%, ViV 8.3%, odds ratio [OR] 4.72, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.89-47.86; p=0.070). The aortomitral angle showed a borderline association with LVOT obstruction (OR 1.22 per degree, 95% CI: 0.99-1.48; p=0.059).

CONCLUSIONS: AML modification enables TMVR in high-risk anatomies with high feasibility but does not eliminate LVOT obstruction. ViMAC represents the most challenging substrate.

Anterior mitral leaflet (AML) modification has emerged as a key preventive strategy, yet real-world data remain limited and residual risk is still unknown. AIMS: We sought to evaluate the outcomes of TMVR with concomitant AML modification across valve-in-mitral annular calcification (ViMAC), valve-in-ring (ViR), and valve-in-valve (ViV) substrates.

title: Repurposing drugs for aortic aneurysm: unlocking new therapeutic opportunities.
abstract: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a life-threatening vascular disease for which no pharmacological therapy has been proven to effectively limit disease progression. Drug repurposing (DR), which leverages existing drugs with established safety profiles, offers a promising and cost-effective strategy to accelerate therapeutic development for AA. In this review, we summarize recent advances in DR research for AA, highlighting the emerging framework that integrates computational prediction with experimental and clinical validation. We discuss key repurposed drug candidates, evaluate the current state of translational evidence, and examine the challenges that have hindered clinical success despite encouraging preclinical findings. Finally, we outline opportunities to enhance target identification, patient stratification, and clinical trial design. By bridging mechanistic discovery and translational application, DR may provide a practical pathway toward effective medical therapies for aneurysmal disease.

title: [Effect of sequential multi-dose tranexamic acid administration on perioperative blood loss in cervical posterior single-door laminoplasty and its safety].
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the effect of sequential multi-dose intravenous administration of tranexamic acid (TXA) on perioperative blood loss and inflammatory response in patients undergoing cervical posterior single-door laminoplasty (LMP), and to evaluate its safety.

METHODS: A prospective study was conducted in patients diagnosed with multi-level cervical spondylotic myelopathy, who underwent cervical posterior single-door LMP between January 2023 and June 2024. Using a computer-generated randomization table, patients were allocated into three groups. Placebo control group (group A): received 100 mL of normal saline intravenously at 30 minutes before incision (after anesthesia induction); the same dose was repeated every 5 hours for a total of 3 administrations. Single-dose control group (group B): received 1.0 g of TXA (dissolved in 100 mL normal saline) at 30 minutes before incision, followed by 100 mL of normal saline every 5 hours for a total of 2 additional doses. Sequential multi-dose group (group C): received 1.0 g of TXA (dissolved in 100 mL normal saline) at 30 minutes before incision, with an additional 1.0 g of TXA administered intravenously at 5 hours and 10 hours postoperatively, for a total dose of 3.0 g. A total of 120 patients met the selection criteria and were included in the study. After excluding lost-to-follow-up and withdrawn patients, 39 cases in group A, 37 in group B, and 38 in group C were included in the final analysis. There was no significant difference between groups (P>0.05) in age, gender, height, body weight, body mass index, comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes), and preoperative hematocrit (HCT), hemoglobin, D-dimer (D-D), interleukin 6 (IL-6), and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels. The primary outcome was total blood loss (TBL). Secondary outcomes included intraoperative blood loss (IBL), postoperative blood loss (PBL), drain removal time (DRT), HCT, D-D, IL-6, CRP, allogeneic blood transfusion rate, and incidence of complications.

RESULTS: Blood loss assessment: TBL, PBL, DRT, postoperative decline in HCT, and the allogeneic blood transfusion rate were all the lowest in group C, followed by group B, and the highest in group A, with significant differences between groups (P<0.05). The IBL was significantly lower in groups B and C than in group A (P<0.05), while there was no significant difference between groups B and C (P>0.05). Changes in inflammatory indicators: the levels of D-D and IL-6 in 3 groups reached peak at 1 day, the level of CRP reached peak at 3 days, and both decreased at 5 days, but still remained higher than preoperative levels, with significant differences (P<0.05). At different time points, the levels of D-D, IL-6, and CRP were significant lower in group C than in groups A and B (P<0.05), and in group B than in group A (P<0.05). Safety evaluation: During the 30-day postoperative follow-up, no deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, incisional infection, incisional hematoma, or TXA-related allergic reaction occurred in 3 groups.

CONCLUSION: Sequential multi-dose TXA administration effectively reduces perioperative blood loss in cervical posterior single-door LMP, suppresses postoperative hyperfibrinolysis and inflammatory response, shortens drainage duration, and does not increase the risk of thromboembolic events. This regimen represents a safe and effective optimization strategy for perioperative blood management in LMP.

METHODS: A prospective study was conducted in patients diagnosed with multi-level cervical spondylotic myelopathy, who underwent cervical posterior single-door LMP between January 2023 and June 2024. Using a computer-generated randomization table, patients were allocated into three groups.

title: Effect of Different Single-Session Durations of Intermittent Pneumatic Compression on the Prevention of Deep Vein Thrombosis in Postoperative ICU Patients: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a common and potentially life-threatening complication in postoperative ICU patients. Intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) is widely used for mechanical thromboprophylaxis; however, the optimal single-session duration of IPC remains unclear. This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy of different single-session durations of IPC for preventing DVT in postoperative ICU patients. MATERIAL AND METHODS This prospective randomized controlled trial enrolled 138 patients who were randomized into 3 groups (n = 46 each) receiving IPC 3 times daily, with single-session durations of 40 minutes, 2 hours, or 6 hours. DVT incidence, coagulation parameters (D-dimer [mg/L] and fibrinogen [FIB; g/L]), and adverse events were compared on postoperative days 3 and 5. RESULTS Baseline characteristics were comparable among groups (P>0.05). The 6-hour group had a DVT incidence of 0% on both days, significantly lower than those in the 40-minute (15.21% and 32.61%) and 2-hour (8.70% and 34.78%) groups (P<0.05). No significant intergroup differences in D-dimer levels were observed (P>0.05); FIB levels significantly differed only on day 3 (P<0.05). Adverse events occurred in 6 patients (13.04%) in the 6-hour group, whereas none occurred in the other 2 groups. CONCLUSIONS Although 6-hour single-session IPC provides the most effective DVT prevention, it is associated with a higher risk of skin-related adverse events. Shorter, more frequent IPC (40 minutes or 2 hours per session, 3 times daily) may represent a preferable strategy for postoperative ICU patients due to its balance of efficacy, safety, and clinical feasibility.

Intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) is widely used for mechanical thromboprophylaxis; however, the optimal single-session duration of IPC remains unclear. This randomized controlled trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy of different single-session durations of IPC for preventing DVT in postoperative ICU patients.

title: Lesion-targeting and vascular matrix-penetrating siRNA nanotherapeutics for the treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysm.
abstract: Inefficient aneurysmal aorta enrichment and vascular matrix penetration represent major challenges against siRNA delivery for the management of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Herein, platelet membrane (PM)-reversibly camouflaged nanocomplexes (NCs) are developed to deliver Poldip2 siRNA (siPoldip2) into vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), which then restore vascular homeostasis by promoting phenotypic switching and mitigating oxidative stress. The NCs comprise a cationic nanocore assembled from siPoldip2 and a guanidinated and fluorinated bifunctional helical polypeptide (8FP), a charge-reversal intermediate layer of poly(l-lysine)-cis-aconitic acid (PC), and an outer shell of PM. After systemic administration in CaCl2-induced AAA rats, the NCs could preferentially accumulate at the aneurysmal site due to PM-mediated recognition of RGD-containing extracellular matrix proteins. The slightly acidic aneurysmal microenvironment subsequently triggers charge reversal of PC from negative to positive, which promotes the detachment of both PM and PC layers. The exposed 8FP/siPoldip2 nanocore penetrates the vascular matrix due to fluorocarbon-assisted repulsion of collagen mesh adsorption, followed by effective internalization by VSMCs. Consequently, Poldip2 expression in VSMCs is downregulated, which restores the contractile phenotype, and improves the aortic elasticity as well as structural integrity. This study provides a promising strategy for overcoming vascular delivery barriers and highlights the therapeutic promise of siRNA-based medical intervention for AAA.

The NCs comprise a cationic nanocore assembled from siPoldip2 and a guanidinated and fluorinated bifunctional helical polypeptide (8FP), a charge-reversal intermediate layer of poly(l-lysine)-cis-aconitic acid (PC), and an outer shell of PM.

title: Prediction of Stroke Outcome After Endovascular Thrombectomy From Clinical Characteristics: A Machine Learning Approach.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predicting outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is challenging. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model to predict outcomes after EVT using only clinical characteristics available shortly after hospital arrival, excluding imaging, laboratory, and angiographic data.

METHODS: We analyzed data from the JSDB (Japan Stroke Data Bank), a multicenter, prospective registry of patients with acute stroke. A total of 4353 patients who underwent EVT between 2016 and 2020 were included, with those from 2016 to 2019 assigned to the derivation cohort and those from 2020 to the validation cohort. The model was developed using 132 routinely collected clinical variables that can be rapidly obtained on patient arrival. Feature selection was performed using the Boruta algorithm, and the model was built using CatBoost. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0 to 2 at discharge.

RESULTS: Among 4353 patients treated with EVT, the derivation cohort included 2764 patients and the validation cohort, 1589 patients. In these cohorts, 973 (35.2%) and 547 (34.4%) achieved mRS 0 to 2, respectively. Boruta selected 47 predictors. CatBoost achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.744 (95% CI, 0.710-0.776) in the derivation test set and 0.781 (95% CI, 0.755-0.803) in the validation cohort. Validation areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves were 0.792 (95% CI, 0.765-0.815) for mRS 0 to 1, 0.766 (95% CI, 0.744-0.787) for mRS 0 to 3, and 0.680 (95% CI, 0.631-0.729) for mRS 6.

CONCLUSIONS: Our machine learning model predicted outcomes following EVT using only admission clinical data. This imaging-independent machine learning approach may support early prognostication and facilitate discussions of expected clinical courses.

METHODS: We analyzed data from the JSDB (Japan Stroke Data Bank), a multicenter, prospective registry of patients with acute stroke.

title: Predictors of Clinically Meaningful 1-Year Health Status Improvements Following Endovascular or Surgical Revascularization: Insights From the BEST-CLI Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite efforts to promote limb salvage in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), the factors associated with meaningful health status improvement after revascularization remain poorly understood. We examined predictors of meaningful 1-year health status improvement following revascularization for CLTI.

METHODS: We pooled endovascular and surgical arms from the BEST-CLI (Best Endovascular Versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients With CLTI) randomized controlled trial, including patients with CLTI (150 international sites, 2014-2019). Health status was assessed at baseline and 1 year using the peripheral artery disease-specific Vascular Quality of Life questionnaire, the generic European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, and the Short Form-12 Physical and Mental Component Summary. Distribution-based minimal clinically important difference thresholds were defined as 0.5 SD of baseline health status scores. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of no meaningful 1-year improvement (same/worsened versus improved).

RESULTS: Among 1017 patients (72.0% men, mean age 66.8±9.7 years), clinically meaningful improvements were reported by 76.5% for Vascular Quality of Life, 52.8% European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, 56.7% for Short Form-12 Physical Component Summary, and 42.1% for Short Form-12 Mental Component Summary, regardless of revascularization type (surgical versus endovascular). Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status increased the odds of no meaningful improvement. Revascularization type was not associated with Vascular Quality of Life improvement (odds ratio, 1.059 [95% CI, 0.91-1.23]; P=0.445; C statistic=0.77).

CONCLUSIONS: One-year postrevascularization, over three-fourths of individuals with CLTI perceived meaningful improvements in peripheral artery disease-specific health, and over half improved overall physical health, regardless of procedure type. Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status predicted 1-year health status response. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02060630.

title: Description of antithrombotic therapy in patients undergoing endovascular revascularization for lower extremity peripheral artery disease (DATE-PAD).
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe real-world antithrombotic prescribing patterns following endovascular revascularization for lower extremity peripheral artery disease (PAD), and to compare short-term efficacy and safety outcomes between dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) and single antiplatelet therapy plus oral anticoagulant (SAPT+OAC) regimens.

METHODS: A retrospective, multi-center descriptive study was conducted on patients 18 years or older with acute limb ischemia (ALI) or chronic limb threatening ischemia (CLTI) who underwent endovascular intervention of the lower extremity between January 2023 and August 2024 and were discharged on DAPT or SAPT+OAC. Patients with surgical interventions for PAD during the same admission were excluded. Primary outcome was the frequency of DAPT compared to SAPT+OAC discharge regimens. Secondary outcomes included 30- and 90-day readmissions, bleeding, ischemic events, and amputations all within 90 days.

RESULTS: Of 221 patients, 86% were discharged on DAPT and 14% on SAPT+OAC. Low dose aspirin and clopidogrel was the predominant DAPT regimen (94%). Apixaban was the most common anticoagulant (71%), with 75% of patients receiving 5 mg twice daily dosing. SAPT+OAC was more frequently used in ALI (50%) than CLTI (10%). No significant differences were observed in 30- or 90-day readmissions, bleeding rates, amputations, or ischemic events.

CONCLUSIONS: DAPT remains the predominant regimen post-revascularization despite recommendations for low-dose rivaroxaban plus aspirin. Apixaban was the predominant anticoagulant despite the paucity of data for use in this population. Comparable short-term outcomes suggest both DAPT and SAPT+OAC regimens may be viable, though further research is needed to clarify optimal anticoagulant of choice and dosing, particularly for apixaban.

METHODS: A retrospective, multi-center descriptive study was conducted on patients 18 years or older with acute limb ischemia (ALI) or chronic limb threatening ischemia (CLTI) who underwent endovascular intervention of the lower extremity between January 2023 and August 2024 and were discharged on DAPT or SAPT+OAC. title: Incidence, diagnosis, treatment, and outcomes of abdominal aortic aneurysms in Ontario: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) management substantially changed in 2003 when endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) became readily available in Canada. The long-term implications to routine practice in Ontario are unknown. We therefore sought to estimate trends in stable (sAAA) and ruptured (rAAA) incidence, treatment (EVAR or open surgical repair [OSR]), and postoperative mortality.

METHODS: We constructed a population-based cohort study of patients with incident sAAA and rAAA in Ontario using administrative health data from April 2012 to March 2023. To assess patterns in incidence, autoregressive integrated moving average models were fit. Three population-level interventions were incorporated: a Canadian Society of Vascular Surgery (CSVS) position statement, sent to Ontario physicians in early 2018, about the Canadian AAA screening recommendations published in 2017; the COVID-19 pandemic onset in 2020; and publication of the CSVS screening guidelines for AAA in 2021.

RESULTS: In total, 24 619 patients were included. Patients were predominantly male (77.2%), from urban settings (87.1%), with low comorbidity (82.3%). There was a small month-over-month increase in reported sAAA identified following the CSVS position statement in 2018. Conversely, the COVID-19 pandemic was associated with a steep drop in sAAA reported, which remained thereafter. Publication of the CSVS screening guidelines in 2021 was not associated with a change in sAAA trends. Incidence of rAAA was also reduced during the pandemic but was not affected by either publication. Treatment with EVAR for rAAA increased from 10.2% to 18%, whereas treatment with OSR declined from 40.8% to 31.3%. Untreated sAAA increased from 28.2% to 42.7%. Thirty-day (54.7%) and 1-year (61.7%) postoperative mortality from rAAA was stable, whereas mortality from sAAA increased slightly (30-d: 5% to 6.5%; 1-yr: 14% to 16.5%).

CONCLUSION: Overall reporting of cases of sAAA and rAAA is decreasing in Ontario. The 2018 position statement on AAA screening guidelines led to slightly increased reported sAAA, while reporting of rAAA was not affected. As expected, the volume of patients with rAAA who received EVAR increased, while the volume of those who received OSR decreased.

The long-term implications to routine practice in Ontario are unknown. title: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies comparing aspirin with anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty have had conflicting results.

METHODS: In a comparative-effectiveness noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty to receive aspirin (81 mg twice daily), warfarin (to a target international normalized ratio of 2.0), or rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) for 30 days. The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion. The noninferiority margin for the risk difference was 0.69 percentage points.

RESULTS: Among 18,883 participants who had undergone randomization, 15,317 (7214 with hip arthroplasty and 8103 with knee arthroplasty) were included in the primary per-protocol analysis. A primary effectiveness outcome event occurred in 77 of 6090 participants (1.26%) in the aspirin group, in 52 of 4231 (1.23%) in the warfarin group, and in 47 of 4996 (0.94%) in the rivaroxaban group; a primary safety outcome event occurred in 177 (2.91%), 142 (3.36%), and 174 (3.48%), respectively. In pairwise comparisons, 6-month risks of a primary effectiveness outcome event were 1.24% and 0.94% for aspirin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.30 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.20 to 0.81); 1.24% and 1.01% for aspirin versus warfarin (difference, 0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.34 to 0.81); and 1.13% and 1.10% for warfarin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.57 to 0.63). Risks of a primary safety outcome event were 3.70% and 3.02% for rivaroxaban versus aspirin (difference, 0.68 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.41); 3.65% and 2.88% for warfarin versus aspirin (difference, 0.77 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.58); and 3.59% and 3.61% for rivaroxaban versus warfarin (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.89 to 0.85). Intention-to-treat analyses yielded similar results.

CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin with respect to death or symptomatic VTE. Warfarin and rivaroxaban were not noninferior to aspirin for safety. (Funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; PEPPER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02810704.).

title: Analysis of fatigue change trajsectories and postoperative cerebral dysfunction factors in acute type A aortic dissection patients.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To identify distinct fatigue trajectories during the acute phase using latent class growth modelling and to investigate risk factors for postoperative cerebral dysfunction (POCD) in acute type A aortic dissection patients.

METHODS: A prospective analysis of patients who underwent acute type A aortic dissection (AAAD) surgery at Fujian Heart Medical Center from December 2023 to December 2024 was conducted. The odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence interval were calculated by unconditional regression analysis to determine the independent risk factors for POCD.

RESULTS: A total of 383 patients were included in this study. Among these patients, 174 (45.4%) experienced postoperative cognitive dysfunction. On the basis of the changes in the fatigue level of patients after AAAD, three potential categories of tracks were determined: the low-fatigue group (n = 85), the increasing-fatigue group (n = 259) and the severe-fatigue group (n = 39). Among them, 10.2% of AAAD patients had a continuous high fatigue level track. With the increasing-fatigue group as the control, regression analysis revealed that the risk of POCD increased in the severe-fatigue group (OR = 2.454, P < 0.05) and the group with a cumulative duration of rcSO2 < 50% and > 15 s (OR = 3.595, P < 0.05). Moreover, age (OR = 1.063, P < 0.001), BMI (OR = 1.138, P < 0.05), hypertension (OR = 3.697, P < 0.05) and arterial blood lactate level (OR = 1.093, P < 0.05) were independent risk factors for POCD after AAAD.

CONCLUSION: Persistent high fatigue levels may be related to POCD in AAAD patients. In clinical work, it is necessary to pay attention to elderly and obese patients, patients with high arterial blood lactate values, and particularly patients with persistently abnormal fatigue levels, and to provide preventative medical and nursing interventions as soon as possible.

METHODS: A prospective analysis of patients who underwent acute type A aortic dissection (AAAD) surgery at Fujian Heart Medical Center from December 2023 to December 2024 was conducted. The odds ratio (OR) and 95% confidence interval were calculated by unconditional regression analysis to determine the independent risk factors for POCD.

title: Multi-Structure Segmentation of Type B Aortic Dissection from CT Images with U-Net.
abstract: Type B aortic dissection (TBAD) is a life-threatening condition in which a tear in the intimal layer separates the aortic wall into a true and a false lumen. Assessment of the lumen, the intimal flap, and false-lumen thrombosis from CT images is important for risk analysis and treatment planning. This work applied U-Net-based deep neural networks to the automatic segmentation of these structures in TBAD. We collected 46 CT scans from 20 patients, with voxel-wise annotations of three structures: the aortic lumen, the intimal flap, and the thrombus. We explored four models: two convolutional networks, nnU-Net (2D and 3D), and two transformer-based architectures, TransUNet (2D and 3D). We observed that (1) for both nnU-Net and TransUNet, the 3D models outperformed their 2D counterparts on all three structures. The difference was small for the aortic lumen but large for the thin flap and the thrombus. The best model, nnU-Net 3D, reached a DSC of 93.05% for the lumen, 50.22% for the flap, and 69.94% for the thrombus. (2) The intimal flap was the most difficult structure for all models. Even the best 3D models showed large thrombus boundary errors in a few scans. These results provide a baseline for developing more advanced models for accurate segmentation of these structures in TBAD.

title: Efficacy and safety of endovascular mechanical thrombectomy for cerebral venous sinus thrombosis: meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) is an uncommon yet potentially disabling cause of stroke that predominantly affects young adults. Anticoagulation remains the cornerstone of treatment; however, a subset of patients experience clinical deterioration despite adequate anticoagulation. Consequently, endovascular mechanical thrombectomy (EMT) has been introduced for high-risk or refractory cases, though its efficacy and safety remain controversial.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Europe PMC were systematically searched to identify studies comparing EMT with anticoagulation or alternative endovascular treatment in patients with CVST; the database searches covered eligible studies through May 2026. Mortality was designated as the primary outcome; mRS ≤ 2, recurrence, and complications were secondary outcomes. Odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects (DerSimonian-Laird) models. Sensitivity, subgroup, and publication-bias analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Overall, 19 studies were included (18 non-randomized and one randomized). EMT was associated with increased odds of mortality in the primary model (12 studies; OR 1.67; 95% CI 1.09-2.56; p = 0.019; I 2 = 6.7%); however, this association was not robust on leave-one-out analysis, and a sensitivity analysis additionally including a National Inpatient Sample administrative-database study yielded an OR of 1.96 (13 studies; 95% CI 1.20-3.22). EMT had no significant effect on mRS ≤ 2 (14 studies; OR 0.83; 95% CI 0.37-1.85; p = 0.650), recurrence (6 studies; OR 0.80; 95% CI 0.33-1.89; p = 0.605), or complications (10 studies; OR 1.20; 95% CI 0.55-2.64; p = 0.643).

CONCLUSION: Since EMT is preferentially applied to the most severely affected patients, the observed association between EMT and mortality may substantially reflect confounding by indication and should not be interpreted as evidence of procedural harm. Randomized trials are needed to define the role of EMT in CVST.

title: Indirect versus combined bypass for perfusion-defined high-risk adult moyamoya disease: a propensity score overlap-weighted analysis of revascularization and postoperative stroke.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Adult patients with moyamoya disease (MMD) and extensive preoperative perfusion delay may be at increased risk for postoperative stroke after combined bypass (CB). We compared indirect bypass (IB) and CB in a perfusion-defined high-risk adult MMD cohort.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed adult MMD hemispheres treated with CB or IB between January 2019 and December 2024. The cohort wasrestricted to hemispheres with a preoperative tissue volume of at least 59.5 mL showing time-to-maximum (Tmax) >6 seconds (6s). Revascularization was assessed by 6-month angiography using the Matsushima grading system, and perfusion improvement was evaluated using postoperative CT perfusion. Baseline imbalance was addressed using overlap-weighted propensity score analysis. Factors associated with postoperative stroke were evaluated using overlap-weighted logistic regression, with sensitivity analyses using patient-clustered robust standard errors and Firth penalized logistic regression.

RESULTS: A total of 124 hemispheres were analyzed (CB, 88; IB, 36). Before weighting, PCA involvement was more frequent in the IB group (86.1% vs. 61.4%; standardized mean difference = 0.586), but all prespecified covariates were balanced after overlap weighting. Good revascularization was comparable between CB and IB before weighting (93.2% vs. 94.4%, p = 1.000) and after overlap weighting (90.6% vs. 98.1%, p = 0.102). Postoperative perfusion outcomes were also similar. Postoperative stroke occurred less frequently after IB both before weighting (5.6% vs. 23.9%, p = 0.021) and after overlap weighting (5.2% vs. 34.6%, p < 0.001). In the overlap-weighted multivariable model, IB was associated with lower odds of postoperative stroke, whereas larger preoperative Tmax>6s volume was associated with higher odds. These findings remained significant after adjustment for intra-patient correlation and were directionally consistent in Firth analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: In this perfusion-defined high-risk adult MMD cohort, IB achieved angiographic and perfusion outcomes comparable to CB, with a lower observed postoperative stroke. IB may be a reasonable risk-adapted option for selected high-risk hemispheres, although non-randomized treatment allocation warrants cautious interpretation.

We compared indirect bypass (IB) and CB in a perfusion-defined high-risk adult MMD cohort. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed adult MMD hemispheres treated with CB or IB between January 2019 and December 2024.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Endovascular Treatment Methods in Patients with Aortoiliac Lesions of Moderate and High Cardiovascular Perioperative Risk.
abstract: Objective. Comparative evaluation of efficacy and safety of the kissing-stent technique and covered endovascular reconstruction of the aortic bifurcation (CERAB) in patients with aortoiliac lesions of moderate and high cardiovascular perioperative risk. Material and Methods. A total of 105 patients with hemodynamically significant aortoiliac atherosclerotic lesions of moderate and high cardiovascular perioperative risk were included in this ambispective cohort study. The Duke Activity Status Index (DASI) and the Gupta MICA scale (Gupta Perioperative Risk for Myocardial Infarction or Cardiac Arrest) were used to assess cardiovascular perioperative risk. III stage chronic lower limb ischemia according to Fontaine-Pokrovsky classification was observed in 84 patients (80.0%) and stage IV in 21 patients (20.0%). A total of 66 patients (62.9%) had infrarenal aortic occlusion. A total of 49 patients underwent CERAB, and 56 patients underwent kissing-stent treatment with bare-metal stents. The severity of calcification in the aortoiliac segment was assessed using the PACSS (Peripheral Arterial Calcium Scoring System) based on computed tomography data. Primary endpoint included primary patency. Secondary endpoint included technical success, operation time, intraoperative blood volume loss, adverse cardiovascular events (local and systemic complications, cardiovascular mortality) in the early postoperative period, intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, hospital length of stay, long-term postoperative complications, secondary patency, freedom from amputation, and survival rate. Results. The median follow-up duration was 48.0 [interquartile range (IQR) 33.0; 54.0] months. The median operation time was 73.5 [IQR 60.0; 100.0] minutes in the CERAB group and 67.5 [IQR 45.0; 95.0] minutes in the kissing-stent group (p = 0.723). The median intraoperative blood volume loss was 80.5 [IQR 75.4; 110.0] mL in the CERAB group and 81.4 [IQR 68.2; 105.0] mL in the kissing-stent group (p = 0.865). Technical success was 98.0% in the CERAB group and 92.9% in the kissing-stent group (p = 0.369). The median ICU length of stay was 1.54 [IQR 1.0; 2.0] days in the CERAB group and 1.67 [IQR 1.0; 2.0] days in the kissing-stent group (p = 0.968). The median hospital length of stay was 5.0 [IQR 4.0; 7.0] days in the CERAB group and 6.4 [IQR 4.5; 7.8] days in the kissing-stent group (p = 0.744). In the early postoperative period, complications occurred in three patients (6.1%) from the CERAB group and in five patients (8.9%) from the kissing-stent group (p = 0.721). In the long-term postoperative period, complications occurred in one patient (2.0%) from the CERAB group and in two patients (3.6%) from the kissing-stent group (p = 1.000). Primary patency at 60 months was 85.1% in the CERAB group and 59.4% in the kissing-stent group (p = 0.047). Secondary patency at 60 months was 92.9% in the CERAB group and 91.3% in the kissing-stent group (p = 0.883). Freedom from amputation at 60 months was 95.4% in the CERAB group and 93.3% in the kissing-stent group (p = 0.985). Survival rate at 60 months was 95.7% in the CERAB group and 96.0% in the kissing-stent group (p = 0.772). Predictors of loss of primary patency of the aortoiliac segment after kissing stent included grade 3-4 calcification according to the PACSS, the presence of thrombotic masses in the lumen of the infrarenal aorta, and hemodynamically significant damage to the outflow arteries. Conclusions. The results of this study demonstrated the advantage of CERAB over kissing-stent technique in terms of five-year primary patency with comparable safety. The predictors of loss of primary patency after kissing-stent treatment identified in this study indicate the need for more careful patient selection and a personalised approach to treatment selection.
