title: Feasibility of patient-specific 3D-printed fragment models for preoperative planning in bicondylar tibial plateau fractures: a retrospective case series.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Schatzker type V and VI tibial plateau fractures have complex three-dimensional patterns that complicate surgical planning and coronal alignment restoration. This study assessed the feasibility of patient-specific 3D-printed fragment models for planning combined medial and lateral approaches and described radiographic and functional outcomes.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 22 patients with Schatzker type V or VI fractures treated at Foshan Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine from January 2023 to July 2024. Preoperative CT data enabled fragment segmentation, color coding, virtual reduction, and fabrication of patient-specific physical models. Posterior tibial slope, medial proximal tibial angle, articular depression, and tibial plateau width were compared pre- and postoperatively. Rasmussen functional and radiological scores and Knee Society Scores were assessed at 3 and 6 months, 1 year, and final follow-up; complications were recorded.

RESULTS: All 22 patients completed follow-up (mean, 30.73 ± 3.20 months). A mean of 24.41 ± 2.26 tibial fragments were identified and segmented per patient. Mean articular depression decreased from 6.70 ± 3.07 to 1.74 ± 0.48 mm. Posterior tibial slope, medial proximal tibial angle, and tibial plateau width improved significantly after surgery (all P < 0.001). Mean postoperative coronal alignment was within the predefined normal range in both preoperative varus and valgus subgroups. All three scores differed significantly across follow-up (all P < 0.001). At final follow-up, mean Rasmussen functional and Knee Society Scores were 27.18 ± 1.84 and 87.55 ± 4.92, respectively, with excellent-or-good rates of 100% and 95.45%. Mild post-traumatic knee osteoarthritis, superficial infection, and deep-vein thrombosis occurred in 5, 1, and 2 patients, respectively. No secondary varus or valgus deformity was observed.

CONCLUSIONS: In complex bicondylar tibial plateau fractures, patient-specific 3D-printed fragment models provided a practical three-dimensional reference for fragment identification, reduction sequencing, and planning of combined medial and lateral approaches. Satisfactory articular reduction, maintenance of proximal tibial coronal alignment, and favorable functional outcomes at final follow-up were observed in this cohort. These findings support the feasibility of incorporating 3D-printed fragment models into preoperative planning for these fractures.

This study assessed the feasibility of patient-specific 3D-printed fragment models for planning combined medial and lateral approaches and described radiographic and functional outcomes. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 22 patients with Schatzker type V or VI fractures treated at Foshan Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine from January 2023 to July 2024.

title: Prognostic Impact of Paravalvular Regurgitation in Patients With Severe Low-Flow, Low-Gradient Aortic Stenosis Undergoing TAVR.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Paravalvular regurgitation (PVR) is a frequent complication after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) and may influence clinical outcomes in patients with high-gradient aortic stenosis. However, its prognostic relevance in patients with low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (LFLG-AS) undergoing TAVR remains incompletely elucidated.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the prognostic significance of PVR severity in patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR with current-generation prostheses.

METHODS: This multicenter registry-based cohort study included consecutive patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR from January 2019 to December 2024 at 17 high-volume Italian centers. PVR severity was classified using a 5-class grading scheme and stratified as <2+ (none/trace or mild) or ≥2+ (mild-moderate or worse) based on separation of Kaplan-Meier curves for the primary outcome. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death and heart failure hospitalization up to 2 years. Propensity score-weighted Cox regression was used to estimate the independent impact of PVR severity on clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: A total of 1,358 patients were included. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed lower event-free survival among patients with ≥2+ PVR at discharge compared with those with <2+ PVR. After propensity score weighting, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with a higher risk of the primary endpoint (adjusted HR: 3.77; 95% CI: 2.88-4.95), as well as higher risks of all-cause death, mainly cardiovascular, and heart failure hospitalization. These findings were consistent across both classical and paradoxical LFLG-AS phenotypes.

CONCLUSIONS: In this large, real-world study of patients with LFLG-AS treated with current-generation TAVR devices, PVR ≥2+ was independently associated with worse clinical outcomes after discharge, regardless of LFLG-AS subtype.

However, its prognostic relevance in patients with low-flow, low-gradient aortic stenosis (LFLG-AS) undergoing TAVR remains incompletely elucidated. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate the prognostic significance of PVR severity in patients with LFLG-AS undergoing TAVR with current-generation prostheses.

title: Association between nasogastric tube placement and self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms in patients receiving endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion: A post-hoc analysis of the ENCHANTED2/MT trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-stroke anxiety and depression are common after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large vessel occlusion (LVO) and impair long-term recovery. Nasogastric tube (NGT) placement marks severe dysphagia and illness, but its association with anxiety or depression remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether NGT placement is associated with the presence and severity of 90-day self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms after successful EVT.

METHODS: We performed a post-hoc analysis of the ENCHANTED2/MT multicentre randomized controlled trial, including patients with anterior-circulation LVO who achieved successful reperfusion and had complete 90-day EQ-5D-3 L data. Participants were stratified by in-hospital NGT placement (No-NGT group vs. NGT group). The primary outcome was self-reported anxiety/depression assessed by the EQ-5D-3 L dimension (no, moderate, or extreme symptoms). We explored the association between NGT placement and the proportion and severity of self-reported anxiety/depression using propensity score matching (PSM) and logistic regression, and performed exploratory subgroup analyses.

RESULTS: Of 575 patients, 280(48.7%) received an NGT. Before matching, the proportion reporting self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms was 38.6% in the NGT group versus 15.6% in the no-NGT group (unadjusted OR3.40, 95%CI 2.30-5.09). After adjustment for measured clinical covariates, the association remained significant (adjusted OR2.97, 95%CI 1.93-4.63; ordinal OR3.06, 95%CI 1.99-4.77). After PSM, 175 patients were matched in each group; NGT placement remained associated with higher odds of self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms (37.7% vs 21.1%; OR2.26, 95%CI 1.41-3.65; ordinal OR2.25, 95%CI 1.41-3.63). In exploratory subgroup analyses, the association appeared more pronounced in patients with admission NIHSS ≤ 15 (OR3.83, 95% CI1.82-8.07; P for interaction = 0.049).

CONCLUSION: In this post-hoc analysis, NGT placement was associated with higher odds of self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms.NGT requirement may identify patients who deserve closer psychological assessment.

Nasogastric tube (NGT) placement marks severe dysphagia and illness, but its association with anxiety or depression remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether NGT placement is associated with the presence and severity of 90-day self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms after successful EVT.

title: Filter-Free Retrograde Popliteal JETSTREAM Atherectomy Followed by Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty: Procedural Safety and One-Year Clinical and Hemodynamic Outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular revascularization is an established treatment for symptomatic femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease. Drug-coated balloon angioplasty allows antiproliferative drug delivery without permanent metallic implantation, while atherectomy may facilitate lesion preparation in calcified and occlusive disease. This study evaluated the procedural safety and one-year clinical and hemodynamic outcomes of filter-free retrograde popliteal JETSTREAM atherectomy followed by drug-coated balloon angioplasty, with additional assessment of dual antiplatelet therapy adherence and continued smoking.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center study evaluated 128 patients treated with filter-free retrograde popliteal JETSTREAM atherectomy followed by Ranger drug-coated balloon angioplasty. Of these, 107 completed 24 h observation and standardized 12-month follow-up; 21 were discharged before completing 24 h and had incomplete longitudinal assessments. Clinical and hemodynamic outcomes were assessed in 107 patients. Exploratory comparisons according to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) adherence and smoking status were performed, including a baseline-adjusted analysis of 12-month ankle-brachial index (ABI).

RESULTS: In the 107-patient longitudinal cohort, mean age was 67.0 ± 6.9 years, 45.8% had total occlusions, 83.2% had Peripheral Arterial Calcium Scoring System (PACSS) grade 4 calcification, and 21.5% required adjunctive stenting. Final technical success was achieved in all 128 treated patients (128/128, 100%). No clinically evident distal embolization was documented in the 107 patients completing 24-h observation (0/107; upper two-sided 95% exact confidence limit, approximately 3.4%). No complications were documented before discharge among the 21 patients with incomplete 24-h observation. At one year, median ABI increased from 0.59 to 1.20, and mean Rutherford category improved from 4.16 to 1.64. In exploratory multivariable analysis, DAPT adherence was associated with higher 12-month ABI (adjusted β = 0.321; 95% CI, 0.214-0.427), whereas continued smoking was not statistically significant after adjustment (β = -0.065; 95% CI, -0.146 to 0.016).

CONCLUSIONS: Substantial one-year clinical and hemodynamic improvements were observed in this selected cohort. Incomplete 24-h safety ascertainment in early-discharge patients and the lack of a comparator group preclude conclusions about the comparative safety of omitting embolic protection. Associations with DAPT adherence and smoking are exploratory and do not establish causality or an optimal DAPT duration.

Drug-coated balloon angioplasty allows antiproliferative drug delivery without permanent metallic implantation, while atherectomy may facilitate lesion preparation in calcified and occlusive disease. This study evaluated the procedural safety and one-year clinical and hemodynamic outcomes of filter-free retrograde popliteal JETSTREAM atherectomy followed by drug-coated balloon angioplasty, with additional assessment of dual antiplatelet therapy adherence and continued smoking.

title: Identification of the Nature of Acute Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion and Preferred Strategy for Mechanical Thrombectomy.
abstract: Acute middle cerebral artery occlusion is a common and critical cerebrovascular disease in clinical practice, characterized by its sudden onset and severe clinical symptoms, posing a substantial threat to neurological function and survival. Therefore, clinicians need to quickly and accurately identify the occlusion type and develop appropriate treatment plans accordingly. In recent years, with the development of neuroimaging technology and a deeper understanding of the pathophysiological mechanisms of acute middle cerebral artery occlusion, various diagnostic methods have been applied to determine the occlusion type. The core treatment goal of acute ischemic stroke is to minimize irreversible neuronal injury and restore effective brain tissue perfusion as soon as possible. Systematic reviews and meta-analyses of multiple randomized controlled trials have consistently confirmed that mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has significant clinical efficacy in acute anterior circulation stroke patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO). Therefore, domestic and international evidence-based guidelines list it as a first-line endovascular intervention for LVO stroke in the early stage of onset (within 6 h; expandable to 24 h with imaging screening). This narrative review summarizes current evidence on diagnostic approaches for different types of acute middle cerebral artery occlusion and mechanical thrombectomy strategies tailored to the presumed occlusion mechanism, with the aim of informing mechanism-based diagnostic assessment and endovascular treatment decisions.

title: Digital Twin-Based Risk Stratification Integrating Aortic Shape and Wall Mechanics in Acute Uncomplicated Type B Aortic Dissection.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study evaluated whether patient-specific digital twins integrating 3D aortic anatomy and structural wall stress could identify patients with acute uncomplicated type B aortic dissection (AUTBAD) at high risk for adverse aortic events.

METHODS: We analyzed CTAs from 50 patients extracted from a 400 AUTBAD patient database treated with optimal medical therapy from 1999-2025. Digital twin models were constructed, and statistical shape modeling and reduced-order fluid-structure interaction analysis were performed. Anatomic shape and biomechanical stress data were integrated into models predicting freedom from aortic events, defined as intervention or aortic-related death, using leave-one-out cross-validation. A cross-validated risk score was generated for each patient, with higher scores indicating higher event risk.

RESULTS: At diagnosis, the median descending aortic diameter was 40.61 mm. During follow-up, 35 patients experienced an aortic event: 28 interventions (56%) and 7 aortic-related deaths (14%). Stratification by descending aortic diameter above or below 40.61 mm yielded higher-versus lower-risk aortic event-free survival of 72.0% versus 84.0% at 1 year and 27.8% versus 56.7% at 6 years (p=0.035; C-index=0.590). In the cross-validated multidimensional model combining morphology and structural stress, higher-versus lower-risk event-free survival was 60.0% versus 96.0% at 1 year and 12.5% versus 68.9% at 6 years (p<0.001; C-index=0.792).

CONCLUSIONS: Digital twin modeling integrating morphology and wall stress provided greater risk separation than univariable predictors in AUTBAD patients. With independent validation, patient-specific AUTBAD risk stratification using geometric and biomechanical data may ultimately contribute to identification of high-risk patients who may benefit from early endovascular repair.

CENTRAL PICTURE: Multidimensional digital twin model stratifies aortic event-free survival in AUTBAD.

CENTRAL MESSAGE: Combining patient-specific 3D aortic morphology and wall stress may improve identification of medically managed AUTBAD patients at high risk for aortic intervention or aortic-related death.

PERSPECTIVE: TBAD geometry is highly patient specific, and one-dimensional measurements may not fully reflect patient risk. Digital twin modeling incorporating 3D morphology and wall mechanics may provide a more complete basis for risk stratification. This study demonstrates the feasibility of integrating multidimensional shape and stress data into a risk-stratification model to identify high-risk AUTBAD patients.

METHODS: We analyzed CTAs from 50 patients extracted from a 400 AUTBAD patient database treated with optimal medical therapy from 1999-2025. Digital twin models were constructed, and statistical shape modeling and reduced-order fluid-structure interaction analysis were performed.

title: Endovascular therapy for cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas: a single-center retrospective study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the clinical efficacy of endovascular therapy for cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas (CSDAVFs).

METHODS: A single-center, retrospective cohort study was conducted involving patients with CSDAVFs who underwent endovascular therapy performed by a single neurointerventionalist at West China Hospital, Sichuan University, between January 2023 and December 2025. Data collected included demographic characteristics, presenting symptoms and neurological signs, baseline and follow-up imaging findings (including digital subtraction angiography), procedural details (e.g., access route, embolic agents, technical success), and clinical outcomes-including angiographic occlusion status, symptom resolution, procedure-related complications, and functional recovery.

RESULTS: Fourteen patients were diagnosed with cavernous sinus dural arteriovenous fistulas (CSDAVFs). Twelve underwent endovascular treatment following definitive diagnosis by digital subtraction angiography (DSA); two declined intervention despite confirmed diagnosis. Thirteen presented with predominant ocular manifestations-such as proptosis, chemosis, and ophthalmoparesis-while one was diagnosed incidentally on cranial MRI performed for headache and dizziness. All 12 patients underwent the procedure successfully: seven underwent arterial-access embolization and five underwent venous-access embolization. Onyx liquid embolic agent was used as the sole embolic material in seven cases; in the remaining five cases, detachable coils were employed as adjunctive agents. Immediate post-procedural DSA demonstrated complete occlusion in nine patients and subtotal occlusion in three. Procedure-related complications occurred in five patients: visual acuity reduction (n = 2), ipsilateral facial hypoesthesia (n = 2), and isolated impairment of abduction and downward gaze (n = 1). Symptomatic improvement was observed in seven patients. At 1-year clinical and imaging follow-up, all 12 treated patients remained under surveillance. Ten exhibited no recurrence; notably, one patient with initial subtotal occlusion achieved complete angiographic occlusion during follow-up. In the remaining two, residual lesions remained stable in size, symptoms improved, and no secondary intervention was required. Among the five patients with procedure-related complications, two developed persistent facial hypoesthesia after intra-arterial embolization; subjective numbness gradually improved but did not fully resolve during follow-up.

CONCLUSION: Endovascular therapy for craniospinal dural arteriovenous fistula (CSDAVFs) is associated with favorable clinical and angiographic outcomes. Although procedure-related complications occur in a subset of patients, most are transient and resolve spontaneously or improve to partial remission during follow-up. Collectively, these findings support endovascular therapy as a safe and effective treatment modality for CSDAVFs.

title: Association between the triglyceride-glucose index and clinical outcomes in acute atherosclerotic ischaemic stroke patients following endovascular thrombectomy: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to investigate the association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and unfavourable clinical outcomes in patients with atherosclerotic acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT).

METHODS: Patients with AIS who underwent EVT between January 2019 and September 2024 were enrolled. The primary outcome was an unfavourable functional outcome at three months (modified Rankin Scale score 3-6); secondary outcomes were symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage (sICH) and all-cause mortality at three months. The TyG index was analysed continuously and in quartiles by logistic regression, restricted cubic splines and receiver operating characteristic curves.

RESULTS: Among 670 patients, 269 (40.1%) had an unfavourable functional outcome at three months, 91 (13.6%) died at three months for all-cause, and 85 (12.7%) developed sICH. Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest TyG quartile was independently associated with unfavourable functional outcome (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.91, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-3.56) and mortality (aOR 5.15, 95% CI 2.06-12.86). The overall spline association was significant for all endpoints; only mortality was non-linear (P = 0.032), with risk rising above a TyG index of approximately 8.9. Discrimination was modest, with area under the curve (AUC) values of 0.583 for unfavourable functional outcome and 0.612 for mortality. No significant interactions were found across prespecified subgroups, except for blood glucose level.

CONCLUSION: An elevated TyG index is independently associated with three-month unfavourable functional outcome, mortality and sICH after EVT, and may aid prognostic risk stratification, although further validation is required based on the existing predictive indicators.

The primary outcome was an unfavourable functional outcome at three months (modified Rankin Scale score 3-6); secondary outcomes were symptomatic intracerebral haemorrhage (sICH) and all-cause mortality at three months.

title: Noninvasive electrical impedance tomography monitoring during total aortic arch replacement: incremental value for prediction of postoperative neurological deficit.
abstract: Introduction: Postoperative neurological deficit (ND) after total aortic arch replacement (TAAR) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, with limited effective preventive therapies available. Intraoperative neuromonitoring plays a critical role in reducing postoperative ND. This prospective cohort study aimed to investigate the prognostic value of electrical impedance tomography (EIT) and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) for predicting postoperative ND in patients undergoing TAAR. Methods: A 16-electrode EIT system and NIRS were utilized for intraoperative cerebral neuromonitoring during TAAR. Correlations between intraoperative EIT and NIRS variables and postoperative ND were comprehensively analyzed. Results: The overall incidence of postoperative ND was 39.1% (59/151), including a 15.2% incidence of postoperative stroke. The time integral of absolute resistivity asymmetry index during hypothermic circulatory arrest (TRAIHCA), the maximum absolute resistivity asymmetry ratio during HCA (MRARHCA), age, body mass index, supra-aortic branch involvement, and operative duration were independent predictors of postoperative ND. Incorporation of EIT parameters into the clinical prediction model significantly improved the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve from 0.752 to 0.817 (P = 0.027). Moreover, the incremental prognostic value of EIT was further validated by improved risk reclassification and discriminatory ability for ND, with a net reclassification index of 0.510 (P = 0.002) and an integrated discrimination improvement of 0.072 (P < 0.001). Conclusion: The EIT parameters have been demonstrated to be an effective means of predicting ND following TAAR. Cerebral EIT may represent a potential alternative for intraoperative noninvasive multimodal neuromonitoring options.

title: Intraoperative measurement of the ascending aortic diameter at the onset of aortic dissection.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although prior studies have associated aortic size with dissection risk, none have corrected for dissection-related aortic expansion. This study aimed to establish a measurement approach to determine the ascending aortic diameter before dissection.

METHODS: The samples of dissected ascending aortas were obtained from 36 patients at the time of their operation. In this study, the intimal lumen diameter measured at its maximal stretching state was used as a reliable surrogate for the pre-dissection aortic diameter. Subsequently, the relationship between this surrogate and the aortic diameter measured on post-dissection CT at the corresponding levels was further analyzed.

RESULTS: Using this method, the pre-dissection ascending aortic diameter was measured as 37.5 ± 6.6 mm, whereas the post-dissection CT measurement at the same level increased to 43.9 ± 7.0 mm. After excluding patients with non-A-non-B aortic dissection, the mean ascending aortic diameter increased by approximately 20% after dissection compared with the pre-dissection value, corresponding to an absolute increase of 7.5 mm in diameter.

CONCLUSIONS: Although aortic diameter remains a robust indicator for prophylactic surgery in the study population, acute aortic dissection is seldom associated with true ascending aortic aneurysms and occurs with normal or near-normal aortic dimensions in most patients. When dissection occurs in the setting of a small aortic diameter, it likely reflects a profound functional vulnerability of the aortic tissue to catastrophic aortic events.

This study aimed to establish a measurement approach to determine the ascending aortic diameter before dissection. METHODS: The samples of dissected ascending aortas were obtained from 36 patients at the time of their operation.

title: Oral anticoagulants and the risk of acute kidney injury: a retrospective real-world cohort study using overlap propensity score weighting.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anticoagulant-related nephropathy, initially described in association with warfarin, has increasingly been reported with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs). However, the comparative risk of acute kidney injury (AKI) within 30 days of treatment initiation between warfarin and DOACs across a broad spectrum of clinical indications remains unclear.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients newly initiated on DOACs or warfarin between January 2014 and May 2025 at the Third Xiangya Hospital of Central South University. Overlap propensity score weighting, with weights derived from a generalized boosted model incorporating 81 baseline covariates, balanced the treatment groups. Weighted logistic regression compared the risk of AKI within 30 days of OAC initiation, defined by KDIGO criteria. Sensitivity analyses included inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) and logistic regression-derived overlap weighting, each with or without doubly robust covariate adjustment.

RESULTS: Among 6 876 patients (5 048 DOAC users; 1 828 warfarin users), DOAC initiation was associated with a higher risk of AKI than warfarin after overlap weighting (OR: 1.346, 95% CI: 1.057-1.715; p = 0.016), and with severe AKI (stage 2-3; OR: 1.694, 95% CI: 1.013-2.832; p = 0.044), whereas stage 1 AKI did not differ significantly. The association persisted after additional covariate adjustment (OR: 1.363, 95% CI: 1.068-1.740; p = 0.013) and across alternative propensity score models, although the unadjusted IPTW model did not. By indication, the association was significant for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation (AF) (OR: 1.566, 95% CI: 1.034-2.369; p = 0.034) but not for venous thromboembolism (VTE) treatment or prophylaxis. Among individual DOACs, rivaroxaban was associated with an elevated risk (OR: 1.392, 95% CI: 1.075-1.804; p = 0.012), whereas edoxaban, dabigatran, and apixaban were not. Lower-dose rivaroxaban initiation was associated with an increased risk (OR: 2.792, 95% CI: 1.524-5.114; p = 0.001), whereas higher-dose and off-label use were not. In prespecified subgroup analyses, ORs were above 1 in most strata, but most comparisons were not significant, and no significant interactions were detected.

CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that DOACs, particularly rivaroxaban, may be associated with a higher short-term risk of AKI than warfarin. Given the expanding use of DOACs, medication-specific renal effects warrant further investigation, and close monitoring of renal function may be advisable in high-risk patients after anticoagulation initiation.

However, the comparative risk of acute kidney injury (AKI) within 30 days of treatment initiation between warfarin and DOACs across a broad spectrum of clinical indications remains unclear. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients newly initiated on DOACs or warfarin between January 2014 and May 2025 at the Third Xiangya Hospital of Central South University.

title: Molecular, genetic, and pharmacogenomic biomarkers of Type B aortic dissection risk in Marfan syndrome: a scoping review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Marfan syndrome is an autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder caused primarily by pathogenic FBN1 variants, with aortic dissection a leading cause of mortality. Improved surgical thresholds have reduced Type A dissection mortality, but Type B dissection remains poorly predicted. This review maps current human evidence on molecular, genetic, and pharmacogenomic biomarkers for Type B aortic dissection risk stratification in Marfan syndrome and identifies gaps that inform a future research agenda.

METHODS: A scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) and the framework of Arksey and O'Malley. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for articles published between January 2010 and October 2025. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and scored each study for evidence certainty across six domains.

RESULTS: Twenty-four studies met criteria, derived from 14 independent source populations; eight came from a single Dutch cohort network. Only two studies reported Type B dissection as a specified outcome; the remainder addressed dissection of unspecified type, aortic diameter or growth, or mechanistic endpoints. Four thematic evidence streams emerged. TGF-β pathway biomarkers show associations with aortic phenotype and disease severity across several cohorts, but their value for prospective prediction of Type B dissection remains unvalidated. Variants in TGFBR2 and TGFB2, and FBN1 cysteine-loss variants, are associated with severe aortic phenotypes yet are not integrated into the Ghent nosology. Losartan shows heterogeneous efficacy, and a predefined randomized trial substudy suggests that benefit may depend on FBN1 variant class, although no trial has stratified outcomes by dissection type. No tool exists to stratify Type B risk in the 5 to 10 percent of clinically diagnosed patients without an identifiable FBN1 variant. Evidence certainty was moderate for the pharmacologic stream and low to very low for the other three, and the biomarker evidence is associational rather than causal.

CONCLUSIONS: A competing-risks multimodal model integrating imaging, genotype, and treatment-adjusted biomarker trajectory, developed and externally validated in multicentre prospective cohorts, represents the next research frontier.

Improved surgical thresholds have reduced Type A dissection mortality, but Type B dissection remains poorly predicted. This review maps current human evidence on molecular, genetic, and pharmacogenomic biomarkers for Type B aortic dissection risk stratification in Marfan syndrome and identifies gaps that inform a future research agenda.

title: Application of endovascular stent graft in ABO-incompatible living donor kidney transplantation: a case report.
abstract: Severe iliac arteriosclerosis is a contraindication for kidney transplantation (KT). This report details a case of a 34-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus and severe iliac arteriosclerosis who underwent ABO-incompatible living donor KT in which the renal graft artery was anastomosed to the self-expandable endovascular covered stent placed in the external iliac artery. The initial anti-blood group anti-A antibody titers were 1:4 and 1:32 for IgG and IgM, respectively. Routine pre-transplant therapy including rituximab 200mg, triple immunosuppressants included tacrolimus (7mg/d, tacrolimus concentration was between 3.8 and 9.2 ng/mL), mycophenolate mofetil (1500mg/d), methylprednisolone (16mg/d). Following one session of double filtration plasmapheresis, anti-blood group antibody titers were reduced 1:4 and 1:8 for IgG and IgM. Two days prior to surgery, patient underwent one session of plasma exchange and antibody titers were IgG 1:4 and IgM 1:8 on the day of KT. Basiliximab was administered for immune induction. The initial routine was performed with conventional end-to-side anastomosis between the renal graft artery and the right external iliac artery. However, pulsation of the transplant renal artery disappeared shortly. Upon opening the anastomosis, thrombosis at the anastomotic site was identified due to plaque embolism from the external iliac artery. Consequently, a self-expandable endovascular covered stent was implanted into the external iliac artery via the right femoral artery under intervention. Because part of the external iliac artery wall was defective, the endovascular stent was partially exposed, used the prosthetic graft for coverage and reinforcement. Finally, the renal allograft artery was anastomosed end-to-side to the stent-prosthetic complex. The anti-blood group antibody titers were 1:2 and 1:4 for IgG and IgM and serum creatinine was 124 μmol/L at 1 month. During the 2 years follow-up, graft function remained satisfactory, the serum creatinine levels were 116, 107, and 113 μmol/L at 6 months, 1 year, and 2 years postoperatively, and no signs of right lower limb ischemia were evident. This study demonstrates that renal graft implanted on the endovascular stent is a feasible therapeutic option for recipients with severe iliac arteriosclerosis.

This report details a case of a 34-year-old female with type 2 diabetes mellitus and severe iliac arteriosclerosis who underwent ABO-incompatible living donor KT in which the renal graft artery was anastomosed to the self-expandable endovascular covered stent placed in the external iliac artery. The initial anti-blood group anti-A antibody titers were 1:4 and 1:32 for IgG and IgM, respectively.

title: Genetic-multi-omics causal inference coupled with integrative in-vitro toxicology reveals immune-metabolite mediators for aortic aneurysm risk.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Aortic aneurysm (AA) is a life-threatening vascular disease characterized by immune disturbance and metabolic dysregulation. Multi-omics-driven precision toxicity prediction, integrating human genetic causal inference with functional in-vitro toxicology, remains under-explored for uncovering metabolite mediators underlying AA disease risk.This study aimed to dissect metabolite-dependent causal pathways linking immune cells to AA, and evaluate dose-response cytotoxicity of key mediating metabolites toward vascular cells.

METHODS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and two-step mediation analysis were performed using European-ancestry GWAS summary datasets covering 731 immune-cell traits, 1,091 plasma metabolites, 3,230 AA cases and 475,964 controls. Complementary in-vitro CCK-8 cytotoxicity experiments on human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs) were further conducted for candidate metabolites Adrenate (22:4n6) and BAFF-R.

RESULTS: BAFF-R on CD20- (OR = 0.859, 95%CI: 0.797-0.926, P = 7.17 × 10-5) and, to a lesser extent, Granulocyte AC (OR = 0.900, 95%CI: 0.843-0.961, P = 1.57 × 10-3) emerged as candidate protective immune-cell markers for AA. Adrenate (22:4n6) and Nisinate (24:6n3) mediated 4.47% and 9.84% of these protective effects, respectively. Adrenate triggered significant dose-dependent cytotoxicity in HASMCs.

CONCLUSION: This multi-omics genetic-toxicology study provides causal genetic evidence for immune-metabolite regulatory axes in AA pathogenesis. Notably, Adrenate presents dual biological effects: it transmits immune-protective signals but exerts direct vascular cellular toxicity. Our findings highlight the utility of MR-assisted precision toxicity prediction for disease risk evaluation and therapeutic target mining for AA.

METHODS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) and two-step mediation analysis were performed using European-ancestry GWAS summary datasets covering 731 immune-cell traits, 1,091 plasma metabolites, 3,230 AA cases and 475,964 controls.

title: Occult Patent Foramen Ovale Causing Severe Refractory Hypoxemia After Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Repair.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: After surgery for acute type A aortic dissection, pulmonary function can be reduced because of several possible causes. It is necessary to identify the main cause.

CASE SUMMARY: A patient experienced refractory hypoxemia following type A aortic dissection repair. Despite proper respiratory and inotropic support, and near-normal chest imaging, severe hypoxia persisted. Echocardiography revealed an occult patent foramen ovale (PFO) with significant right-to-left shunting, driven by positive-pressure mechanical ventilation and elevated right-sided cardiac pressures. Percutaneous transcatheter closure immediately improved oxygenation, enabling successful ventilator weaning.

DISCUSSION: Occult PFO should be suspected in unexplained postsurgical hypoxemia. Early echocardiographic evaluation and prompt percutaneous closure can rapidly reverse hypoxia, preventing prolonged mechanical ventilation and secondary complications.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Persistent refractory hypoxemia after acute type A aortic dissection repair is not always pulmonary in origin. Occult PFO should be suspected and early echocardiographic confirmation with prompt PFO closure can produce immediate clinical improvement.

title: Social-biological misalignment modulates the prognostic impact of infarct volume after endovascular thrombectomy.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) achieves high rates of reperfusion, yet functional recovery remains heterogeneous. We investigated whether social-biological time misalignment modifies the association between final infarct volume and 90-day functional outcome.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 160 patients with large vessel occlusion treated with EVT. Misalignment was quantified using a composite score incorporating occupational shift exposure and symptom onset timing. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the interaction between misalignment and final infarct volume on favorable 90-day outcome (modified Rankin Scale 0-2).

RESULTS: Misalignment was not independently associated with favorable outcome. However, a significant interaction was observed (OR = 9.70, 95% CI 1.74-54.10, LRT p = 0.008), remaining significant after FDR correction (q = 0.034), stable across profile likelihood and Firth penalized regression. The interaction improved model fit (AIC 124.35 → 119.38) and provided modest incremental net benefit. Exploratory threshold analysis suggested a potential inflection point approximating 25 mL, but this is hypothesis-generating and requires validation.

CONCLUSION: Misalignment does not exert a uniform adverse effect but acts as a state-dependent modifier, modifying the association between final infarct volume and favorable outcome. The interaction between chronobiological state and infarct burden offers a novel framework for understanding outcome heterogeneity.

We investigated whether social-biological time misalignment modifies the association between final infarct volume and 90-day functional outcome. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 160 patients with large vessel occlusion treated with EVT.

title: Machine-learning-derived laboratory signatures associated with postoperative day-3 ultrasound-detected lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis after fractures around the knee.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to construct risk-discrimination models for postoperative-day-3 ultrasound-detected lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) status in patients with fractures around the knee (FAK) using five machine-learning algorithms and compare model performance across five machine-learning algorithms.

METHODS: Electronic medical records of 1,071 patients who underwent surgical treatment for FAK at Suining Central Hospital from January 2023 to August 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 749) and a test set (n = 322) at a 7:3 ratio. Feature selection occurred exclusively within the training dataset. Predictive variables were screened using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, the Boruta algorithm, and recursive feature elimination-extreme gradient boosting (RFE-XGBoost). Five predictive models were developed, including logistic regression, k-nearest neighbor (KNN), random forest (RF), light gradient-boosting machine (LightGBM), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost). Model performance was evaluated comprehensively via the area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score. Receiver-operating-characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision-curve analysis (DCA) were utilized to identify the selected model. Finally, Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were employed to interpret the global and local prediction outputs of the selected model.

RESULTS: Seventeen overlapping features were identified via feature-selection procedures for final modelling, among which postoperative-day-1 and postoperative-day-3 laboratory biomarkers contributed most substantially to model output. XGBoost was chosen for subsequent SHAP interpretability analyses based on balanced performance observed in cross-validated out-of-fold outputs from the training set. Several non-linear models yielded comparably high discrimination, with overlapping 95% confidence intervals for AUROC.The cross-validated AUC for the XGBoost model in the training set was 0.9932, with a classification threshold of 0.57 derived from the Youden index. In the test set, the AUROC was 0.998 (95% CI: 0.993-1.000), AUPRC was 0.996 (95% CI: 0.988-1.000), accuracy was 0.991 (95% CI: 0.978-1.000), sensitivity was 0.969 (95% CI: 0.930-1.000), specificity was 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000), precision was 1.000 (95% CI: 1.000-1.000), and F1-score was 0.984 (95% CI: 0.964-1.000). The Brier score for the test set was 0.013. Calibration curves and decision-curve analysis demonstrated favourable probability calibration and higher estimated net benefit across a range of threshold probabilities. SHAP-value analysis highlighted that postoperative-day-1 CRP, postoperative-day-3 FIB, postoperative-day-3 APTT, postoperative-day-3 CRP, postoperative-day-3 FDP, postoperative-day-3 PT, postoperative-day-1 UREA, and postoperative-day-1 CREA were major contributing features.

CONCLUSION: The XGBoost model demonstrated excellent discrimination and favorable calibration in the internal test set for identifying postoperative-day-3 ultrasound-detected DVT among patients with FAK. However, several predictors in the final model were measured on postoperative day 3, temporally proximate to the time-point of DVT ascertainment; these biomarkers may reflect biochemical changes secondary to already-formed thrombus rather than pre-thrombotic prospective risk signals. Therefore, the near-perfect discrimination observed in this retrospective cohort should be interpreted cautiously and should not be regarded as definitive evidence of prospective early-prediction performance. Temporal and multicenter external validation using a prespecified prediction time point, ideally restricted to variables available prior to DVT assessment, is required to determine the model's generalizability and prospective clinical applicability.

METHODS: Electronic medical records of 1,071 patients who underwent surgical treatment for FAK at Suining Central Hospital from January 2023 to August 2026 were retrospectively reviewed. Patients were randomly divided into a training set (n = 749) and a test set (n = 322) at a 7:3 ratio.

title: Triglyceride-glucose index and the incidence of peripheral artery disease: a dose-response meta-analysis of longitudinal studies.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a simple surrogate marker of insulin resistance and has been increasingly investigated as a predictor of cardiovascular diseases. However, longitudinal evidence regarding its association with incident peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains limited and inconsistent. We conducted a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis to evaluate the association between the TyG index and the risk of incident PAD.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were systematically searched from inception to June 28, 2026. Longitudinal observational studies evaluating the association between the conventional TyG index and incidents PAD in adults were eligible. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) comparing the highest versus lowest TyG categories were calculated using restricted maximum likelihood random-effects models. Linear and nonlinear dose-response meta-analyses were performed using restricted cubic spline models.

RESULTS: Five longitudinal studies involving 417,499 participants and 7,800 incident PAD events were included. Compared with the lowest TyG category, a high TyG index was associated with a significantly increased risk of incident PAD (RR = 1.49, 95% CI 1.06 to 2.10; p = 0.02), although substantial heterogeneity was observed (I2 = 88.4%). Sensitivity analyses demonstrated robust findings. In the linear dose-response meta-analysis, each 1-unit increase in the TyG index was associated with a 22% higher risk of incident PAD (RR = 1.22, 95% CI 1.08 to 1.37; p = 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a significant overall dose-response association (p = 0.001) with no evidence of nonlinearity (p for nonlinearity = 0.367), indicating an approximately linear relationship between the TyG index and PAD risk.

CONCLUSIONS: A higher TyG index is associated with an increased risk of incident PAD in a dose-dependent and approximately linear manner.

SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261470450.

However, longitudinal evidence regarding its association with incident peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains limited and inconsistent. We conducted a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis to evaluate the association between the TyG index and the risk of incident PAD.

title: Evaluating the Society for Vascular Surgery 90-Min Door-to-Intervention Target for Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms (rAAAs) are a life-threatening condition requiring rapid surgical intervention for survival. Guidelines from the Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) in 2018 advised a door-to-intervention time of ≤90 min. We hypothesized that door-to-intervention time would not predict outcomes following rAAA repair, as treatment timelines may reflect differences in physiological severity, diagnostic assessment and operative modality, including the use of endovascular repair (EVAR).

METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study of 29 patients presenting to University Hospitals Plymouth who underwent surgical intervention for rAAA between February 2018 and December 2024. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients achieving the SVS-recommended door-to-intervention time of ≤90 min. Secondary outcomes were the rates of EVAR compared to open repair and the associated mortality and morbidity.

RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients were included, of whom only three (10.3%) met the SVS target. Median door-to-intervention time was 182 min. Arrival-to-diagnosis time was associated with the greatest delay, with a median time of 84 min. Twenty-three patients (79.3%) underwent open repair, with a 60.9% (14/23) mortality rate compared to 16.7% (1/6) for EVAR cases. Shorter door-to-intervention time was associated with higher 30-day mortality, although no association was observed with overall mortality. Morbidity rates were 95.6% (22/23) for open cases and 50.0% (3/6) for EVAR cases. No statistically significant association was identified between overall morbidity rates and door-to-intervention time. However, higher grade complications were statistically significantly associated with both shorter arrival to diagnosis time (P = 0.011) and shorter arrival to knife-to-skin time (P = 0.039).

CONCLUSION: Overall, 89.7% (26/29) of rAAAs presenting to University Hospitals Plymouth between February 2018 and December 2024 exceeded the recommended SVS door-to-intervention target of ≤90 min. Shorter timelines were observed among patients with higher grade complications and who subsequently died. Mortality was higher following open repair. This study is limited due to its small sample size and retrospective methodology. Earlier identification of rAAAs could reduce door-to-intervention time; education, prealerting and optimized imaging pathways are potential methods for achieving this. These findings suggest that the SVS 90-minute threshold may have limited value as a standalone outcome-based quality metric and should be interpreted alongside measures of physiological severity and pathway performance. Expedited treatment is likely influenced by underlying hemodynamic instability. The development of validated risk stratification tools may be beneficial in determining modality of operation and timing.

title: Venous thromboembolism after breast cancer surgery: incidence, predictive factors and outcomes in 270,564 patients.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Breast cancer surgery is generally considered to be low risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, when VTE occurs, it may lead to severe complications and increased mortality. This study aimed to determine the incidence, predictors, and clinical impact of postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery using a large, multicenter surgical database.

METHODS: The American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database (2008-2023) was queried to identify female patients undergoing surgery for breast cancer without concurrent reconstruction. Patients were stratified according to postoperative VTE occurrence. Demographics, comorbidities, laboratory values, operative characteristics, and 30-day outcomes were compared. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors of VTE and to construct a predictive model, which was internally validated using bootstrap resampling.

RESULTS: Among 270,564 patients included, 465 (0.2%) developed postoperative VTE. Of these, 247 (53.1%) had deep vein thrombosis, 177 (38.1%) pulmonary embolism, and 41 (8.8%) both. Patients who developed VTE were older, had higher body mass index (BMI), greater comorbidity burden, and longer operative times (all p < 0.001). They also demonstrated lower preoperative serum albumin, hematocrit, prothrombin time, and albumin-to-creatinine ratio. VTE was associated with significantly longer hospital stays, increased rates of reoperation and readmission, and a more than 20-fold higher crude 30-day mortality (1.9% vs. 0.1%) (all p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, increasing age (OR 1.26 per 10 years), BMI (OR 1.17 per 5 kg/m²), congestive heart failure (OR 2.43), metastatic cancer (OR 2.05), lower serum albumin (OR 0.63 per 1 g/dL), and longer operative duration (OR 1.09 per 30 min) were independently associated with postoperative VTE. Compared with partial mastectomy, total mastectomy (OR 2.58), modified radical mastectomy (OR 2.22), and radical mastectomy (OR 2.80) were associated with significantly higher odds of postoperative VTE. The predictive model demonstrated acceptable discrimination (AUC 0.717; optimism-corrected 0.700) and good calibration. Age, BMI, congestive heart failure, metastatic cancer, mastectomy and operative time remained associated with VTE in all sensitivity analyses.

CONCLUSION: Postoperative VTE following breast cancer surgery is uncommon but associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Advanced age, obesity, cardiac comorbidity, metastatic disease, hypoalbuminemia, longer operative duration, and greater surgical extent were independently associated with increased thromboembolic risk. Awareness of these risk factors may support individualized perioperative risk assessment and thromboprophylaxis decisions, as recommended by current consensus guidance, and facilitate earlier recognition of postoperative VTE.

title: Evaluation of Total Patent Branch Vessel Ostial Area at Preoperative CT Angiography for Predicting Type II Endoleak after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair.
abstract: Background Type II endoleak (T2EL) is a common complication after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) that may lead to aneurysm sac enlargement. Although guideline-based criteria are used to identify high-risk patients, their predictive accuracy remains limited. Purpose To evaluate the predictive value of preoperative total branch vessel ostial area at CT angiography (CTA) for T2EL after EVAR. Materials and Methods This single-center retrospective study included patients undergoing EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) between January 2010 and December 2020. After exclusion of other endoleak types, CTA-derived anatomic parameters and outcomes were compared by isolated T2EL status. Total branch vessel ostial area was evaluated using prespecified Cox models and Cox-least absolute shrinkage and selection operator analysis. Discrimination and reproducibility were assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, intraclass correlation coefficients, and Bland-Altman analysis. Results Of 216 patients in this study (mean age, 66 years ± 7.6 [SD]; 190 male; median follow-up, 4.7 years), 86 (39.8%) developed T2EL. Total branch vessel ostial area showed excellent reproducibility (intraclass correlation coefficients, 0.98-1.00) and was larger in patients with T2EL than in those without T2EL (median, 24.5 vs 11.7 mm2; P < .001). Sac enlargement was more frequent with T2EL (45.3% [39 of 86] vs 12.3% [16 of 130]; P < .001) and was associated with reintervention (hazard ratio [HR], 2.83; P = .003) but not overall survival (HR, 1.76; P = .28). In the fully adjusted Cox model, total branch vessel ostial area was associated with T2EL (HR, 1.06 per 1-mm2 increase [95% CI: 1.04, 1.08]; P < .001). Total branch ostial area showed better discrimination for T2EL than guideline-based criteria (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.82 vs 0.64; P < .001), with a Youden index-derived cutoff of 15.55 mm2. Restricted cubic spline analysis showed a positive continuous association in T2EL risk with increasing ostial area (P < .001). Conclusion Preoperative CTA-derived total branch vessel ostial area outperformed conventional branch diameter and count criteria for predicting T2EL in patients after EVAR for infrarenal AAA. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. See also the editorial by Liddell in this issue.

title: Metabolic Equivalents and Cardiac Metrics Predict Delisting Better Than Traditional Frailty Measures and Enhance the Nationally Utilized Kidney Transplant Decision Aid.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Cardiovascular disease is the most common cause of death among kidney transplant waitlist patients. Cardiac and frailty information are not included in the scientific registry of transplant recipients kidney transplant decision aid (SRTR-KTDA) used to predict outcomes during transplant evaluation. We compared the predictiveness of an expanded model of kidney waitlist drop-off with the nationally utilized SRTR-KTDA.

METHODS: 239 variables related to patient demographics, frailty, and cardiac history/testing were collected for 312 Veterans consecutively listed for kidney transplant between 2015 and 2020. Analysis compared transplanted/listed patients versus delisted patients using bootstrapped stepwise logistic regression and Fine-Gray competing risk modeling that identified variables most consistently predictive of delisting for comparison with the SRTR-KTDA.

RESULTS: Predictors of delisting included treadmill METs, BNP, pulse, systolic blood pressure, history of angina, history of heart failure, calcium channel blocker use, angiotensin receptor blocker use, clonidine use, glomerulonephritis causing renal failure, > 70% left anterior descending artery stenosis on cardiac catheterization, and troponin. Within our population, the SRTR-KTDA model (age, sex, race, height, weight, blood type, cPRA, years on dialysis, diabetes, cancer history, peripheral artery disease) produced an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.65-0.716. Adding significant bootstrap variables to the SRTR-KTDA increased the AUC to 0.78-0.80.

CONCLUSIONS: All the information needed to predict delisting in our cohort can occur during a single evaluation visit including a robust history/physical exam, measurement of treadmill METs, and blood draw. The addition of cardiac information and METs significantly improved the predictiveness of the SRTR-KTDA. Optimally modeling waitlist outcomes is crucial since its 2025 introduction as a national transplant performance metric.

Cardiac and frailty information are not included in the scientific registry of transplant recipients kidney transplant decision aid (SRTR-KTDA) used to predict outcomes during transplant evaluation. title: Diagnostic accuracy of point-of-care ultrasound for the detection of acute aortic syndrome in the emergency department: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute aortic syndromes (AAS) are a group of aortic disorders with a wide range of presentations that are easily misdiagnosed in the emergency department (ED). The 2024 European Society of Cardiology Guidelines recommended focused transthoracic echocardiography as the first-line imaging tool for the detection of aortic dissection, but the performance of point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in detecting AAS in ED varies considerably in the existing literature. We aim to gather and synthesize existing studies to provide a more comprehensive overview of the diagnostic accuracy and value of POCUS for the detection of AAS and its generalizability in the ED setting. METHODS: Ovid MEDLINE, EMBASE, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched for studies published from 1 January 2000 to 21 July 2025. Diagnostic accuracy studies of POCUS in the ED for the detection of AAS were included. For included studies, the diagnostic accuracy of POCUS for detecting AAS was revealed by calculating the sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative likelihood ratio, and diagnostic odds ratio, with 95% credible intervals (CrI). The diagnostic performance of POCUS was evaluated by summary receiver operator curve (SROC). RESULTS: A total of 4,855 patients from seven studies were included in the meta-analysis. For any sonographic signs for detecting AAS, the pooled sensitivity and specificity of POCUS were 88.3% (95%CrI: 85.1% -91.2%) and 80.3% (95%CrI: 63.4%-92.9%), respectively. The area under the SROC of any sonographic signs for detecting AAS was 0.91 (95%CrI: 0.65-0.96). CONCLUSION: This systematic review provides support that POCUS may be a useful early imaging tool for ruling in AAS in the ED due to its high specificity for direct sonographic sign. While the overall certainty of evidence is moderate to low, larger-scale prospective studies on the use of POCUS with other diagnostic tools for detecting AAS are necessary in ED settings.

title: A 10-Year Single-Center Experience in Pediatric Thromboembolism: Management Strategies and Clinical Outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric thromboembolism is uncommon but clinically important, and its epidemiology varies according to age, underlying disease, catheter exposure, and referral patterns. This study evaluated the epidemiology, risk factors, management, and outcomes of pediatric thromboembolism over a 10-year period in a tertiary care center.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed children aged 0-18 years with symptomatic, radiologically confirmed thromboembolism between January 2010 and January 2020. Incidentally detected asymptomatic thromboses and cases without imaging confirmation were excluded. Venous and arterial events were analyzed separately.

RESULTS: Among 51,025 pediatric admissions, 70 patients had thromboembolism, corresponding to an admission-based rate of 13.7 per 10,000 admissions. Venous thromboembolism accounted for 51 cases (72.9%) and arterial thromboembolism for 19 cases (27.1%). Median age at diagnosis was 6 years (range, 1 day-18 years), and 49 patients (70.0%) were male. The central nervous system was the most frequent anatomical region involved. Central venous catheterization was the leading modifiable acquired risk factor. Active antithrombotic or interventional treatment was used in 68 patients (97.1%); low molecular weight heparin containing regimens were used in 46 patients (65.7%). Complete recovery was documented in 55 patients (78.6%), recurrence in 12 (17.1%), and mortality in 3 (4.3%). Recurrence was more frequent after venous than arterial events (23.5% vs 0%; p = .028).

CONCLUSION: In this 10-year cohort, venous events predominated and catheter related thrombosis remained a major preventable contributor. Recurrence was confined to venous events, supporting careful long term follow up and individualized secondary prevention for high risk children. Standardized catheter care practices and selective, appropriately timed thrombophilia testing are practical priorities.

This study evaluated the epidemiology, risk factors, management, and outcomes of pediatric thromboembolism over a 10-year period in a tertiary care center. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed children aged 0-18 years with symptomatic, radiologically confirmed thromboembolism between January 2010 and January 2020.

title: Venous thromboembolism after joint arthroplasty: where do we stand with aspirin?
abstract: Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total joint arthroplasty remains heterogeneous, particularly regarding the role of aspirin within modern fast-track pathways. Although aspirin is widely used in North American arthroplasty practice, European guidelines remain more conservative and often provide limited or non-operational recommendations for its use after total hip and knee arthroplasty. Contemporary evidence supports aspirin as a viable prophylactic option in selected patients, with potential advantages related to its safety profile, cost, ease of administration and reduced treatment burden. The clinical role of aspirin should be interpreted within a risk-stratified framework that accounts for thromboembolic risk, bleeding risk, surgical complexity, early mobilization and duration of prophylaxis. Available evidence, including recent randomized data, supports aspirin-based prophylaxis in appropriately selected patients, both as part of sequential strategies and, increasingly, as monotherapy within contemporary fast-track pathways. This scoping review synthesizes current guideline-level evidence and contemporary clinical data to clarify practical considerations for agent selection, dosing, duration and aspirin-based prophylaxis after total joint arthroplasty.

title: [Value of a CT angiography-based deep learning model for differentiating SVS grade Ⅱ and grade Ⅲ blunt thoracic aortic injury: a retrospective multicenter staged study].
abstract: Objectives: To develop a segmentation-guided multitask deep learning model for Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) grades Ⅰ to Ⅳ classification of blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI) and validate its clinical utility for differentiating SVS grades Ⅱ and Ⅲ. Methods: This is a retrospective case series study. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) data were collected from 317 patients with BTAI at 12 hospitals in China, including the First Medical Center of Chinese People's Liberation Army General Hospital, West China Hospital of Sichuan University, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University, and other local hospitals, between January 2006 and May 2026. The cohort included 258 male and 59 female patients, with an age of (54.8±15.3) years (range:16 to 92 years). The 253-patient development cohort was divided using a patient-level random split stratified by SVS injury grade and source center at an approximate ratio of 8∶2 into a training set of 202 patients and an internal validation set of 51 patients. The 64 BTAI cases from the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University were locked in advance as an independent external test set. The model consisted of a shared encoder, a lesion-segmentation branch, and a mask-guided classification branch. The primary outcomes were the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and grade Ⅲ sensitivity for differentiating SVS grade Ⅱ (intramural hematoma) from grade Ⅲ (pseudoaneurysm) in the external test set. Secondary outcomes included segmentation, automated measurements, and offline reader-study results. Results: The internal validation set covered SVS grades Ⅰ to Ⅳ, with an overall grading accuracy of 92.2% (47/51) and a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.919. The external test set included 31 SVS grade Ⅱ (intramural hematoma) cases and 33 SVS grade Ⅲ (pseudoaneurysm) cases. The model had an AUC of 0.968 (95%CI:0.924 to 0.996), an accuracy of 92.2% (59/64), grade Ⅲ sensitivity of 93.9% (31/33), and grade Ⅱ specificity of 90.3% (28/31); two grade Ⅲ cases were misclassified as grade Ⅱ. The automated segmentation success rate was 96.9% (62/64), the overall lesion Dice similarity coefficient was 0.872±0.072 (range:0.46 to 0.99), and model inference time per case was (15.4±2.4) s (range:10.8 to 22.6 s). In the fixed-sequence reader study, six junior physicians had higher grade Ⅱ/Ⅲ accuracy and grade Ⅲ sensitivity and shorter interpretation times during the artificial intelligence-assisted phase than during the unaided phase. Conclusions: The segmentation-guided CTA deep learning model developed in this study performed BTAI lesion segmentation, SVS grading, and measurement of key morphologic parameters, and maintained good discrimination between SVS grades Ⅱ and Ⅲ in the independent external test set. Model assistance may help reduce missed grade Ⅲ cases by junior physicians and shorten interpretation time, thereby supporting standardized imaging assessment of BTAI.

Methods: This is a retrospective case series study. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) data were collected from 317 patients with BTAI at 12 hospitals in China, including the First Medical Center of Chinese People's Liberation Army General Hospital, West China Hospital of Sichuan University, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University, and other local hospitals, between January 2006 and May 2026.

title: Major re-amputation after initial diabetic foot amputation: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Reamputation after initial diabetic foot amputation remains a major clinical challenge associated with substantial morbidity. Identifying factors related to major reamputation may improve patient management and limb preservation. This study evaluated the impact of clinical, metabolic, nutritional, and vascular parameters on the risk of major reamputation. This retrospective cohort study included 141 patients who underwent lower-extremity amputation for diabetic foot disease between 2020 and 2025. Demographic variables, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, peripheral arterial disease (PAD), infection history, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels, and Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI) were analyzed. Major reamputation was defined as a subsequent ipsilateral amputation progressing to a below-knee or above-knee level; contralateral amputations and more proximal minor amputations confined to the foot were not considered outcome events. The median follow-up was 3.0 years (range, 1-5). Continuous variables were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test and categorical variables using the Pearson chi-square test. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate major reamputation-free survival, and Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to evaluate factors associated with time to major reamputation. A Fine-Gray competing-risk analysis was additionally performed considering death before major reamputation as a competing event. Major reamputation occurred in 31 patients (22.0%). Patients with reamputation had significantly lower BMI and PNI values and higher HbA1c levels (all P < .001). Smoking and PAD were significantly more frequent in the reamputation group (both P < .001), whereas no significant between-group differences were observed for age, sex, serum albumin, or infection history. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, PAD (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.25, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.13-18.32, P < .001) and higher HbA1c (adjusted HR 1.40, 95% CI 1.19-1.65, P < .001) were independently associated with an increased hazard of major reamputation, whereas higher PNI was associated with a reduced hazard (adjusted HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-0.99, P = .009). Lower BMI, higher HbA1c, reduced PNI, smoking, and PAD were associated with major reamputation. In multivariable time-to-event analysis, PAD, HbA1c, and PNI remained independently associated with the outcome. These findings demonstrate associations between routinely available clinical parameters and major reamputation and warrant further evaluation in prospective studies.

Identifying factors related to major reamputation may improve patient management and limb preservation. This study evaluated the impact of clinical, metabolic, nutritional, and vascular parameters on the risk of major reamputation.

title: Contralateral major amputation following diabetes- and peripheral artery disease-related limb loss: A systematic review and pooled meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major amputation remains a devastating and understudied outcome in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and diabetes mellitus (DM)-related limb disease. Although modern vascular care emphasizes index and symptomatic limb surveillance, the population-level risk of nonindex limb (NIL) major amputation remains incompletely defined. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to quantify NIL major amputation incidence and evaluate factors associated with contralateral limb loss.

METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed (MEDLINE), Embase, and Scopus through January 2026 was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analyses guidelines. Studies reporting contralateral above- or below-knee amputation in adults with PAD, CLTI, DM-related limb disease, or previous ipsilateral major amputation were included. Single-arm random-effects meta-analysis using the restricted maximum likelihood estimator was performed with log-transformed effect sizes. Subgroup analyses were conducted by clinical phenotype, geographic location, study era, and DM prevalence. Secondary outcomes included overall mortality, bilateral major amputation, NIL minor amputation, NIL revascularization, and development of NIL CLTI.

RESULTS: Seventeen cohorts encompassing 30,359 patients were included. The pooled incidence of NIL major amputation was six per 100 person-years [95% confidence interval (CI), 3-9], with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 98.93%). Meta-regression showed no significant differences by clinical phenotype (P = .622), geographic region (P = .662), study era (P = .893), or DM prevalence (P = .127). Clinical phenotypes included CLTI vs non-CLTI PAD or DM vs postipsilateral major amputation. Geographic region was divided into United States and international studies. Study era was divided into modern (2010-2025) and legacy (pre-2010) studies. Longer follow-up duration was inversely associated with reported incidence (P < .001). Pooled mortality rate was 38% (95% CI, 30%-47%), and the pooled rate of bilateral major amputation was 12% (95% CI, 8%-18%). Other secondary outcomes included a pooled NIL minor amputation rate of 11% (95% CI, 3%-37%), NIL revascularization rate of 19% (95% CI, 6%-47%), and NIL CLTI development rate of 32% (95% CI, 11%-64%).

CONCLUSIONS: NIL major amputation remains a persistent risk in PAD and DM-related limb disease. These findings support the need for structured bilateral limb surveillance and early NIL risk stratification to inform comprehensive limb preservation care.

Although modern vascular care emphasizes index and symptomatic limb surveillance, the population-level risk of nonindex limb (NIL) major amputation remains incompletely defined. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to quantify NIL major amputation incidence and evaluate factors associated with contralateral limb loss.

title: Index below-knee endovascular intervention for intermittent claudication is associated with increased amputation risk.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guidelines advise against infrapopliteal peripheral vascular intervention (PVI) for intermittent claudication (IC) due to potential harm with unclear benefit. We hypothesized that below-knee (BK) intervention at index PVI for IC confers higher future amputation risk than above-knee (AK)-only treatment.

METHODS: From the Vascular Quality Initiative VQI PVI registry (2015-2025), we identified elective, initial PVIs for IC, and compared those patients undergoing AK-only treatment to those having any BK intervention. Using our previously described methodology, the long-term amputation data were obtained by linking the PVI and amputation registries via unique patient identifiers. Demographic and procedural data were analyzed descriptively. Kaplan-Meier analysis estimated risk of major and any (major + minor) amputation, with independent predictors of amputation identified by multivariable Firth logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 92,899 treated limbs (AK, 81,338; BK, 11,561), BK patients had increased rates of diabetes (54% vs 41%), congestive heart failure (18% vs 13%), and end-stage renal disease/dialysis (4.7% vs 1.7%; P < .001). BK patients were more likely to be Black (21% vs 13%; P < .001), Hispanic (8.8% vs 4.3%; P < .001), and Asian (1.5% vs 1.0%; P < .001). Smoking history predominated in AK (89% vs 67%; P < .001). A total of 16,086 limbs required repeat PVI, 13,831 (17%) in the AK group vs 2255 (20%) in the BK group (P < .001). At reintervention, BK patients were more likely to have progressed to chronic limb-threatening ischemia (41% vs 25%; P < .001) and undergo ≥2 repeat interventions (32% vs 27%; P < .001). Initial BK intervention was associated with greater ipsilateral major (odds ratio, 2.39; 95% confidence interval, 1.70-3.35) and any (odds ratio, 2.36; 95% confidence interval, 1.75-3.18) amputation. Kaplan-Meier showed increased major (1-year: 0.3% vs 0.1%; 5-years: 0.4% vs 0.1%) and any amputation risk (1-year: 0.5% vs 0.1%; 5-years: 0.7% vs 0.2%).

CONCLUSIONS: Index BK intervention for IC portends greater risk of progression to chronic limb-threatening ischemia, repeat PVI, and ipsilateral amputation, highlighting the potentially dangerous treatment trap of infrapopliteal intervention in patients with intermittent claudicants.

We hypothesized that below-knee (BK) intervention at index PVI for IC confers higher future amputation risk than above-knee (AK)-only treatment. METHODS: From the Vascular Quality Initiative VQI PVI registry (2015-2025), we identified elective, initial PVIs for IC, and compared those patients undergoing AK-only treatment to those having any BK intervention.

title: Midterm outcomes with extended follow-up of open and endovascular repair of visceral artery aneurysms using a target-artery preservation strategy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment of visceral artery aneurysms is heterogeneous, and sacrifice of the target vessel is frequently accepted. This study reports a single-center experience of visceral artery aneurysm treatment aiming for target-artery preservation.

METHODS: All consecutive elective open and endovascular visceral artery aneurysm repairs performed with the intent of aneurysm exclusion and target-artery preservation between January 2016 and April 2025 were retrospectively analyzed; minimum follow-up was 1 year. The primary end point was treatment success (visceral artery aneurysm exclusion + target-artery patency). Secondary end points included primary treatment failure and analysis of associated factors. Time-to-event outcomes were survival, freedom from reinterventions, and freedom from loss of treatment success; patients exceeding 5 years were described separately.

RESULTS: Forty patients were included; the splenic artery was the most frequent location (45%). Primary treatment success was achieved in 36 of 40 patients (90%): 10 of 10 (100%) after open and 26 of 30 (87%) after endovascular repair; after 4 conversions (3 splenic artery), assisted treatment success was 37 of 40 (93%). No organ ischemia, splenectomy, or 30-day death occurred. Splenic failures were associated with moderate-to-severe calcification (P = .011) and severe tortuosity (P = .027). At median follow-up of 48 months, 5-year survival was 90 ± 6%, freedom from reintervention was 94 ± 4%, and freedom from loss of treatment success was 100%. Whole-cohort 7-year survival was 79 ± 9%; no reintervention occurred beyond 2 years.

CONCLUSION: Visceral artery aneurysm exclusion with target-artery preservation is feasible, safe, and durable at midterm after open and endovascular repair, with encouraging long-term observations. In this small series, severe tortuosity and calcification of the proximal splenic artery were associated with endovascular failure.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Treatment of visceral artery aneurysms is heterogeneous, and sacrifice of the target vessel is frequently accepted. This study reports a single-center experience of visceral artery aneurysm treatment aiming for target-artery preservation. METHODS: All consecutive elective open and endovascular visceral artery aneurysm repairs performed with the intent of aneurysm exclusion and target-artery preservation between January 2016 and April 2025 were retrospectively analyzed; minimum follow-up was 1 year.
