title: Intraoperative estimated blood loss and perioperative transfusion are independently associated with postoperative morbidity and mortality after lower-extremity bypass.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Intraoperative estimated blood loss (EBL) and need for perioperative packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion are common during lower-extremity bypass (LEB) for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and have each been associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. However, their joint associations with postoperative outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion, individually and jointly, with postoperative morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing LEB for CLTI.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative database. Patients undergoing LEB for CLTI between 2014 and 2023 were identified. Receiver-operating characteristic analysis identified an optimal EBL threshold of 225 mL (area under the curve, 0.72) for predicting transfusion, which was used to stratify patients into low-EBL (<225 mL) and high-EBL (≥225 mL) groups. Primary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, 30-day mortality, and a composite end point. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess adjusted associations across four groups defined by EBL and transfusion status. Separate model was used to evaluate the interaction between EBL and pRBC transfusion.

RESULTS: Among 36,019 procedures, 58.5% had low EBL, and 41.5% had high EBL. Patients who had high EBL and did not require blood transfusion had increased odds of adverse postoperative outcomes, including 30-day mortality [adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 1.26; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.01-1.59], MI (aOR, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.48-2.39), stroke (aOR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.09-2.29), and the composite outcome (aOR 1.51, 95% CI, 1.29-1.78). Patients who had low EBL and received blood transfusion had increased odds of 30-day mortality (aOR, 2.46; 95% CI, 1.95-3.10), MI (aOR, 6.57; 95% CI, 5.26-8.21), stroke (aOR, 2.75; 95% CI, 1.84-4.12), and the composite outcome (aOR, 4.08; 95% CI, 3.48-4.78). Patients who had both high EBL and required perioperative blood transfusion demonstrated the highest odds of adverse outcomes, including 30-day mortality (aOR, 2.54; 95% CI, 2.09-3.08), MI (aOR, 7.39; 95% CI, 6.08-8.98), stroke (aOR, 3.79; 95% CI, 2.76-5.21), and the composite outcome (aOR, 4.42; 95% CI, 3.87-5.05). Formal interaction testing demonstrated significant between EBL and transfusion.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing LEB for CLTI, intraoperative EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion were both independently and jointly associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality. These findings identify EBL and transfusion as markers of perioperative risk and support further investigation of blood-sparing strategies and individualized transfusion practices.

However, their joint associations with postoperative outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion, individually and jointly, with postoperative morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing LEB for CLTI.

title: Carotid endarterectomy versus transcarotid artery revascularization for asymptomatic carotid stenosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The treatment for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis includes a surgical or interventional approach in selected cases. Although endarterectomy should be considered over stenting for selected patients, according to the latest European Society of Vascular Surgery guidelines, the Carotid Revascularization and Medical Management for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis Trials suggested that carotid stenting would be associated with low rates of perioperative stroke or death. The transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) technique is a relatively new endovascular method that involves placing a stent at the carotid bifurcation through direct carotid artery access, performed under a flow reversal system. This approach avoids manipulation of the aortic arch, potentially reducing embolic events. The aim of this systematic review is to compare TCAR with carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in asymptomatic patients undergoing carotid intervention. It seeks to evaluate whether TCAR is associated with improved perioperative outcomes, such as lower rates of stroke and death, compared with CEA, given its potentially less invasive approach.

METHODS: The review was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) on the platforms PubMed/MEDLINE, OVID/Embase, and Scopus. The following MeSH terms were used: "asymptomatic carotid stenosis" AND "carotid endarterectomy," "transcarotid artery revascularization" OR "TCAR." Full-text screening and data extraction were performed with the support of the COVIDENCE platform. Six studies were selected for this systematic review, comprising a total of 132,684 patients (30,581 undergoing TCAR and 102,103 undergoing CEA). Statistical analysis was performed using R software.

RESULTS: The selected studies for this systematic review showed similar results in terms of perioperative stroke and death for asymptomatic patients who underwent carotid endarterectomy and TCAR.

CONCLUSIONS: Our results suggest that there are no significant differences between CEA and TCAR for the treatment of asymptomatic patients who require a surgical or interventional approach. Further studies are necessary to provide more robust data in this field.

Although endarterectomy should be considered over stenting for selected patients, according to the latest European Society of Vascular Surgery guidelines, the Carotid Revascularization and Medical Management for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis Trials suggested that carotid stenting would be associated with low rates of perioperative stroke or death. The transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) technique is a relatively new endovascular method that involves placing a stent at the carotid bifurcation through direct carotid artery access, performed under a flow reversal system.

title: Use and Safety of Peripherally Inserted Venous Catheters Versus Central Venous Catheters for Patients With Lymphoma Receiving Frontline Anthracycline-based Chemotherapy.
abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Peripheral intravenous catheters (PIVs) for the administration of anthracycline-based chemotherapy have the potential risk of vascular and tissue injury due to extravasation of vesicant agents. Central venous catheters (CVCs) are frequently utilized to mitigate this. This multicenter retrospective real-world analysis (RWA) evaluated complications associated with PIVs versus CVCs for the administration of anthracycline-based chemotherapy in patients with lymphoma.

METHODS: We conducted a RWA across 9 US medical centers, including adults with newly diagnosed lymphoma who received anthracycline-based chemotherapy via PIV or CVC between 2010 and 2025. Detailed baseline characteristics and safety outcomes were collected, applying standard definitions for extravasation and other recognized complications. Incidence rates of safety outcomes were calculated, and multivariable Poisson regression models were applied to adjust for confounders.

RESULTS: In total, 1776 patients were included: 1077 with CVCs, 886 with PIVs, and 187 with both. The most common diagnoses were large B-cell lymphomas, followed by Hodgkin lymphoma, and then T-cell lymphoma. In total, there were 5464 and 4049 treatment cycles in the CVC and PIV cohorts, respectively. There was one definite case of extravasation with PIV use (incidence rate 0.19 events per 1000 infusion-cycles), compared to no cases with CVC use. PIV use was more commonly associated with flare, phlebitis, and pain, whereas CVC use was more commonly associated with deep vein thrombosis; other complications were not different between cohorts. Rates of extravasation and other complications were low in both PIV and CVC cohorts.

CONCLUSION: Altogether, PIVs represent a viable modality for patients with lymphoma requiring anthracycline-based chemotherapy.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Peripheral intravenous catheters (PIVs) for the administration of anthracycline-based chemotherapy have the potential risk of vascular and tissue injury due to extravasation of vesicant agents. Central venous catheters (CVCs) are frequently utilized to mitigate this. This multicenter retrospective real-world analysis (RWA) evaluated complications associated with PIVs versus CVCs for the administration of anthracycline-based chemotherapy in patients with lymphoma.

title: Functional Vulnerability and Long-Term Mortality in Adults with Ankle-Brachial Index-Defined Peripheral Artery Disease: An NHANES Cohort Study.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Functional limitations are common in peripheral artery disease (PAD), but the association of a brief self-reported functional-burden measure with objectively defined PAD and long-term mortality remains incompletely characterized.

METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2004 participants aged ≥ 40 years with ankle-brachial index (ABI), physical functioning, and linked mortality data. PAD was defined as minimum ABI ≤ 0.90. An NHANES-derived functional vulnerability index (NFVI; range 0-4) was constructed from difficulty walking a quarter mile, walking up 10 steps, stooping/crouching/kneeling, and standing for long periods. NFVI was intended as a brief functional-burden measure rather than a diagnostic frailty instrument. Survey-weighted models evaluated PAD status, NFVI, and mortality, with validated modified cardiovascular health (mCVH) used for additional adjustment.

RESULTS: The PAD NFVI cohort included 462 participants and 375 deaths. PAD was associated with high NFVI after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and mCVH (odds ratio [OR] 1.748, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.218-2.510; P = 0.005). In PAD participants, each 1-point higher NFVI was associated with all-cause mortality after adjustment for sociodemographic factors and minimum ABI (hazards ratio [HR] 1.095, 95% CI 1.017-1.179; P = 0.017). After additional mCVH adjustment, the continuous association was attenuated (HR 1.075, 95% CI 0.993-1.165; P = 0.075), whereas high NFVI remained associated with mortality (HR 1.346, 95% CI 1.026-1.767; P = 0.032). Complete-case selection was substantial (462/647 PAD participants), with marked differences between included and excluded participants, particularly in age, potentially limiting generalizability.

CONCLUSION: Functional vulnerability was more common among adults with ABI-defined PAD and was associated with long-term all-cause mortality. These findings demonstrate an epidemiologic association rather than the clinical utility, validation, or incremental prognostic value of NFVI and do not establish a clinically meaningful NFVI mortality threshold. Prospective PAD-specific validation and comparison with established frailty measures are required before clinical use.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Functional limitations are common in peripheral artery disease (PAD), but the association of a brief self-reported functional-burden measure with objectively defined PAD and long-term mortality remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: We analyzed National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2004 participants aged ≥ 40 years with ankle-brachial index (ABI), physical functioning, and linked mortality data. PAD was defined as minimum ABI ≤ 0.90.

title: Effects of Endovascular Repair Timing on the Outcomes of Type B Aortic Dissection in an Asian Multicenter Cohort.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study assessed thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) timing and its impact on outcomes in type B aortic dissection (TBAD).

METHOD: This multicenter retrospective study included 247 patients who underwent TEVAR for TBAD between 2011 and 2018, using data from the Chang Gung Research Database. Primary outcomes were in-hospital and postdischarge mortality.

RESULTS: The study included 47, 122, and 78 patients with hyperacute (<1 day), acute/subacute (1-90 days), and chronic (>90 days) TBAD, respectively. Chronic TBAD had more aortic expansion before TEVAR (0% vs. 6.6% vs. 17.6%; P = 0.001). In-hospital mortality was highest in hyperacute TBAD (17%) and lowest in chronic TBAD (6.4%; adjusted P for trend = 0.036); conversely, long-term mortality was highest in chronic TBAD (12.3%) and lowest in hyperacute TBAD (0%; adjusted P for trend = 0.017). A restricted cubic spline model showed that delayed intervention beyond 90 days is associated with increasing long-term mortality risk. Among secondary outcomes, delayed TEVAR was associated with more aortic, cardiovascular, infection-related deaths, and residual aneurysms (adjusted P for trend = 0.039, 0.012, 0.048, and 0.006, respectively).

CONCLUSION: TEVAR may lead to unfavorable outcomes in hyperacute and chronic TBAD. Delayed TEVAR in chronic TBAD is associated with adverse aortic remodeling and rising long-term mortality. TEVAR before the chronic phase could be considered to improve short-term and long-term outcomes.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: This study assessed thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) timing and its impact on outcomes in type B aortic dissection (TBAD). METHOD: This multicenter retrospective study included 247 patients who underwent TEVAR for TBAD between 2011 and 2018, using data from the Chang Gung Research Database. Primary outcomes were in-hospital and postdischarge mortality.

title: Guideline-to-Practice Gap in Ankle-Brachial Index Screening Among Inpatients with Newly Documented Lower Extremity Wounds.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is common and underdiagnosed. Hospitalized patients with lower extremity wounds may represent a missed opportunity for recognition. This study described inpatient ankle-brachial index (ABI) screening patterns in this population.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included adults admitted to 2 hospitals within a single urban academic health system in 2025 with a new lower extremity wound documented in nursing wound flowsheets. Recent screening was defined as ABI testing performed during the index hospitalization or within 1 year prior to admission. Patient and admission characteristics were compared by screening status, and logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with screening. Wound location and noninvasive vascular testing results were summarized descriptively.

RESULTS: Among 2,244 inpatients with newly documented lower extremity wounds, 343 patients (15.3%) were screened with ABIs. Screened patients were younger (65 vs.69 years; P < 0.001) and had a higher burden of atherosclerotic or diabetic comorbidities. After multivariable adjustment, pre-existing PAD (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 2.79; P < 0.001), diabetes mellitus (aOR, 2.72; P < 0.001), and end-stage renal disease (aOR, 1.60; P = 0.021) were independently associated with ABI screening. Female sex was associated with lower odds of screening (aOR, 0.73; P = 0.045). Compared with medicine or hospitalist services, admission to general surgery/acute care surgery (aOR, 2.15; P = 0.002) and vascular surgery (aOR, 4.29; P < 0.001) was associated with higher odds of screening. Screening proportions were 23.6% for toe wounds, 20.6% for ankle/Achilles wounds, 19.9% for foot/heel wounds, and 12.8% for lower leg wounds. Among screened patients with available measurements, 50.4% had an abnormal ABI, 63.8% had an abnormal TBI, and 69.0% had at least 1 abnormal ABI or TBI.

CONCLUSION: PAD screening was performed in a minority of hospitalized patients with newly documented lower extremity wounds and was associated with recognized vascular risk factors and admitting service. Abnormal physiologic testing was common among screened patients. Standardized wound-triggered screening pathways may reduce missed opportunities for vascular evaluation.

title: Long-Term Outcomes of Primary Femoropopliteal Stents: A Retrospective Multicenter Experience and the Role for a Doppler Ultrasound Surveillance Program.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a significant global health concern. Endovascular revascularization is frequently used for symptom control and limb salvage in patients with femoropopliteal PAD. However, restenosis, often necessitating reintervention, remains a challenge. This study performs a retrospective outcomes analysis to suggest which patient populations may benefit from a Doppler ultrasound (DUS) surveillance program in improving primary patency and amputation-free survival following femoropopliteal stenting in patients with PAD.

METHODS: A multicenter, retrospective cohort study was conducted using data from patients who underwent femoropopliteal stenting between January 2015 and April 2023 within a vascular network with 6 hospital sites. Data were collected from 238 stents in 220 patients. Demographics, stent characteristics, and surveillance protocols were analyzed. Cox proportional hazards and logistic regression models were used to identify risk factors for primary patency and amputation-free survival. Kaplan-Meier survival curves were generated for both outcomes. Descriptive statistics were used to compare outcomes between suprapopliteal and infrapopliteal stents.

RESULTS: A total of 238 stents were inserted in a population in which 28.6% were women, with the median age of 72.5 ± 11.5 years. In 74.8% (178) of cases, patients presented with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). Primary patency rates at 30 days, 6 months, 1 year, 3 years, and 5 years were 90%, 67.7%, 51.2%, 26.6%, and 11.7%, respectively. The average amputation-free survival was 3.2 years. Cox regression identified CLTI (hazard ratio, 6.37, P = 0.001), type 1 diabetes mellitus (hazard ratio, 3.16, P = 0.006), and female sex (hazard ratio, 1.69, P = 0.037) as significant predictors of loss of primary patency. Drug-eluting stents and diabetes were associated with poorer amputation-free survival.

CONCLUSION: The study illustrates a cohort of high-risk patients, particularly those with CLTI and diabetes, who may benefit from future enrollment in an enhanced DUS surveillance program targeted to improve long-term outcomes. However, further research is required to explore the clinical effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, and implementation feasibility of such programs in clinical practice.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a significant global health concern. Endovascular revascularization is frequently used for symptom control and limb salvage in patients with femoropopliteal PAD. However, restenosis, often necessitating reintervention, remains a challenge.

title: Medial Arterial Calcification in Diabetes-Related Foot Disease: An Arterial-Wall Dimension Uncharacterized in Current Limb Staging.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To synthesize the evidence on medial arterial calcification (MAC) in diabetes-related foot disease, addressing its arterial-wall phenotype, effects on hemodynamic assessment, prognostic associations, and its potential role in limb staging.

METHODS: Narrative review of clinical, imaging, pathological, and mechanistic literature identified through targeted database searches, interpreted with reference to the Wound, Ischemia and foot Infection (WIfI) classification and the Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS).

RESULTS: MAC is common in diabetes-related foot disease, particularly with chronic kidney disease, and is an arterial-wall phenotype distinct from intimal atherosclerosis. An elevated ankle-brachial index is uninterpretable, and a reference-range value does not exclude peripheral artery disease. Across cohorts of differing design and definition, MAC has been consistently associated with major amputation, delayed wound healing, and mortality, in line with a systematic review of 51 calcification-scoring studies; the 5-point pedal score has been externally validated, and associations persisted after adjustment for WIfI stage. Model comparison in one cohort suggests incremental information, but discrimination, calibration, and reclassification beyond established staging have not been reported. Neither WIfI nor GLASS characterizes arterial-wall phenotype.

CONCLUSION: The consistency and reproducibility of the prognostic evidence justify formal consideration of MAC in forthcoming revisions of limb-staging systems and guidelines. Incremental-value analyses should accompany that evaluation and inform the form of any modifier rather than delay it. One concrete route is to use MAC as a qualifier of the reliability of the WIfI ischemia grade in the individual limb.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: To synthesize the evidence on medial arterial calcification (MAC) in diabetes-related foot disease, addressing its arterial-wall phenotype, effects on hemodynamic assessment, prognostic associations, and its potential role in limb staging. METHODS: Narrative review of clinical, imaging, pathological, and mechanistic literature identified through targeted database searches, interpreted with reference to the Wound, Ischemia and foot Infection (WIfI) classification and the Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS). RESULTS: MAC is common in diabetes-related foot disease, particularly with chronic kidney disease, and is an arterial-wall phenotype distinct from intimal atherosclerosis.

title: Brachial Plexus Injuries from Overhead Arm Positioning During F/BEVAR: A Case Series and Call for Standardized Technique.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Overhead arm positioning during fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) may improve imaging quality and reduce procedural radiation dose. Elevated arm positioning during general anesthesia, however, may result in risk for nerve symptoms. The aim of this study was to assess the occurrence of upper extremity symptoms (UES) after overhead arm positioning during F/BEVAR.

METHODS: All consecutive patients undergoing F/BEVAR performed with bilateral overhead arm positioning at Uppsala Univerity Hospital between 2023 and 2025 were included in this retrospecive cohort study. Neutral head position, padded overhead support, and abduction limited to ≤90° were used in accordance with standardized positioning protocols. Demographic, comorbidity, and procedural data were accessed from the clinical records. The primary aim was to evaluate the rate of postoperative UES and brachial plexus injury (BPI). In cases with BPI, neurological consultation and rehabilitation outcomes were assessed.

RESULTS: Among 67 patients who underwent F/BEVAR with bilateral overhead arm position, 6 patients (9.0%) developed postoperative UES. Two patients (3.0%) had neurologist-confirmed BPI; one developed bilateral palsy with partial recovery after 8 weeks, whereas the other developed unilateral palsy with complete recovery by 3 months. Neither patient required surgical intervention, The remaining 4 patients (6.0%) experienced minor transient UES. There was no difference in baseline parameters between patients with and without UES. Urgent repair was more frequent among patients experiencing any UES than among those without UES (50.0% vs. 9.8%; P = 0.028). Both patients with BPI underwent procedures lasting >180 min. Procedural technical success was 98.5%, and in-hospital mortality 1.5%.

CONCLUSION: Bilateral overhead arm positioning during F/BEVAR was associated with a measurable incidence of UES. Although most symptoms were transient and resolved without intervention, clinically significant BPI occurred in a small proportion of patients despite standardized positioning. These findings support cautious and selective use of prolonged overhead arm positioning and warrant prospective evaluation of safe positioning duration and patient-related susceptibility.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Overhead arm positioning during fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) may improve imaging quality and reduce procedural radiation dose. Elevated arm positioning during general anesthesia, however, may result in risk for nerve symptoms. The aim of this study was to assess the occurrence of upper extremity symptoms (UES) after overhead arm positioning during F/BEVAR.

title: One-Year Sac Regression after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair Is Not Always Associated with Favorable Outcomes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: It is not clear whether 1-year sac regression after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) indicates the completion of treatment. The purpose of our study is to identify the association between 1-year sac behaviors and clinical outcomes and specifically whether it is safe to extend follow-up intervals for patients with 1-year sac regression.

METHODS: This is a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 317 consecutive patients who underwent nonruptured EVAR from January 2011 to December 2020. All patients were stratified into three groups based on their 1-year sac behavior: sac regression (decrease in diameter of ≥ 5 mm), stable sac (<5 mm change), and sac expansion (increase in diameter of ≥ 5 mm). The primary outcome was late reintervention, including endovascular reintervention and open conversion (OC).

RESULTS: A total of 317 patients were enrolled based on sac status on 1-year follow-up imaging: 126 with sac regression, 177 with stable sacs, and 14 with sac expansion. Over a median follow up of 69.5 months, sac expansion was a significant risk factor for late reintervention compared to sac regression (hazard ratio [HR], 2.335; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.048-5.191; P = 0.047). However, the rate of late reintervention was not significantly lower in the sac regression group compared to the stable sac group (HR, 0.694; 95% CI, 0.383-1.258; P = 0.229). Among patients with sac regression at 1 year, 5.6% (7/126) required embolization due to endoleak (EL), and 3.2% (4/126) needed OCs.

CONCLUSION: Late reintervention rates did not differ significantly between patients with stable versus regressed sacs at 1 year. Patients with sac regression also require regular imaging surveillance to detect late complications.

The purpose of our study is to identify the association between 1-year sac behaviors and clinical outcomes and specifically whether it is safe to extend follow-up intervals for patients with 1-year sac regression. METHODS: This is a retrospective, single-center cohort study of 317 consecutive patients who underwent nonruptured EVAR from January 2011 to December 2020.

title: Early Morphological Changes in Superficial Varicose Veins after Endovenous Radiofrequency Ablation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To quantify early changes in untreated varicose tributaries and treated saphenous veins after isolated radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and to assess 3-month technical outcomes.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 133 patients undergoing RFA of the great saphenous vein (GSV; n = 120) or small saphenous vein (SSV; n = 13). The primary outcome was within-patient change in the largest untreated varicose tributary diameter from baseline to approximately 3 months. The same radiologist reassessed the anatomically documented site. We used paired analyses, bootstrap confidence intervals, and multivariable analysis of covariance with robust standard errors.

RESULTS: Median tributary diameter decreased from 14.2 mm (interquartile range [IQR], 10.5-21.0) to 11.0 mm (IQR, 7.4-14.2). The median within-patient reduction was 3.0 mm (IQR, 0.9-5.8; 95% bootstrap confidence interval [CI], 2.2-3.7; P < 0.001). Completion duplex ultrasonography (DUS) confirmed closure of the proximal treated saphenous segment and patency of the adjacent deep vein in all patients. At approximately 3 months, complete occlusion was present in 99 of 120 GSVs (82.5%) and all 13 SSVs. The remaining 21 GSVs had short-segment partial recanalization with residual reflux near the saphenofemoral junction; none had complete recanalization. In an exploratory adjusted analysis, diabetes mellitus was associated with a 1.15-mm larger 3-month GSV diameter (95% CI, 0.23-2.07; P = 0.015).

CONCLUSION: Isolated RFA was associated with an early reduction in untreated varicose tributary diameter. These anatomical findings suggest that reassessment before adjunctive tributary treatment may be reasonable; however, clinical benefit cannot be inferred without patient-reported outcomes. The association between diabetes and 3-month GSV diameter is hypothesis-generating.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 133 patients undergoing RFA of the great saphenous vein (GSV; n = 120) or small saphenous vein (SSV; n = 13). The primary outcome was within-patient change in the largest untreated varicose tributary diameter from baseline to approximately 3 months.

title: Immediate Intercostal Artery Opacification with Multi-Fenestrated Physician-Modified Endografts During Hybrid Aortic Repair: Early Clinical Experience.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extensive aortic coverage can compromise the spinal cord collateral network. We evaluated the preliminary technical feasibility of a multi-fenestrated physician-modified endograft (PMEG) during complex hybrid aortic repair and assessed immediate postoperative intercostal artery opacification.

METHODS: Six consecutive patients underwent single-stage hybrid repair combining open surgery and endovascular stent-graft implantation between July 2024 and February 2025. All underwent left subclavian artery revascularization. Approximately 3 mm fenestrations were distributed circumferentially over the distal half of the second endograft. Aortic coverage was measured along the postoperative three-dimensional computed tomography angiography (CTA) centerline. Completion aortographic counts represented bilateral intercostal artery pairs.

RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in all six patients. Median aortic coverage was 230.2 mm (range, 225.0-315.3). A median of 7.5 intercostal artery pairs (range, 7-9) lay within the covered segment, and a median of 5 pairs (range, 4-6) opacified on completion aortography. No spinal cord ischemia (SCI) or early endoleak was recorded. Two patients experienced stroke on postoperative day 3, with residual motor impairment at follow-up; one developed acute kidney injury. Median follow-up after discharge was 489 days (range, 379-575), with no reintervention, 30-day mortality or 1-year mortality. Available CTA showed stable endograft positioning without detected endoleak.

CONCLUSIONS: This six-patient hybrid series documents preliminary technical feasibility and immediate postoperative intercostal artery opacification. Direct flow through individual fenestrations, sustained branch patency, structural durability and SCI protection remain unconfirmed.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Extensive aortic coverage can compromise the spinal cord collateral network. We evaluated the preliminary technical feasibility of a multi-fenestrated physician-modified endograft (PMEG) during complex hybrid aortic repair and assessed immediate postoperative intercostal artery opacification. METHODS: Six consecutive patients underwent single-stage hybrid repair combining open surgery and endovascular stent-graft implantation between July 2024 and February 2025.

title: Sex-Based Outcomes after Carotid Artery Revascularization in Symptomatic Patients: A Multicenter Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex-based differences in outcomes after carotid revascularization remain poorly defined in symptomatic patients. We aimed to compare short and long-term outcomes between men and women with symptomatic carotid artery disease who underwent carotid revascularization across a 10-year period in 3 stroke centers.

METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on a consecutive series of cases between 2016 and 2026. Cases included patients presenting with stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), or amaurosis fugax attributable to ipsilateral carotid artery stenosis within 6 months prior carotid endarterectomy (CEA), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), or transfemoral carotid artery stenting (TFCAS). Patients with prior neck radiation were excluded. Primary outcomes were stroke, TIA, myocardial infarction (MI), and death within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included long-term stroke, TIA, MI, death, restenosis, and reintervention. Both primary and secondary outcomes were analyzed individually and as a composite end point. To account for sex-based differences and vulnerable plaque feature burden, a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) analysis was performed among patients with available magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging.

RESULTS: A total of 822 procedures were performed (men: 571, 69.5%; women: 251, 30.5%) with a mean age of 73.2 ± 9.2 years. Procedure distribution was similar between groups (CEA: 69.4% vs. 70.9%; TCAR: 6.1% vs. 5.6%; TFCAS: 24.5% vs. 23.5%, P = 0.89). Demographics and comorbidities were otherwise comparable between groups. Women had higher total cholesterol (185.9 ± 50.1 vs. 158.1 ± 43.4 mg/dL, P < 0.01), high density lipoprotein (56.8 ± 18.1 vs. 45.9 ± 15.2 mg/dL, P < 0.01), and low density lipoprotein (101.5 ± 45.4 vs. 86.3 ± 38.0 mg/dL, P < 0.01); however, the low density lipoprotein/high density lipoprotein ratio was not significant. Medication regimens were similar between groups, except estrogen use, which was exclusive to women (4.0%, P < 0.01). Symptom presentation was comparable for stroke (49.0% vs. 48.6%, P = 0.91), TIA (32.0% vs. 33.5%, P = 0.69), and amaurosis fugax (22.1% vs. 20.7%, P = 0.67). At 30 days, the composite of stroke, TIA, MI, and death was similar (4.2% vs. 4.0%, P = 0.88), with no statistically significant differences in ipsilateral stroke (2.5% vs. 1.6%, P = 0.61), TIA (0.7% vs. 1.6%, P = 0.23), MI (0.5% vs. 0.0%, P = 0.25), or mortality (0.5% vs. 1.2%, P = 0.30). On long-term follow-up at 3.3 ± 2.6 years, the composite outcomes remained comparable (24.2% vs. 24.3%, P = 0.97), as were ipsilateral stroke (3.7% vs. 5.2%, P = 0.32), TIA (5.1% vs. 4.0%, P = 0.50), MI (2.6% vs. 3.6%, P = 0.45), mortality (17.5% vs. 19.1%, P = 0.58), restenosis (4.9% vs. 7.2%, P = 0.19), and reintervention rates (2.5% vs. 4.8%, P = 0.08). In the PSM cohort (men: 91, women: 91, N = 182), the 30-day (3.3% vs. 2.2%, P = 1.00) and long-term (34.1% vs. 31.9%, P = 0.88) composite outcome of stroke, TIA, MI, and death were similar. Restenosis (4.4% vs. 7.7%, P = 0.54), and reintervention (1.1% vs. 6.6%, P = 0.12) were also not statistically significantly different between groups.

CONCLUSION: No statistically significant sex-based differences were identified in 30-day or long-term outcomes after CEA, TCAR, or TFCAS across a 10-year period at 3 high-volume stroke centers. Furthermore, on propensity score matching of our highest risk patient population with vulnerable plaque features did not affect their short- and long-term outcomes.

We aimed to compare short and long-term outcomes between men and women with symptomatic carotid artery disease who underwent carotid revascularization across a 10-year period in 3 stroke centers. METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on a consecutive series of cases between 2016 and 2026.

title: Insulin dependence erodes the cardiac and survival advantage of asymptomatic status after carotid revascularization.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is associated with adverse outcomes after carotid revascularization, with insulin dependence conferring risk beyond DM alone. How this risk varies by symptom status and intervention type remains unclear. We evaluated the independent association of insulin-dependent DM (IDDM) and non-IDDM with 30-day and 1-year outcomes after carotid endarterectomy, transcarotid artery revascularization, and carotid artery stenting, stratified by symptom status.

METHODS: The Vascular Quality Initiative registry was queried for carotid interventions performed between January 2005 and January 2025. Patients were stratified by insulin-dependence and symptom status at presentation. End points were 30-day and 1-year myocardial infarction (MI), ipsilateral stroke, all-cause mortality, ipsilateral stroke or death, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; MI, ipsilateral stroke, or mortality). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, clinical, and procedural covariates estimated odds ratios (ORs).

RESULTS: Of 275,668 patients meeting inclusion criteria, 73,582 (26.7%) had DM: 44,041 (59.9%) non-IDDM and 29,541 (40.1%) IDDM. At 30 days, there were 1645 MIs, 2051 ipsilateral strokes, 1806 deaths, 3626 strokes or deaths, and 5029 MACE; at 1 year, 2378 MIs, 2924 ipsilateral strokes, 8269 deaths, 10,750 strokes or deaths, and 12,646 MACE, respectively. Controlling for comorbidities and procedure type, IDDM was independently associated with elevated odds of 30-day MI (OR, 1.63), ipsilateral stroke (OR, 1.24), mortality (OR, 1.19), and MACE (OR, 1.19), but not ipsilateral stroke or death. Excess IDDM risk was concentrated among asymptomatic patients (30-day MACE: OR, 1.35 vs 1.07 in symptomatic patients; interaction P < .001). Asymptomatic IDDM patients had higher 30-day MI odds (OR, 1.54; P < .001) than symptomatic patients without DM, with equivalent 30-day MACE (OR, 1.05; P = .41) and higher 1-year MACE (OR, 1.19; P < .001). Relative to carotid endarterectomy, transcarotid artery revascularization, and carotid artery stenting were associated with higher 30-day ipsilateral stroke odds (OR, 2.10 and 1.93, respectively; P ≤ .01 for both) without differences in MI or mortality; an interaction with insulin dependence was nonsignificant for every end point.

CONCLUSIONS: Insulin-dependent, diabetes was independently associated with substantially elevated odds of MI, ipsilateral stroke, mortality, and MACE after carotid revascularization, with risk sustained at 1 year. For cardiac and survival end points, asymptomatic patients with IDDM occupied a risk stratum comparable with symptomatic patients without diabetes. Asymptomatic status may therefore not confer the same composite risk advantage in insulin-dependent patients, with the excess being cardiac- and survival-driven. These findings support more cautious, individualized counseling and shared decision-making for asymptomatic patients with IDDM and identify insulin dependence as a clinically important, currently underemphasized modifier of perioperative risk.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is associated with adverse outcomes after carotid revascularization, with insulin dependence conferring risk beyond DM alone. How this risk varies by symptom status and intervention type remains unclear. We evaluated the independent association of insulin-dependent DM (IDDM) and non-IDDM with 30-day and 1-year outcomes after carotid endarterectomy, transcarotid artery revascularization, and carotid artery stenting, stratified by symptom status.

title: Femoral artery access outcomes and technical considerations in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Femoral artery access in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (VEDS) poses unique technical challenges due to structurally fragile arteries. This study evaluated femoral access-related complications in patients with genetically confirmed-VEDS and sought to identify procedural and biologic factors that may inform access planning for endovascular procedures.

METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis of patients with pathogenic/likely pathogenic COL3A1 variants who underwent endovascular procedures requiring femoral artery access. Data were obtained from the global genetically confirmed-VEDS Natural History Study and a retrospective single center cohort. Demographics, genotype, procedural indication, access and closure techniques, access-related complications, and outcomes were abstracted from clinical record. Major access-related complications were defined as femoral artery dissection, pseudoaneurysm, rupture, or closure device failure requiring open operative repair.

RESULTS: A total of 117 femoral artery access sites were used in 105 endovascular interventions among 60 patients between 1989 and 2025. Median age at intervention was 39 years, and 53.3% of patients were male. Among 99 procedures with known access modality, 84 were performed percutaneously and 15 involved planned open femoral exposure. Manual compression was used in 33 percutaneous access sites, with no major access-related complications. Percutaneous closure devices were used in 39 access sites; major complications occurred in five access sites across five procedures, all requiring unplanned surgical exposure and repair. One additional percutaneous access site required unplanned open repair for access-related arterial injury and external iliac artery dissection before any closure device was attempted. Of percutaneous closure device failures, Perclose ProGlide (Abbott Vascular, Inc.) and StarClose (Abbott Vascular, Inc.) had the highest rate of failure (18.8% and 33.3%, respectively). Three of four affected patients had large amino acid substitutions or exon skip mutations; the remaining patient had a small amino acid substitution but underwent 16F sheath placement. No access-related complications occurred after planned open exposure.

CONCLUSIONS: Femoral artery access in VEDS requires deliberate individualized planning. In this cohort, manual compression for smaller-caliber access (≤6F) was associated with favorable outcomes, whereas major complications occurred predominantly following attempted percutaneous closure. Planned open exposure, despite use in procedures involving larger sheath sizes, was not associated with access-related complications and may warrant consideration in selected circumstances, including procedures requiring larger sheath sizes, known previous closure-related arterial injury, and high-risk genotypes.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Femoral artery access in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (VEDS) poses unique technical challenges due to structurally fragile arteries. This study evaluated femoral access-related complications in patients with genetically confirmed-VEDS and sought to identify procedural and biologic factors that may inform access planning for endovascular procedures. METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis of patients with pathogenic/likely pathogenic COL3A1 variants who underwent endovascular procedures requiring femoral artery access.

title: Contemporary patterns of lower extremity revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia in the United States: 2016-2022.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is a major contributor to morbidity and mortality. Although revascularization improves limb outcomes in CLTI, contemporary practice patterns and real-world outcomes remain poorly characterized, particularly considering the conflicting evidence from randomized trials regarding the optimal revascularization and nonoperative management strategies. Our study utilized National Inpatient Sample (NIS) data coupled with U.S. Census data to characterize the contemporary trends of incidence, revascularization approach, and in-hospital outcomes for adults hospitalized for CLTI.

METHODS: We utilized NIS data (2016-2022) to generate survey-weighted national estimates of U.S. adult hospitalizations for CLTI. Age-normalized incidence rates per 100,000 person-years were calculated using population denominators from the U.S. Census Bureau. Admissions with secondary diagnoses of trauma or arterial dissection were excluded. We evaluated the incidence of CLTI hospitalizations and the rates of in-hospital revascularization type (open, endovascular, or no revascularization), major amputation, and mortality. Outcomes by revascularization strategies (open vs endovascular) were stratified a priori by sex, frailty (Risk Analysis Index), diabetes status, and clinical presentation subgroups. The Mann-Kendall test was used to determine the monotonic temporal trends.

RESULTS: The analysis included 46,915 adult CLTI hospitalizations (mean age, 69.7 years; 40.0% women; 69.5% White patients). The overall CLTI incidence was 7.28 per 100,000 person-years, initially declining until nadir in 2020 with a reversal and steady increase thereafter. A total of 28,763 (61.3%) CLTI hospitalizations involved revascularization (n = 14,252 [49.5%] open and/or n = 16,950 [58.9%] endovascular). The proportion of open revascularization procedures decreased (Ptrend = 0.016), whereas the proportion of endovascular procedures remained stable (Ptrend = 0.368), and the number of hospitalizations without revascularization increased (Ptrend = 0.016) over time. The rates of endovascular revascularization increased among women, nonfrail patients, and patients presenting with rest pain (all Ptrend > 0.05). Overall, the rates of in-hospital amputation (n = 6270 [13.4%]) and mortality (n = 1086 [2.3%]) remained stable (Ptrend > 0.05). However, the proportion of patients discharged alive and without amputation increased the most substantially among those with hospitalization without revascularization (Ptrend = 0.007).

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides an contemporary analysis of U.S. hospitalizations for CLTI, demonstrating increasing rates following 2020. Overall, the in-hospital rates of open revascularization declined in favor of nonoperative strategies, corresponding with the greatest increase in alive discharges without amputations. The relative selection of endovascular strategies varied notably by sex, frailty, and clinical presentation. Our findings indicate the need for further investigation into the optimal selection of patients with CLTI and the coordinated integration of nonoperative care, including medical optimization, with revascularization strategies.

title: Revascularization of Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis: Cognitive Results of the CREST-2 Randomized Trials.
abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Studies show that asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis is associated with diminished cognition. Whether carotid revascularization leads to cognitive improvement is unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether carotid revascularization improves cognition.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Prespecified cognitive secondary outcomes of the CREST-2 randomized clinical trials of patients 35 years or older with 70% or greater asymptomatic carotid stenosis. Enrollment was December 2014 through July 2024, and follow-up ended July 2025. Five cognitive tests were administered before treatment and annually up to 4 years. Cognitive performances from 146 clinical sites were centrally assessed by telephone, blinded to treatment.

INTERVENTIONS: Two trials compared carotid stenting plus intensive medical management (CAS + IMM) with IMM alone and carotid endarterectomy plus IMM (CEA + IMM) with IMM alone.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Five cognitive tests, assessing learning, memory, executive function, attention, and processing speed, administered to all patients, were assessed for unadjusted and adjusted mean z scores using a linear mixed model. The minimal clinically important difference was 0.50 SD between treatment groups. The prespecified primary analysis was the fully adjusted composite z score at 4 years. Secondary analyses assessed the individual tests and at the test intervals.

RESULTS: Among 2366 US study patients, 2165 (91.5%) participated in cognitive assessments, 1078 in the CAS trial (529 CAS + IMM; 549 IMM alone) and 1087 in the CEA trial (543 CEA + IMM; 544 IMM alone); mean age was 70.1 years (SD, 7.7) and 37.8% were female. Following baseline, 4954 test batteries were administered for a mean of 2.24 (SD, 1.09) follow-up years. There were no treatment-related differences in the fully adjusted estimated composite z scores at 4 years for either the CAS trial (CAS + IMM, 0.22 [95% CI, 0.13 to 0.30] vs IMM alone, 0.18 [95% CI, 0.09 to 0.27]; between-group difference, 0.03 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.15]) or the CEA trial (CEA + IMM, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.17 to 0.33] vs IMM, 0.23 [95% CI, 0.15 to 0.32]; between-group difference, 0.02 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.14]). There were no significant differences between revascularization plus medical management vs IMM alone for any individual cognitive test.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In patients with severe asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis, revascularization with either CAS or CEA plus IMM, compared with IMM alone, did not significantly improve cognitive function at up to 4 years of follow-up.
englishSummary: IMPORTANCE: Studies show that asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis is associated with diminished cognition. Whether carotid revascularization leads to cognitive improvement is unclear. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether carotid revascularization improves cognition.

title: Revascularization in Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis With Hemodynamic Impairment and Cognitive Outcomes: The CREST-H Substudy of the CREST-2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cerebral hemodynamic impairment in patients with asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis is associated with reduced cognition. It is uncertain whether revascularization might be an effective treatment for cognitive impairment in these patients.

OBJECTIVE: To test whether any cognitive benefit from revascularization of high-grade, asymptomatic ICA stenosis varies based on the degree of baseline cerebral hemodynamic impairment.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This substudy was conducted within a multicenter phase 3 randomized clinical trial. Adults (aged 35-86 years) without dementia with eighth-grade education or higher and unilateral asymptomatic ICA stenosis greater than or equal to 70% were enrolled from January 2018 to July 2024 at 61 sites in North America (last follow-up in July 2025). Of 607 participants screened from 2485 in CREST-2, 392 were enrolled. Magnetic resonance or computed tomographic perfusion imaging tested for baseline hemodynamic impairment defined by delayed time-to-peak (TTP) arrival of intravenous contrast in the hemisphere ipsilateral minus contralateral to the stenotic artery.

INTERVENTION: Carotid revascularization (endarterectomy or stenting) plus intensive medical management (IMM) vs IMM alone.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the difference in composite cognitive z score over 1 year based on 5 cognitive tests. The primary analysis tested for an interaction between treatment group (revascularization vs IMM alone) and degree of baseline hemodynamic impairment among those with reduced baseline cognition (cognitive z score ≤-1.0 SD).

RESULTS: Of 392 participants enrolled (mean age, 71 years; 125 [32%] females), 61 were excluded for missing baseline imaging and 40 for missing cognitive examinations or other covariates, leaving 291 with complete data. Fifty-one had reduced cognition at baseline (25 in the revascularization group and 26 in the IMM alone group). TTP ranged from no interhemispheric TTP delay to a more-than-2-second delay. Mean (SD) cognitive z scores were -1.36 (0.51) at baseline and -1.17 (0.47) at 1 year in the revascularization group and -1.34 (0.83) at baseline and -1.01 (0.97) at 1 year in the IMM alone group. The primary analysis showed no difference in cognition by treatment group over 1 year, adjusting for treatment group × hemodynamic status interaction and other covariates (adjusted difference in cognitive z score, -0.15 SD [95% CI, -0.54 to 0.24]). The interaction was not significant (β estimate = 0.018 [95% CI, -0.025 to 0.061]; P = .40).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this substudy of a randomized clinical trial, there was no differential effect of revascularization vs IMM alone on cognition over 1 year by cerebral hemodynamic status among those with baseline reduced cognition, suggesting that revascularization does not improve cognitive dysfunction by restoring flow to the brain in chronic asymptomatic carotid stenosis.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03121209.

It is uncertain whether revascularization might be an effective treatment for cognitive impairment in these patients. OBJECTIVE: To test whether any cognitive benefit from revascularization of high-grade, asymptomatic ICA stenosis varies based on the degree of baseline cerebral hemodynamic impairment.

title: Update of a living network meta-analysis comparing noncompounded 1% polidocanol endovenous microfoam (Varithena) ablation versus endovenous thermal ablation in chronic venous insufficiency.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: We previously published a network meta-analysis showing no statistically significant difference between commercially manufactured 1% polidocanol endovenous microfoam (PEM) and endovenous thermal ablation (ETA) for vein closure or deep vein thrombosis, when PEM was distinguished from physician-compounded foam. This living network meta-analysis updates the previous analysis comparing the effectiveness and safety of PEM ablation vs ETA for the primary treatment of adult patients with venous insufficiency caused by lower-extremity truncal vein incompetence.

METHODS: Systematic review searches following the prespecified protocol were conducted quarterly through March 2026. No changes were made to selection criteria. Vein closure, deep venous thrombosis, and ulcer healing were summarized as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). A composite outcome of disease-specific quality of life (QoL) or symptom improvement scales was summarized with Hedges' g standardized mean difference.

RESULTS: The updated search yielded 507 new citations and 11 new eligible studies, for a total of 24 studies (235,413 patients). PEM was not statistically different from ETA for vein closure (OR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.42-1.21). A sensitivity analysis at longest follow-up (mean, 28 months; range, 12-72 months) showed similar results (OR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.45-1.11). There was no evidence of increased deep venous thrombosis risk with PEM vs ETA (OR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.29-2.43). Post-treatment improvement in disease-specific QoL or venous insufficiency symptoms showed no statistically significant difference between PEM and ETA (Hedges' g standardized mean difference, 0.04; 95% CI, -0.16 to 0.25), though the network was not fully connected. Finally, ulcer healing data was limited, but an exploratory analysis found no evidence of a statistically significant difference.

CONCLUSIONS: This living network meta-analysis update reinforced the original findings that 1% PEM is not statistically different from ETA for venous closure or deep venous thrombosis in the treatment of chronic venous insufficiency, and adds new preliminary information on outcomes relevant to the patient experience. There was no evidence of a statistically significant difference between PEM ablation and ETA for a composite of disease-specific QoL and symptom improvement, or for ulcer healing. The living approach maintains rigor and efficiently keeps evidence current as new studies emerge.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: We previously published a network meta-analysis showing no statistically significant difference between commercially manufactured 1% polidocanol endovenous microfoam (PEM) and endovenous thermal ablation (ETA) for vein closure or deep vein thrombosis, when PEM was distinguished from physician-compounded foam. This living network meta-analysis updates the previous analysis comparing the effectiveness and safety of PEM ablation vs ETA for the primary treatment of adult patients with venous insufficiency caused by lower-extremity truncal vein incompetence. METHODS: Systematic review searches following the prespecified protocol were conducted quarterly through March 2026.

title: Variation and temporal trends in Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group billing for carotid endarterectomy across Vascular Quality Initiative centers.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospitals use Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) coding to bill for each admission, with higher payment provided for those with complications or comorbidities (CCs) or major CCs (MCCs). We analyzed variation in MS-DRG coding for carotid endarterectomy (CEA) across Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) centers to identify opportunities for improvement.

METHODS: We matched CEA cases in the VQI registry with Medicare claims data from 2013 through 2023. A multivariable stepwise logistic regression model was created to identify variables associated with CC or MCC billing (with odds ratios [ORs]). We examined variations in CC or MCC billing percentages among centers and applied a multivariable model to compare observed-to-expected (O:E) CC or MCC billing rates to adjust for patient differences. Billing trends over time were analyzed using linear regression.

RESULTS: Among 75,064 primary CEA admissions for Medicare beneficiaries, 39.5% were billed with CCs or MCCs (31.1% CCs, 8.4% MCCs) and 60.5% without. Eleven VQI clinical variables that indicated CCs were significantly associated with CC or MCC billing: dialysis dependence (OR, 22.30), postoperative neurological events (OR, 5.25), length of stay >2 days (OR, 4.98), pre-existing heart failure (OR, 4.08), any postoperative complication (OR, 3.70), reoperation (OR, 3.65), preoperative neurological event (OR, 1.70), higher American Society of Anesthesiologists class (OR, 1.50), urgent/emergent procedure (OR, 1.28), postoperative intravenous blood pressure management (OR, 1.27), and institutional transfer (OR, 1.16). Across 371 VQI centers, CC or MCC billing rates varied 5.6-fold, ranging from 15% to 84% of admissions. After risk adjustment, observed-to-expected ratios still demonstrated 4.2-fold variation, from 0.45 to 1.90 across centers. The observed rate of CC or MCC billing increased over time, from 35.5% in 2015 to 46.1% in 2023 (P < .001). In contrast, the expected adjusted rates predicted by the model remained stable (P = .269). A discrete inflection point was identified between 2016 and 2017, after which higher billing rates persisted (P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: Substantial variation exists for MS-DRG billing for CEA across VQI centers. Billing rates for CCs or MCCs increased from 2013 through 2023. These findings suggest potential underbilling at some centers and overbilling at others. Leveraging Medicare-linked VQI registry data and the proposed model could help to improve coding and billing accuracy, optimize reimbursement, and reduce Medicare audit risk.

We analyzed variation in MS-DRG coding for carotid endarterectomy (CEA) across Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) centers to identify opportunities for improvement. METHODS: We matched CEA cases in the VQI registry with Medicare claims data from 2013 through 2023.

title: Patient-specific finite element modeling of image-derived shell morphoelastic growth: A general framework and application to stented aortic dissection.
abstract: Vascular pathology often manifests in complex shape evolution visualized by longitudinal computed tomography (CT) imaging. Growth and remodeling (G&R) frameworks have been integrated into finite element (FE) modeling to probe the mechanics underlying this progression, extending into patient-specific approaches. Their scalability and translatability, however, are limited by the computational burden associated with heterogeneous, anisotropic growth fields and through-thickness meshing. While existing shell growth formulations can mitigate this burden, they require nontrivial FE implementation especially in commercial softwares (e.g., Abaqus) and their efficacy in patient-specific geometries under complex loading is unclear. In this work, we present a general computational framework to implement shell morphoelastic growth computed directly from registered patient-specific CT images. This shell implementation is validated against solid 3D formulations, allows thickness tunability, and increases compatibility with CT surfaces. We demonstrate the robustness of this formulation through modeling post-operative growth in a patient-specific aortic dissection under stent-based loading. Results first show that complex stent-based loading can deform the shell dissection flap to reproduce post-operative geometry. The outer aortic wall is then given a growth field calculated from registration of 1-month and 5-year post-operative CT images, which is implemented along with stent-based loading and pressurization. Results from this model capture the trends in total and lumen morphological evolution observed at intermediate timepoints. These findings establish a general framework, validated with a patient-specific case study of aortic dissection, with the potential to expand to other complex systems, scale to larger patient populations, and apply G&R to clinical translation.

Growth and remodeling (G&R) frameworks have been integrated into finite element (FE) modeling to probe the mechanics underlying this progression, extending into patient-specific approaches. Their scalability and translatability, however, are limited by the computational burden associated with heterogeneous, anisotropic growth fields and through-thickness meshing.

title: Predictive value of combined cerebral blood volume index and systemic inflammation indices for 90-day functional outcomes following endovascular treatment in patients with acute ischemic stroke and proximal large vessel occlusion: machine learning model construction and population attributable fraction analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We investigated whether the cerebral blood volume (CBV) index and pretreatment systemic inflammatory indices (SIIs) provide complementary prognostic information for 90-day functional outcomes after successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for anterior circulation large vessel occlusion and evaluated the advantages of machine learning models in terms of prognostic outcomes and quantified adverse outcomes using the population attributable fraction (PAF).

METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation. SIIs were calculated from the first venous sample obtained at presentation, before intravenous thrombolysis, and before arterial puncture for EVT. Multivariate logistic regression and eight predictive algorithms were evaluated. PAF estimates were considered exploratory.

RESULTS: Among 474 patients, 41.6% and 28.5% achieved favorable and excellent outcomes, respectively. Higher CBV indices were more frequent among patients with favorable outcomes, whereas higher inflammatory indices were associated with worse outcomes. Logistic regression showed the highest AUC for mRS 0-2 (0.868, 95% CI 0.806-0.929), while SVM had the highest AUC for mRS 0-1 (0.839, 95% CI 0.764-0.915). The external validation AUCs were 0.816 and 0.802. PAF analysis indicated that improving the CBV index increased favorable and excellent outcomes by 97.2% and 74.8%, respectively, whereas reducing inflammatory overactivation improved them by 22.4%-39.7% and 51.2%-59.5%, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Baseline CBV index and pretreatment SII values provided complementary prognostic information after successful EVT. However, prospective validation in a broader population is required before clinical implementation.

METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation.

title: A Vascular Surgery and Primary Care Partnership for Improving Resident Training in Peripheral Artery Disease Management.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early diagnosis, establishment of best medical management, and timely specialty referral for patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD) remain ongoing challenges. In this study, we sought to identify gaps in internal medicine (IM) and family medicine (FM) residents' self-rated competency of PAD management and investigated whether an educational session led by vascular surgeons could promote recognition and confidence in patient care.

METHODS: A single educational session, featuring a PowerPoint presentation, hands-on training (pulse and Doppler examination), and open discussion, was offered to IM and FM residents on two separate occasions. A presession survey assessed self-rated knowledge, practices, attitudes, and medical training regarding PAD, followed by a truncated postsession survey. The responses were grouped as high versus moderate/low. Descriptive statistics and the McNemar Exact test were used for paired sample comparison.

RESULTS: Thirty-one residents completed both surveys (65% IM, 35% FM, 58% male, and 77% first- or second-year trainees). Presession data revealed gaps in knowledge with few residents rating their understanding as "high". Postsession, there was a significant increase across all measured areas (P < 0.001). Notably, improvements were seen in the number of residents who felt highly confident in diagnosing PAD (from 16.1% to 90.3%), using a vascular Doppler (6.5% to 83.9%), ordering noninvasive testing (from 6.5% to 83.9%), performing a lower extremity pulse exam (from 12.9% to 87.1%), managing PAD for amputation prevention (from 12.9% to 71.0%), and referring to a vascular specialist (from 25.8% to 83.9%).

CONCLUSION: Resident knowledge and confidence improved significantly as a result of a singular educational session. This collaborative model between vascular surgery educators and primary care residency programs demonstrates an adaptable framework that successfully addresses a gap in PAD management training.

In this study, we sought to identify gaps in internal medicine (IM) and family medicine (FM) residents' self-rated competency of PAD management and investigated whether an educational session led by vascular surgeons could promote recognition and confidence in patient care. METHODS: A single educational session, featuring a PowerPoint presentation, hands-on training (pulse and Doppler examination), and open discussion, was offered to IM and FM residents on two separate occasions.

title: Calibrated Microspheres versus Liquid Embolic Agents for Chronic Subdural Hematoma: A Single-Center Clinicoradiologic Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAe) is an effective treatment for chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH), but the optimal embolic agent remains debated. Landmark randomized trials predominantly used liquid embolics, although calibrated microspheres remain widely used. We compared clinicoradiologic outcomes after MMAe with 75 μm Embozene microspheres versus liquid embolics (n-butyl cyanoacrylate or Onyx 18).

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed single-agent MMAe for cSDH at a tertiary center (January 2019-January 2025). The embolized MMA was the unit of analysis; agent choice was discretionary. The efficacy cohort required 2-8 week imaging (n = 66); the safety cohort included all single-agent procedures (n = 67; 35 particle, 32 liquid). Primary outcomes were embolization failure and unplanned surgical evacuation. Secondary outcomes included early SDH thickness, midline shift, and latest modified Rankin scale (mRS).

RESULTS: Fifty patients underwent 66 embolizations (16 bilateral): 34 particle and 32 liquid. Embolization failure occurred in 5/34 versus 4/32, and unplanned evacuation in 3/34 versus 1/32; events were few and the comparison underpowered. Female patients were more frequent in the particle group (47% vs. 19%, P = 0.020). Early SDH thickness was 8 (6) versus 6 (6) mm (P = 0.340). The safety cohort had one fatal posterior-circulation infarct after Embozene (1/35 vs. 0/32) and no other periprocedural complications.

CONCLUSIONS: Embolization failure was similar between 75 μm Embozene and liquid embolics, while unplanned evacuation was numerically higher with particles. Given infrequent events, limited sample size, and baseline imbalances, agent selection may be individualized by anatomy, visualization, and operator experience.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Middle meningeal artery embolization (MMAe) is an effective treatment for chronic subdural hematoma (cSDH), but the optimal embolic agent remains debated. Landmark randomized trials predominantly used liquid embolics, although calibrated microspheres remain widely used. We compared clinicoradiologic outcomes after MMAe with 75 μm Embozene microspheres versus liquid embolics (n-butyl cyanoacrylate or Onyx 18).

title: Cause-Specific Endovascular Thrombectomy Time Windows in Basilar Artery Occlusion: ATTENTION Trial Post Hoc Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) outperforms best medical treatment (BMT) for basilar artery occlusion (BAO), but the influence of stroke cause on the time sensitivity of EVT remains unclear. We hypothesized nonatherosclerotic BAO would require earlier EVT, whereas atherosclerotic BAO-with chronic stenosis and more robust collaterals-would retain EVT benefit in extended windows. We conducted a post hoc 3-way interaction analysis of the ATTENTION trial (Trial of Endovascular Treatment of Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion) to explore cause-specific EVT time patterns.

METHODS: Using randomized ATTENTION trial data (36 Chinese centers, 2021-2022), patients were stratified by onset-to-puncture time (<6 versus ≥6 hours) and TOAST (Trial of ORG 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment) cause (atherosclerotic: large-artery atherosclerosis; nonatherosclerotic: cardioembolism/undetermined/other causes). The primary outcome was 90-day favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 0-3), with relative risk as the primary estimand; the 3-way interaction was tested via joint Wald test. A weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis served as an exploratory tool, with multivariable regression adjusting for confounders.

RESULTS: Among 340 patients (226 EVT+BMT, 114 BMT), for onset-to-puncture time <6 hours, patients with nonatherosclerotic BAO who received EVT achieved a significantly higher favorable outcome rate (46.7% versus 20.4%; relative risk, 2.29 [95% CI, 1.25-4.18]; P=0.007); the atherosclerotic group showed numerical outcome benefit (40.4% versus 26.1%, P=0.259). For onset-to-puncture time ≥6 hours, the numerical benefit in the atherosclerotic group increased from 14.3% to 30.6% (56.9% versus 26.3%; P=0.199), accompanied by ordinal modified Rankin Scale score improvement (common odds ratio, 3.30 [95% CI, 1.13-9.62]; P=0.029) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score reduction; the benefit in the nonatherosclerotic group decreased from 26.3% to 17.8% with loss of significance (39.5% versus 21.7%, P=0.341). The treatment time×cause interaction was not significant (P=0.662). The weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis identified a provisional 5.3-hour reference point in nonatherosclerotic BAO.

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with nonatherosclerotic BAO, atherosclerotic BAO appears less time-sensitive, potentially retaining EVT responsiveness over longer windows. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

title: Comparison of DOAC Versus VKA for Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cerebral venous thrombosis is an uncommon cause of stroke that primarily affects young adults. Several clinical trials and observational studies have compared vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) for treating cerebral venous thrombosis, but the small sample sizes limit the ability to draw firm conclusions.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing DOACs with VKAs for the treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis. Studies published between January 2007 and July 2025 were included. Prespecified subgroup analyses were conducted by study design, DOAC class (anti-factor Xa inhibitors versus direct thrombin inhibitors), and VKA. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk-of-Bias Tool 2 for randomized trials and the Risk of Bias in Nonrandomized Studies of Interventions for observational studies. Pooled risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs were calculated using random-effects models.

RESULTS: Fourteen studies (8 randomized clinical trials [RCTs] and 6 observational studies) were included. Among 3698 patients, 1669 (45.1%) received DOACs and 2029 (54.9%) received VKAs. Rates of recurrent venous thromboembolism (10.24% versus 10.99%), major bleeding (4.26% versus 6.18%), clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding (2.63% versus 1.66%), good functional outcomes (95.09% versus 89.25%), and mortality (3.37% versus 3.30%) were similar in DOACs and VKAs. Recurrent venous thromboembolism was similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.35-3.24]) and in the overall pooled analysis of all studies (RR, 0.92 [95% CI, 0.55-1.53]). Major bleeding did not differ between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.24-2.22]) or in the overall analysis (RR, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.44-1.25]; P=0.26). Clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was also comparable in RCTs (RR, 1.06 [95% CI, 0.25-4.48]) and overall (RR, 1.22 [95% CI, 0.38-3.86]). Good functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score of 0-2) were similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.00 [95% CI, 0.84-1.19]) and in the combined analysis of all studies (RR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93-1.11]). Mortality was similar between DOACs and VKAs in RCTs (RR, 1.15 [95% CI, 0.28-4.68]) and in the pooled analysis. When direct thrombin inhibitors were compared with factor Xa inhibitors, there were no significant differences in outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: DOACs demonstrated comparable efficacy and safety to VKAs in the treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis. These findings support the use of DOACs as a reasonable alternative.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Cerebral venous thrombosis is an uncommon cause of stroke that primarily affects young adults. Several clinical trials and observational studies have compared vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) with direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) for treating cerebral venous thrombosis, but the small sample sizes limit the ability to draw firm conclusions. METHODS: We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials and observational studies comparing DOACs with VKAs for the treatment of cerebral venous thrombosis.

title: Endovascular repair of a true profunda femoris aneurysm.
abstract: True aneurysms of the profunda femoris artery are exceedingly rare, comprising less than 1% of all peripheral artery aneurysms. Their diagnosis is often challenging because of their atypical anatomical location and nonspecific symptoms, and rupture carries substantial morbidity. We report a patient with a history of popliteal artery aneurysm thrombosis who was subsequently found to have a 3.9 cm true aneurysm of the right profunda femoris artery. The lesion was successfully treated endovascularly with overlapping nitinol stent grafts, achieving good technical and clinical results. This represents one of the few reported cases of a true profunda femoris artery aneurysm managed by endovascular exclusion.

title: An evaluation of a newly implemented stroke team activation protocol in Manitoba.
abstract:
PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to evaluate a revised stroke 25 protocol in Manitoba, which integrated Stroke Team Activation by the Virtual Emergency Care and Transfer Resource Service (VECTRS), and to determine whether its implementation reduced time to acute stroke treatment compared to the previous protocol.

METHODS: This retrospective chart review utilized Emergency Medical Services (EMS) data from the Winnipeg Fire Paramedic Service (WFPS) and hospital electronic medical records from the Winnipeg Health Sciences Centre (HSC), comparing 12 months before and 12 months after implementation of the revised Stroke 25 protocol. For each patient, the interval from EMS arrival at HSC to initiation of acute stroke treatment was calculated. Mean times to thrombolysis and EVT were compared between pre- and post-implementation cohorts.

RESULTS: In the pre-intervention cohort, 757 patients with suspected stroke were triaged to HSC, of whom 131 received Alteplase or Tenecteplase (TNK) and 33 underwent EVT. In the post- intervention group, 717 patients were triaged, with 110 receiving Alteplase/TNK and 30 undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). Mean time to thrombolysis decreased from 59.1 min pre- intervention to 52.8 min post- intervention, while mean time to EVT decreased from 92.2 min to 84.1 min, respectively.

CONCLUSION: Implementation of the revised Stroke 25 protocol was associated with modest reductions in absolute time to treatment for patients with acute ischemic stroke; however, while these differences were not statistically significant, the impact for these patients may still be clinically significant.
