title: Patient-Reported Outcomes and Disease-Specific Quality of Life After Surgical and Conservative Treatments for Lower Limb Varicose Veins: A Systematic Review.
abstract: Lower limb varicose veins are a common manifestation of chronic venous disease and can adversely affect physical functioning, symptom burden, and disease-specific quality of life (QoL). Although high ligation and stripping have traditionally been considered standard surgical approaches, conservative and minimally invasive options, such as compression therapy, sclerotherapy, and endovenous thermal or non-thermal techniques, have increasingly gained prominence. However, comparative evidence regarding patient-reported outcomes (PROMs) remains heterogeneous and dispersed across randomized trials. This systematic review aimed to evaluate randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between 2016 and 2026 that compared surgical with conservative or minimally invasive interventions for lower limb varicose veins, with particular emphasis on patient-reported and disease-specific QoL outcomes. The review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. PubMed/Medical Literature Analysis and Retrieval System Online (MEDLINE), Scopus, Web of Science, Excerpta Medica database (Embase), the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar were searched for eligible RCTs published from January 2016 to July 2026. Studies evaluating surgical versus conservative or minimally invasive management and reporting PROMs or disease-specific QoL outcomes were included. Methodological quality was evaluated using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool. Due to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively in accordance with Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) guidance. Fourteen RCTs met the eligibility criteria. Interventions included open surgery, endovenous laser ablation (EVLA), radiofrequency ablation (RFA), mechanochemical ablation (MOCA), cyanoacrylate adhesive closure, ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy (UGFS), and compression therapy. Improvements in disease-specific QoL and PROMs were reported from baseline in most treatment groups. However, these within-group improvements did not necessarily indicate superiority over alternative treatments. Between-group differences in QoL outcomes were generally small and inconsistent, although some trials reported differences in procedural pain, anatomical outcomes, or the need for re-intervention. Due to substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, the findings were synthesized narratively. Surgical, conservative, and minimally invasive approaches were associated with meaningful improvements in patient-reported and disease-specific QoL, with no consistent evidence demonstrating clear superiority of one modality. Treatment decisions should therefore incorporate anatomical suitability, patient preference, procedural morbidity, potential need for re-intervention, and healthcare resource considerations alongside QoL outcomes.

However, comparative evidence regarding patient-reported outcomes (PROMs) remains heterogeneous and dispersed across randomized trials.

title: Early and follow-up results of reinterventions for type 2 endoleak following endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm in the multicenter Reinterventions for Type 2 Endoleak study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Type II endoleak (T2EL) is frequent after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) repair and may require reintervention in selected patients. However, the optimal treatment strategy for durable resolution remains uncertain. This study aimed to retrospectively evaluate the perioperative and long-term outcomes of T2Els' reinterventions, both endovascular and open surgical, in a large patient cohort from 20 high-volume academic centers.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis of consecutive patients undergoing first reintervention for T2ELs was conducted across 20 centers over a 10-year period. Patients requiring concomitant treatment for other endoleak types were excluded. A total of 403 patients were included. Primary outcomes included technical success, 30-day AAA-related mortality and reintervention-free survival during follow-up. Secondary outcomes were perioperative complications, early reintervention, overall survival, freedom from aneurysm-related death and rupture, freedom from recurrent endoleaks, freedom from open conversion or semiconversion in patients previously treated endovascularly and sac behavior during follow-up. Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression analyses were performed to analyze follow-up results.

RESULTS: Patients were predominantly male (90%) with a mean age of 77 years. Reintervention was indicated for sac enlargement in 94.5% of cases; 4% presented with rupture. Median time from endovascular AAA repair to reintervention was 4.3 years. Lumbar arteries (55%) and the inferior mesenteric artery (35%) were the main sources. Endovascular treatment was performed in 86% and open conversion/semiconversion in 14%. Technical success was 96%, with 1% mortality and 4% major complications. Overall survival was 80.5% and rupture-free survival 79.2% at 5 years. Recurrent T2EL occurred in 64.2%, and reintervention-free survival was 48.3%. Endovascular group showed significantly lower freedom from reintervention rates when compared to open conversion/semiconversion group [42.4% vs 86.8%; standard error, 0.04 vs standard error, 0.05; P < .001; log-rank, 15.9]. Conversion/semiconversion after endovascular treatment occurred in 14%. No differences were recorded comparing different fabric materials of the endograft in terms of freedom for reintervention and freedom from open surgery. A sac diameter ≥7 cm at the time of reintervention predicted further reinterventions, whereas primary open treatment improved durability.

CONCLUSIONS: Reinterventions for T2ELs are safe, with satisfactory immediate technical success and low perioperative mortality. During follow-up, risks of rupture and AAA-related death remain low. However, the endoleak recurrence rate exceeds 60% at 5 years, necessitating reintervention in over 40% of patients. Early intervention for patients with a sac diameter approaching 7 cm can be suggested, whereas a primary open approach may be considered in low-risk patients.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Type II endoleak (T2EL) is frequent after endovascular abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) repair and may require reintervention in selected patients. However, the optimal treatment strategy for durable resolution remains uncertain. This study aimed to retrospectively evaluate the perioperative and long-term outcomes of T2Els' reinterventions, both endovascular and open surgical, in a large patient cohort from 20 high-volume academic centers.

title: Characterizing the Thrombotic Spectrum and Clinical Phenotypes of Tranexamic Acid-Associated Adverse Events: A Pharmacovigilance Study Based on the FAERS Database.
abstract: Tranexamic acid (TXA) is widely used to reduce bleeding in surgical, trauma, obstetric, and gynecological settings. However, concerns remain regarding TXA-associated thrombotic adverse events, and their phenotypic heterogeneity and clinical severity have not been comprehensively characterized. This study investigated TXA-associated thrombotic events using the Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) from 2004Q1 to 2026Q1. Thrombotic adverse events were identified using the Standardized MedDRA Query (SMQ) "Embolic and thrombotic events" and evaluated by disproportionality analysis based on reporting odds ratios (RORs). Qualifying thrombotic events were assigned to the SMQ vessel-type subgroups-arterial, vessel-type unspecified/mixed, and venous-and demographic characteristics, indications, clinical outcomes and time-to-onset were compared across subgroups; signal strength was further related to clinical severity. In all, 515 thrombotic cases associated with TXA and 26 selected thrombotic terms were found (arterial, 157; mixed, 168; venous, 190). Venous thromboembolism-pulmonary embolism (n = 128, ROR 13.94) and deep vein thrombosis (n = 58, ROR 9.09)-is the most frequent type and brings about the most severe and fatal consequences (death reported in 16.8% of venous versus 2.5% of arterial reports), whereas the strongest disproportionality signals were observed for rare site-specific events such as ovarian vein thrombosis (ROR 352.95) and cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (ROR 118.35). The three subgroups differed markedly in demographic and clinical characteristics: venous events occurred predominantly in women (73.7%) treated for menorrhagia (35.3%), whereas arterial events arose mainly in surgical or procedural settings (intravenous route 36.3%; surgery/prophylaxis 19.1%) and presented earliest after exposure [median time-to-onset (TTO) 0 versus 7 days]. Signal strength was not concordant with clinical severity across the thrombotic spectrum. These findings provide a deeper understanding of the thrombotic safety of TXA, indicate that the clinical background may influence the phenotypic differences among the different thrombotic types, and emphasize the necessity of enhanced attention and risk stratification in high-risk groups.

However, concerns remain regarding TXA-associated thrombotic adverse events, and their phenotypic heterogeneity and clinical severity have not been comprehensively characterized. This study investigated TXA-associated thrombotic events using the Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) from 2004Q1 to 2026Q1.

title: Initial Direct Oral Anticoagulants Versus Warfarin After Cerebral Venous Thrombosis: A Target Trial Emulation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Vitamin K antagonists have traditionally been used after cerebral venous thrombosis, whereas direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are increasingly prescribed. Whether DOACs are noninferior to warfarin for preventing 1-year symptomatic recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a registry-based target trial emulation in a bidirectional multicenter Chinese cerebral venous thrombosis registry (retrospective phase, 2015-2022; prospective phase, 2023-2025). Eligible patients were adults with imaging-confirmed cerebral venous thrombosis who initiated either a DOAC or warfarin within 30 days after diagnosis. Time zero was the date of the first oral anticoagulant prescription. The primary efficacy outcome was symptomatic recurrent VTE within 1 year. Propensity score overlap weighting was used, and weighted Fine-Gray models treated death as a competing event. The clinically acceptable noninferiority margin was defined as an absolute increase of 1.5 percentage points in 1-year recurrent VTE risk, corresponding approximately to a relative margin of 1.50 for the primary Fine-Gray analysis.

RESULTS: Among 2476 eligible patients, 942 initiated a DOAC (rivaroxaban, n=701; dabigatran, n=121; apixaban, n=113; edoxaban, n=7) and 1534 initiated warfarin. Within 1 year, symptomatic recurrent VTE occurred in 36 and 73 patients, respectively. The overlap-weighted 1-year recurrence risks were 3.74% and 5.47%, corresponding to a risk difference of -1.73 percentage points (95% CI, -3.76 to 0.30). DOAC treatment was associated with a lower subdistribution hazard ratio of 0.67 compared with that of warfarin ([95% CI, 0.37-1.21]; P=0.184), meeting the prespecified noninferiority criterion (P for noninferiority=0.004). Major bleeding was rare within 1 year (0 versus 1 patient). Clinical nonmajor bleeding occurred in 18 versus 34 patients, and any bleeding occurred in 48 versus 75 patients.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with cerebral venous thrombosis selected for oral anticoagulation, initial treatment with a DOAC met the noninferiority criterion relative to warfarin for the prevention of symptomatic recurrent VTE at 1 year. Findings regarding bleeding outcomes were exploratory and do not permit conclusions regarding comparative safety or equivalence.

Whether DOACs are noninferior to warfarin for preventing 1-year symptomatic recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain. METHODS: We conducted a registry-based target trial emulation in a bidirectional multicenter Chinese cerebral venous thrombosis registry (retrospective phase, 2015-2022; prospective phase, 2023-2025).

title: Caprini Score-Guided Venous Thromboembolism Prophylaxis in Spine Instrumentation Surgery: A Comparative Analysis of Mechanical vs. Pharmacomechanical Strategies Across Etiological Subgroups.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), encompassing deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), is a major source of morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing spine surgery. Although various risk factors for developing VTE have been identified, pharmacological prophylaxis is used selectively in spine surgery due to the risk of epidural hematoma. We report our institutional experience with VTE prophylaxis following spine instrumentation surgery across all surgical etiologies.

METHODS: A single-center retrospective cohort study of patients ≥18 years of age who underwent spine instrumentation surgery for degenerative, traumatic, or oncologic pathologies, and patients of all ages who underwent surgery for spinal deformity over a three-year period was performed. Caprini VTE risk score was used for individual risk stratification.

RESULTS: A total of 265 patients were included: degenerative (n=174, 65.7%), trauma (n=45, 17.0%), deformity (n=33, 12.5%), and tumor (n=13, 4.9%). The overall mean age was 46.1±17.5 years, and there were 133 male patients (50.2%). Significant differences existed across groups in age (Kruskal-Wallis H=97.4, p<0.001), index procedure characteristics, and VTE risk profiles. Mechanical prophylaxis alone was employed in 212 patients (80.0%), while 53 patients (20.0%) received combined pharmacomechanical prophylaxis. No patient (0%) in the mechanical-only group developed a perioperative VTE event or postoperative hematoma. One patient (1.9%) in the combined pharmacomechanical group developed a postoperative PE, arising in the context of a preoperative proximal DVT. Firth's penalized logistic regression identified polytrauma (OR 29.0, 95% CI 3.3-3835.0; p=0.001), Caprini score ≥7 (OR 8.8, 95% CI 3.8-20.9; p<0.001), and prior VTE history (OR 61.8, 95% CI 5.7-8406.4; p<0.001) as independent predictors of combined prophylaxis receipt.

CONCLUSION: Mechanical prophylaxis, implemented as part of a structured protocol that included sequential pneumatic compression devices and standardized postoperative care, was associated with low VTE risk following spine instrumentation surgery. Individualized risk stratification using validated tools such as the Caprini score, combined with selective pharmacomechanical prophylaxis in high-risk patients, may optimize outcomes in this population. Prospective multicenter studies are needed to validate these findings.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), encompassing deep venous thrombosis (DVT) and pulmonary embolism (PE), is a major source of morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing spine surgery. Although various risk factors for developing VTE have been identified, pharmacological prophylaxis is used selectively in spine surgery due to the risk of epidural hematoma. We report our institutional experience with VTE prophylaxis following spine instrumentation surgery across all surgical etiologies.

title: Admission C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio is associated with early major amputation after minor amputation in patients with infected foot wounds.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Minor amputation is commonly performed as a limb-salvage procedure for infected foot wounds; however, some patients experience early limb-salvage failure and progress to major amputation. Reliable biomarkers predicting early failure remain limited.

PURPOSE: To evaluate whether the admission C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) is associated with major amputation within 90 days after minor amputation in patients with infected foot wounds.

STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

METHODS: Patients who underwent minor amputation for infected foot wounds between March 2005 and September 2025 were retrospectively reviewed. Of 358 screened patients, 257 met the inclusion criteria. Admission CAR was calculated from C-reactive protein and serum albumin levels. The primary outcome was major amputation within 90 days. Univariable logistic regression and multivariable Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed. Predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.

RESULTS: Among 257 patients, 60 (23.3%) progressed to major amputation within 90 days. Higher admission CAR values were significantly associated with major amputation. CAR remained an independent predictor in multivariable analysis (hazard ratio 1.17; 95% confidence interval 1.05-1.31; p value = .004). Adding CAR improved the predictive performance of the baseline model (area under the curve .883 vs .810).

CONCLUSIONS: Admission CAR is a simple and independent factor associated with early major amputation after minor amputation and may help facilitate early risk stratification.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Minor amputation is commonly performed as a limb-salvage procedure for infected foot wounds; however, some patients experience early limb-salvage failure and progress to major amputation. Reliable biomarkers predicting early failure remain limited. PURPOSE: To evaluate whether the admission C-reactive protein-to-albumin ratio (CAR) is associated with major amputation within 90 days after minor amputation in patients with infected foot wounds.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear.

METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups.

RESULTS: Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows.

DISCUSSION: In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.

METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality.

title: Sex-related differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes of ischemic stroke following thrombectomy: data from an inverse propensity score weighted analysis.
abstract:
PURPOSE: We investigated sex differences in baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes among ischemic stroke patients undergoing endovascular treatment (EVT) within 24 h from last known well.

METHODS: Consecutive stroke patients who underwent a multimodal CT study protocol, EVT, and non-contrast CT follow-up imaging at 24 h were analyzed. We compared clinical and safety outcomes between males and females who received EVT in both the original population and a Propensity Score-balanced set. We performed univariable analyses to identify baseline neuroimaging, treatment workflow, and outcomes that differed between sexes. We used multivariable logistic regression to assess whether sex was associated with outcomes after adjusting for covariates.

RESULTS: Among 615 patients included in the analysis, 318 (51.7%) were female. Compared to females, males were younger (p <0.001), more independent before stroke (p <0.001), had a lower prevalence of atrial fibrillation (p < 0.001), and had lower internal carotid artery occlusion (p < 0.013). Compared to male, females had lower total hypoperfused tissue (109.3 mL [IQR=66.4-151.3] vs. 86.3 mL [IQR=43.4-132.3]; p<0.001), lower penumbra volumes (78.1 mL [IQR=43.9-114.8] vs. 47.7 mL [IQR=24.6-76.6], p<0.001), lower mismatch ratio (2.63 [IQR=1.86-4.49] vs. 3.67 [IQR=2.27-6.53]; p<0.001), and lower hypoperfusion intensity ratio (0.30 [IQR=0.18-0.50] vs. 0.38 [IQR=0.22-0.50]; p<0.001). In multivariable logistic regression analysis, sex was not an independent predictor of good clinical outcomes after EVT, although females died less than males and had a lower incidence of hemorrhagic transformation.

CONCLUSION: In our cohort of acute ischemic stroke treated with EVT, females showed an overall better perfusion profile at baseline compared to males, suggesting they may be slow progressors; however, this did not translate into better clinical outcomes. More data are needed to clarify the relationship between neuroimaging and sex, as well as the influence of other clinical factors on outcomes among patients undergoing EVT.

METHODS: Consecutive stroke patients who underwent a multimodal CT study protocol, EVT, and non-contrast CT follow-up imaging at 24 h were analyzed. We compared clinical and safety outcomes between males and females who received EVT in both the original population and a Propensity Score-balanced set.

title: Expressing Needs and Concerns During Nursing Care: An Ethnographic Study of Patients Undergoing Open Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repair.
abstract: This focused ethnographic study aimed to explore how patients expressed their needs and concerns during nursing care while undergoing planned open repair for abdominal aortic aneurysm. Fieldwork was conducted in a vascular surgery ward at a Danish university hospital between December 2024 and August 2025. Ten patients admitted for planned open repair were followed during their inpatient stay through participant observation. The ethnographic record comprised 85 hours of observation and was analyzed using Spradley's Developmental Research Sequence within a hermeneutic interpretive orientation. The overall cultural theme identified was "Expressing vulnerability while trying not to be a burden." This theme captures how physical recovery needs were more readily expressed, whereas emotional and existential concerns were softened, held back, or communicated through silence, humor, or reliance on family members. The included cases illustrate three domains: unspoken suffering as a barrier to well-being, family members' work in making patients' needs visible, and becoming dependent on nursing care as a patient. The findings show that patients undergoing open repair struggle to voice vulnerability directly during hospitalization. The study highlights the importance of nursing care that attends not only to explicit requests for help, but also to subtle verbal, embodied, and relational expressions of vulnerability.
englishSummary: This focused ethnographic study aimed to explore how patients expressed their needs and concerns during nursing care while undergoing planned open repair for abdominal aortic aneurysm. Fieldwork was conducted in a vascular surgery ward at a Danish university hospital between December 2024 and August 2025. Ten patients admitted for planned open repair were followed during their inpatient stay through participant observation.

title: ArtAssist sequential compression biomechanical device as a cost-dominant limb salvage strategy for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia: A decade and half, single-center cohort study with health economic and quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major lower limb amputation for no-option chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) costs the Irish Health Service Executive a median €88,820/patient; the long-term health economic and quality-adjusted survival evidence for ArtAssist Sequential Compression Biomechanical Device (SCBD) is lacking.

METHODS: Longitudinal cohort analysis of 428 patients with nonreconstructible CLTI managed with ArtAssist SCBD at a single tertiary center (January 2008-June 2025). Primary end points were limb salvage, cost-effectiveness vs primary amputation, and quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity. Kaplan-Meier analysis of limb salvage, multivariable Cox regression for major amputation, competing-risks analysis, and health economic modelling using contemporaneous cost data were performed.

RESULTS: Overall crude limb salvage, defined as freedom from major amputation, was achieved in 85% (294/347 patients). At last follow-up, 48% of patients were alive without major amputation. Kaplan-Meier estimated 5-year limb salvage at 95%. The cumulative incidence of major amputation at 5 years was 8% when accounting for death as a competing event, confirming durable limb preservation despite substantial long-term mortality in this elderly, comorbid population. Male sex, hypertension, and ischemic heart disease independently predicted major amputation or limb-salvage failure (hazard ratio: 1.70, 1.80, 1.71; all P ≤ .012). Comorbidity burden showed a dose-response relationship (P = .008). Ninety-day rental (€1373/patient) reduced total expenditure sixfold vs primary amputation (€5.3M vs €30.8M), saving €76,500/patient. Quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity yielded a gain of 3.37 quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) per patient; incremental cost-effectiveness ratio €21,900/QALY confirms a dominant strategy.

CONCLUSIONS: ArtAssist SCBD achieves a sixfold reduction in costs vs primary amputation, +3.37 QALYs/patient, and an incremental cost-effectiveness ratio of €21,900/QALY a dominant strategy supported by durable limb preservation, with 85% overall crude limb salvage and an estimated 5-year limb salvage of approximately 95% in the largest single-center cohort reported. These findings support universal commissioning of ArtAssist SCBD for nonreconstructible CLTI.

METHODS: Longitudinal cohort analysis of 428 patients with nonreconstructible CLTI managed with ArtAssist SCBD at a single tertiary center (January 2008-June 2025). Primary end points were limb salvage, cost-effectiveness vs primary amputation, and quality-adjusted time without symptoms or toxicity.

title: Early venous filling is associated with unfavorable outcomes in acute basilar artery occlusion after mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between early venous filling (EVF) on digital subtraction angiography and poor outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for acute basilar artery occlusion (ABAO).

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort included consecutive patients with ABAO who underwent MT at a comprehensive stroke center, achieved successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction grade ≥ 2b), and had 90-day functional follow-up data. Baseline clinical, imaging, and procedural variables were collected. Candidate predictors were assessed using univariable logistic regression. Four variables (fasting blood glucose, baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, EVF, and posterior circulation Alberta Stroke Program Early CT score) were included in Firth penalized multivariable logistic regression models for postprocedural malignant cerebellar edema (MCE) and poor prognosis (90-day modified Rankin Scale score > 2). Discrimination was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with internal validation by bootstrap optimism correction using 1,000 resamples.

RESULTS: Among 101 patients, 26 (25.7 %) had EVF, 29 (28.7 %) developed MCE, and 56 (55.4 %) had poor prognosis. With four predictors, the events-per-variable values were 7.25 for MCE and 11.25 for poor prognosis, using the smaller outcome category. EVF was associated with MCE (OR 34.650, 95 % CI 9.024-184.087; P < 0.001) and poor prognosis (OR 10.239, 95 % CI 2.889-54.718; P < 0.001) in the Firth models. For MCE, the apparent AUCs of the clinical model and the clinical model plus EVF were 0.804 and 0.944, respectively; the corresponding optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.788 and 0.926. For poor prognosis, the apparent AUCs were 0.762 and 0.836, and the optimism-corrected AUCs were 0.742 and 0.818. The optimism-corrected AUC increments with EVF were 0.138 for MCE and 0.076 for poor prognosis.

CONCLUSIONS: EVF was independently associated with MCE and poor prognosis after MT in patients with ABAO.

METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort included consecutive patients with ABAO who underwent MT at a comprehensive stroke center, achieved successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction grade ≥ 2b), and had 90-day functional follow-up data. Baseline clinical, imaging, and procedural variables were collected.

title: Optimizing Vessel Preparation in Femoropopliteal Lesions: Does the Chocolate Balloon Deliver on Its Clinical Promise?
abstract: The "leave nothing behind" paradigm using drug-coated balloons (DCBs) has reshaped femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease treatment, though clinical success remains heavily contingent upon optimal vessel preparation. In a recent issue of The American Journal of Cardiology, Li and colleagues address the limitations of conventional plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA) through a propensity score-matched analysis of 508 patients from the multicenter PROMISING registry, comparing specialized vessel preparation using the nitinol-constrained Chocolate balloon against POBA before DCB angioplasty. The Chocolate balloon significantly reduced the primary endpoint of bailout stenting (20.47% vs 29.92%) and facilitated larger final DCB diameters, though these acute mechanical advantages did not translate into statistically significant differences in clinical outcomes at 12 months. This commentary examines this striking "procedural-to-clinical paradox," highlighting how the potent antiproliferative effect of DCBs and the acute compensatory function of bailout stents may temporarily mask early clinical divergence. Given that cumulative mechanical failures of permanent metallic implants typically emerge beyond one year in hostile biomechanical environments, longer-term observation remains essential to capture the true clinical dividend of a stent-free strategy.

The Chocolate balloon significantly reduced the primary endpoint of bailout stenting (20.47% vs 29.92%) and facilitated larger final DCB diameters, though these acute mechanical advantages did not translate into statistically significant differences in clinical outcomes at 12 months.

title: In-hospital vascular surgery consultation is associated with improved follow-up and earlier identification of aneurysmal degeneration after acute type A aortic dissection.
abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Acute type A aortic dissections (TAADs) are historically managed by cardiac surgery. However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD.

METHODS: Patients who underwent surgical intervention for acute TAAD from 2014 to 2025 were identified. Patients who experienced death within 30-days or those with dissection limited to zone 0 or 1 were excluded. Vascular surgery evaluation and time to consultation (index-hospitalization, outpatient, and none) was documented. Follow-up was classified as complete, incomplete, or lost to follow-up (LTF) according to the frequency of contrasted thoracoabdominal imaging, consistent with clinical practice guidelines. Trends in completeness of follow-up were described. Demographics, anatomic/operative characteristics, and perioperative outcomes were compared between complete follow-up and incomplete follow-up/LTF groups. Long-term outcomes (such as aortic degeneration, planned secondary intervention, and survival) were assessed with Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 241 patients were included; 80% had vascular surgery consultation (70% inpatient, 30% outpatient) and 86% of consultations occurred within 1-year of index procedure. In total, 46% of patients had complete follow-up, 41% had incomplete follow-up, and 13% were LTF. In-hospital consultation increased by 58% over the study period. Demographics, comorbidities, and anatomic characteristics were similar between groups. Patients with complete follow-up had higher rates of complex arch repair (zone 1-3; complete 56% vs incomplete/LTF 27%; P < .001), were more likely to undergo genetic testing (complete 52% vs incomplete/LTF 18%; P < .001), in-hospital thoracic endovascular aortic repair extension (7% vs 2%; P = .028), and thoracic endovascular aortic repair extension within 3 months (complete 17% vs incomplete/LTF 5%; P = .002). In time-to-event analysis, complete follow-up was associated with more planned secondary interventions (complete 12% vs incomplete 5%; P = .007) and identified aneurysmal degeneration (32% vs 15%; P = .002) within 1-year of acute dissection. The long-term survival differed by completeness of follow-up; 1-year (complete 97% vs incomplete 97% vs LTF 91%), 3-years (complete 92% vs incomplete 95% vs LTF 81%; P = .021). There were no aortic-related deaths for patients with complete follow-up and five aortic-related deaths (5%) in patients with incomplete follow-up (P = .13). In-hospital vascular surgery consultation was associated with complete follow-up (hazard ratio, 2.87; 95% confidence interval, 1.6-5.1) and planned secondary interventions (hazard ratio, 2.07; 95% confidence interval, 1.1-3.9).

CONCLUSIONS: Vascular surgery consultation is associated with increased identification of aneurysmal degeneration, planned secondary interventions, and midterm survival. These data suggest that longitudinal vascular surgical care, starting with in-hospital consultation, is a critical component of care following acute TAAD and should be strongly considered to ensure appropriate postoperative surveillance and improve long-term patient outcomes.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Acute type A aortic dissections (TAADs) are historically managed by cardiac surgery. However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD.

title: Prevalence of Guideline-Recommended Genetic Testing in Patients at Risk for Heritable Thoracic Aortic Disease.
abstract: Heritable thoracic aortic diseases (HTAD) include genetic conditions that increase risk of thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts. We conducted a retrospective study using the TriNetX Research Network (2005-2025). Three guideline-based cohorts were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes: (1) thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, (2) family history of thoracic aortic disease, and (3) nonthoracic arterial aneurysms. Genetic testing was defined by ICD-10-CM codes for genetic screening or susceptibility. Testing prevalence was stratified by age, sex, race, and ethnicity, and annual testing incidence (2005-2024) was evaluated. Among 57,935 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, 1,205 (2.09%) underwent genetic testing. Among 2,811,862 patients with a family history of thoracic aortic disease, 66,699 (2.38%) received testing. Among 347,000 patients with nonthoracic arterial aneurysms, 4,913 (1.42%) underwent testing. Testing was consistently higher in females than males and varied across age groups. Annual testing incidence increased over time but remained <0.6% by 2024. In conclusion, genetic testing for HTAD remains markedly underutilized, with <2.5% of at-risk patients tested despite guideline recommendations, highlighting persistent implementation gaps and the need to improve equitable access to genetic evaluation.

We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts.

title: A safe and efficient analgesic approach for percutaneous transluminal angioplasty: Fentanyl plus targeted local anesthesia.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stenosis is a common complication of arteriovenous access (AV), for which percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) is a well-established intervention. Nevertheless, balloon dilation commonly induces pain. Common analgesic approaches during PTA encompass moderate intravenous sedation and analgesia, brachial plexus block, and local infiltrative anesthesia, each with its own limitations. A need currently exists for a safe, simple, and effective analgesic approach during PTA.

METHODS: This retrospective observational study was conducted between January 2020 and July 2022 at a single tertiary medical center. Patients with AV access dysfunction undergoing PTA were included. Patients were allocated into two groups based on the analgesia approach: one group received intraluminal fentanyl injection alone, and the other a combination of intraluminal fentanyl and local lidocaine infiltration at the stenotic site. Data regarding AV access type, lesion locations, 11-point Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) scores, and procedural complications were collected. Comparative analysis between groups was conducted using appropriate statistical methods, and significance was set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: A total of 120 patients (mean age, 62.9 ± 11.8 years; 65% were male) were included in the study: 34 in the fentanyl-only group (group A) and 86 in the fentanyl combined with lidocaine group (group B). Group A had a higher proportion of male patients compared with group B (79.4% vs 59.3%, p = 0.037). No significant differences were found in balloon size, inflation pressure, fluoroscope time, or procedural complications between groups. The primary outcome, procedural pain, was significantly lower in group B as compared to group A (NRS score 2.3 ± 0.9 vs 5.1 ± 2.2, p < 0.001), and this analgesic advantage remained after adjusting for gender and age.

CONCLUSION: Our study findings suggest that administering a combination of intraluminal fentanyl and a direct lidocaine injection in patients undergoing percutaneous transluminal angioplasty is both an efficient and safe analgesic procedure for PTA.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Stenosis is a common complication of arteriovenous access (AV), for which percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) is a well-established intervention. Nevertheless, balloon dilation commonly induces pain. Common analgesic approaches during PTA encompass moderate intravenous sedation and analgesia, brachial plexus block, and local infiltrative anesthesia, each with its own limitations.

title: Real-life venous thromboembolism risk scores in multiple myeloma receiving daratumumab, lenalidomide, and dexamethasone.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Treatment with daratumumab and lenalidomide has improved survival in patients with multiple myeloma (MM), however the risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE) is high. Data on the accuracy of VTE risk scores in MM receiving daratumumab are limited.

OBJECTIVES: To assess (i) the prognostic accuracy of available VTE risk scores (IMPEDE-VTE, SAVED, PRISM, and EHR-CAT scores) in non-transplant-eligible MM (NTE-MM) and relapsed/refractory MM (RRMM) consecutively treated with daratumumab, lenalidomide and dexamethasone (Dara-Rd); and (ii) the feasibility and safety of guideline-recommended thromboprophylaxis with low molecular weight heparin for 6 months followed by aspirin (LMWH-ASA).

DESIGN: Single-center, retrospective, cohort study.

METHODS: All consecutive MM patients treated with Dara-Rd and concomitant LMWH-ASA thromboprophylaxis between July, 2018 and September, 2023 were evaluated through chart review. Kaplan-Meier method and Concordance-Index (C-index) were used to estimate risk scores' prognostic accuracy.

RESULTS: 95 patients (median age 74 years) were included (n= 47 NTE-MM, and n= 48 RRMM). At 12 months from Dara-Rd initiation, 10 (10.4%) patients developed VTE; 4 (4.2%) had bleeding complications, and 2 (2.1%) patients died. Six VTE events (6.2%) occurred within first 6 months from Dara-Rd initiation while on LMWH prophylaxis, whereas 2 VTE (2%) developed in two patients receiving aspirin. The accuracy of IMPEDE-VTE, SAVED, PRISM and EHR-CAT scores was generally poor, with C-Index values ranging from 0.43 (95% confidence intervals [95%CI] 0.30 to 0.56) to 0.53 (95%CI: 0.38 to 0.68). LMWH-ASA prophylaxis was completed by 89.5% of the cohort.

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-life cohort of MM patients treated with Dara-Rd and guideline-recommended antithrombotic prophylaxis, currently available VTE risk scores demonstrated moderate to poor prognostic accuracy. LMWH-ASA prophylaxis was feasible but associated with residual VTE risk.

Data on the accuracy of VTE risk scores in MM receiving daratumumab are limited. OBJECTIVES: To assess (i) the prognostic accuracy of available VTE risk scores (IMPEDE-VTE, SAVED, PRISM, and EHR-CAT scores) in non-transplant-eligible MM (NTE-MM) and relapsed/refractory MM (RRMM) consecutively treated with daratumumab, lenalidomide and dexamethasone (Dara-Rd); and (ii) the feasibility and safety of guideline-recommended thromboprophylaxis with low molecular weight heparin for 6 months followed by aspirin (LMWH-ASA).

title: Nongeneral Anesthesia for Endovascular Aneurysm Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Clinical Outcomes and Robustness of Evidence.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal anesthetic strategy for endovascular aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) remains debated. While recent meta-analyses suggested potential benefits for nongeneral anesthesia (non-GA), available evidence is observational, and the robustness of pooled estimates remains uncertain.

METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative observational studies (2015-2025) were conducted across PubMed, Medline, Embase, and Scopus. Primary outcomes were 30-day and in-hospital mortality. Secondary outcomes included length of stay (LOS) and postoperative complications. Random-effects models utilized the Paule-Mandel estimator with Hartung-Knapp adjustment, prediction intervals (PIs), and prespecified influence diagnostics.

RESULTS: Twenty-two studies comprising >150,000 EVAR procedures were analyzed. Non-GA was not associated with reduced 30-day mortality compared with GA (risk ratio [RR] 0.90, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.54-1.52; I2≈86%; wide PI). Influence diagnostics identified one influential study; its exclusion yielded a lower mortality for non-GA (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.59-0.87; I2≈1%). Non-GA was associated with a modest reduction in hospital LOS (mean difference -0.53 days, 95% CI -1.02 to -0.03), but no consistent differences were observed in intensive care unit stay or major complications. The overall certainty of evidence was judged very low (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation).

CONCLUSION: Non-GA for EVAR does not increase 30-day mortality risk compared to GA. However, survival estimates are sensitive to study-level characteristics and procedural complexity. Current observational evidence supports individualized anesthetic selection rather than proving superiority or equivalence of either technique.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The optimal anesthetic strategy for endovascular aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR) remains debated. While recent meta-analyses suggested potential benefits for nongeneral anesthesia (non-GA), available evidence is observational, and the robustness of pooled estimates remains uncertain. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative observational studies (2015-2025) were conducted across PubMed, Medline, Embase, and Scopus.

title: Outcomes of Open Versus Endovascular Repair of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Involving the Iliac Bifurcation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aneurysmal involvement of the iliac bifurcation increases the complexity of both open and endovascular repair of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), potentially raising the risk of postoperative complications. Randomized trials comparing endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and open aortic repair (OAR) for AAA showed that EVAR is associated with a lower postoperative mortality rate. However, it remains unclear whether these results apply to AAA involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB). Several small single-institutional studies have shown conflicting results. This study aims to compare the outcomes of EVAR and OAR for AAAIB in a real-world, multi-institutional setting.

METHODS: The Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) database was queried for patients who underwent repair for AAAIB. The cohort was divided into 2 groups based on the intervention: EVAR versus OAR. Baseline demographic, clinical, and perioperative characteristics, as well as outcomes such as overall 30-day mortality, in-hospital mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, stroke), intestinal ischemia, overall reinterventions, and 1-year survival, were compared between the groups. Univariable analysis, multivariable inverse probability-weighted regression (IPWR), survival analysis with the Kaplan-Meier method, log-rank test, and Cox proportional hazards regression were performed.

RESULTS: Of all reviewed patients, 7,535 were included in the final analysis, of whom 5,742 (76.2%) underwent EVAR, whereas 1,793 (23.8%) underwent OAR. In IPWR models, patients who underwent EVAR had significantly lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality (odds ratio [OR]: 0.25, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.18-0.34, P < 0.001), 30-day mortality (OR: 0.31, 95% CI: 0.23-0.42, P < 0.001), MACE (OR: 0.24, 95% CI: 0.19-0.31, P < 0.001), and other postoperative adverse events compared to OAR. The Cox proportional hazards model demonstrated a significantly higher 1-year survival rate for EVAR compared to OAR (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.61, 95% CI: 0.50-0.76, P < 0.001).

CONCLUSION: In this real-world, multi-institutional study, EVAR for AAAIB was associated with lower odds of overall in-hospital mortality, 30-day mortality, MACE, as well as a higher 1-year survival rate, compared to the OAR. EVAR should be considered the primary method for repairing aortoiliac aneurysm involving the iliac bifurcation in anatomically suitable patients. Longer follow-up studies are needed to confirm these findings and compare the long-term reintervention and aorta-related mortality rates between the 2 treatment modalities.

Randomized trials comparing endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) and open aortic repair (OAR) for AAA showed that EVAR is associated with a lower postoperative mortality rate. However, it remains unclear whether these results apply to AAA involving the iliac bifurcation (AAAIB).

title: Clinical outcomes of transperitoneal versus retroperitoneal approaches of open aortic repair for abdominal aortic aneurysm stratified by iliac bifurcation involvement.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortic aneurysm with iliac bifurcation involvement (AAAIB) is associated with higher rates of systemic comorbidities and increased complexity of open aortic repair (OAR), resulting in worse outcomes compared with OAR for isolated abdominal aortic aneurysm (IAAA). The Society for Vascular Surgery practice guidelines recommend the retroperitoneal approach (RPA) for OAR in certain patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). However, there is limited evidence to determine whether the relative advantages and disadvantages of RPA and the transperitoneal approach (TPA) change depending on whether the aneurysm distally involves the iliac bifurcation. This study compared the outcomes of TPA and RPA for AAA, stratified by iliac bifurcation involvement, in a multi-institutional, real-world setting.

METHODS: The Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative database was queried for patients who underwent OAR for AAA from January 2003 to September 2024. Patients were stratified as having AAAIB or IAAA based on whether the aneurysm involved the iliac bifurcation and required a distal anastomosis beyond the common iliac artery bifurcation, or not. Baseline characteristics and clinical outcomes, such as overall 30-day mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, and stroke), and 1-year survival, were compared between the TPA and RPA groups in patients with IAAA and AAAIB. Univariable and multivariable analyses and a confirmatory analysis with inverse probability-weighted regression were performed.

RESULTS: Of all the reviewed patients, 17,009 were included in the final analysis, of whom 15,218 (89.5%) had IAAA and 1791 (10.5%) had AAAIB. Among patients with IAAA, compared with RPA, TPA was associated with a higher odds of overall 30-day mortality (odds ratios [OR], 1.26; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05-1.49; P = .011) and of MACE (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.11-1.44; P = .001) and a lower 1-year survival rate (hazard ratio, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.09-1.39; P = .001). Among patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with a lower odds of lower extremity ischemia (OR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.25-0.91; P = .024), without significant differences in 30-day mortality (OR, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.42-1.51; P = .485), MACE (OR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.52-1.42; P = .563), and 1-year survival (hazard ratio, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.59-1.47; P = .768).

CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world study, iliac bifurcation involvement in AAA was an effect modifier for the outcomes of different OAR approaches. For patients with IAAA, compared with RPA, TPA was associated with worse 30-day mortality, MACE, and 1-year survival. In contrast, for patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with a lower odds of lower extremity ischemia, without significant differences in 30-day mortality, MACE, or 1-year survival. This study suggests that RPA may be the procedure of choice for IAAA if it is otherwise feasible. However, TPA may be the procedure of choice for patients with AAAIB who are otherwise anatomically suitable. Larger prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Aortic aneurysm with iliac bifurcation involvement (AAAIB) is associated with higher rates of systemic comorbidities and increased complexity of open aortic repair (OAR), resulting in worse outcomes compared with OAR for isolated abdominal aortic aneurysm (IAAA). The Society for Vascular Surgery practice guidelines recommend the retroperitoneal approach (RPA) for OAR in certain patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). However, there is limited evidence to determine whether the relative advantages and disadvantages of RPA and the transperitoneal approach (TPA) change depending on whether the aneurysm distally involves the iliac bifurcation.

title: Updated systematic review and meta-analysis comparing Myval versus Sapien 3 transcatheter heart valves in severe aortic stenosis: focus on early and one-year mortality.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a guideline-recommended treatment for severe aortic stenosis (AS). While the balloon-expandable Edwards Sapien 3 valve has long been the benchmark, the newer Myval valve has emerged as a potential alternative. Comparative data on mid-term survival, specifically one-year all-cause mortality, are lacking but crucial for clinical evaluation.

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesised direct comparative evidence on the Myval versus Sapien 3 valves in patients undergoing TAVI, searching PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central up to November 2025. The primary outcomes included all-cause mortality within 30 days and 1 year. Secondary outcomes were 30-day safety events and hemodynamic parameters.

RESULTS: Five studies (n = 2771) were included. The pooled analysis indicated no statistical difference in 30-day mortality (RR: 1.05, 95% CI: 0.53-2.07; p = 0.89; I2=0%) or in one-year all-cause mortality (RR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.64-1.35; p = 0.70; I2=0%). Rates of stroke, major bleeding, pacemaker implantation, and other 30-day complications were also comparable (all p > 0.05). Hemodynamically, the Myval valve was superior at 30 days, with a lower mean gradient (MD: -2.37, 95% CI: -3.45 to -1.30; p < 0.0001) and larger effective orifice area (MD: 0.26, 95% CI: 0.17-0.35; p < 0.00001). Available one-year data from two randomised trials indicated this hemodynamic benefit was sustained.

CONCLUSION: This updated meta-analysis demonstrates that the newer Myval valve offers comparable early safety and one-year survival to the established Sapien 3 valve, with superior and sustained hemodynamic performance. These findings support its role as a safe and effective alternative in the TAVI landscape.

title: Beyond Patency: Patient-Centered Outcomes and the Proposed Accountability Gap in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
abstract: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) carries 1-year mortality of 20% to 25%, comparable with many solid-organ malignancies. Technically successful revascularization, defined by anatomical patency, does not reliably deliver pain relief, restored function, or sustained quality of life. This narrative review synthesizes landmark randomized trials (BEST-CLI, BASIL-1, BASIL-2) and current European and United States guidelines, grading every claim with a scheme in which population indirectness downgrades design strength. We examine 4 domains of morbidity persisting after anatomically successful revascularization: mechanistically heterogeneous pain; functional and quality-of-life decline; psychological burden; and sustained health care use, including chronic opioid use (approximately 35%), unhealed wounds at 1 year (10%-32%), and unplanned 30-day readmission (approximately 25%). No patient-reported outcome measure has been validated specifically for CLTI or used as a co-primary trial endpoint. We propose an accountability gap: the under-measured transfer of unresolved morbidity from vascular services to primary care. We state it as a falsifiable prediction about the discrimination of patency rather than prevalence, with a pre-specified effect size, explicit treatment of death as a competing risk, and a core outcome battery justified against COSMIN criteria. Patient co-production is the indispensable next step.

title: Omega-6 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids and Peripheral Artery Disease: An Individual Participant-Level Analysis of 9 International Prospective Studies.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) have previously been associated with several peripheral artery disease (PAD) risk factors. We studied the association between individual omega-6 PUFAs and incident PAD in a multicohort analysis.

METHODS: This study was conducted among participants from 9 cohorts (N=137 704; PAD cases=2014) in the FORCE (Fatty Acids and Outcomes Research Consortium) who were free of clinical PAD at baseline. Omega-6 PUFAs were measured at baseline and with a median follow-up of 14 years. Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were conducted in individual cohorts to evaluate associations of omega-6 PUFAs (continuous cohort-standardized interquintile ranges [difference between the medians of the 10th and 90th omega-6 PUFAs percentiles] and cohort-specific quintiles) with incident clinical PAD adjusting for prespecified covariates. Inverse-variance weighted meta-analysis was used to calculate the combined hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% CIs.

RESULTS: Linoleic acid (LA) was measured in all 9 cohorts, arachidonic acid in 8 (N=33 541; PAD cases=1766), dihomo-γ-LA and γ-LA in 7 (N=29 861; PAD cases=1686), and eicosadienoic acid in 6 (N=27 538; PAD cases=1435). Only LA was associated with a lower risk of incident PAD (quintile 5 versus quintile 1: HR, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.64-0.89]; P=0.0009). Results did not differ in a statistically significant manner by age, sex, diabetes status, or smoking status.

CONCLUSIONS: Results suggest that the omega-6 PUFA LA may be protective against PAD, and other omega-6 PUFAs are not associated with PAD incidence. This is further evidence that omega-6 PUFA-disease relationships should be evaluated by individual fatty acids rather than grouped as total omega-6 PUFAs.

title: Endovascular stenting of extracranial cervical artery dissections: A two-center study.
abstract:
PURPOSE: Extracranial arterial dissections (EAD) are uncommon in the general population but represent a relatively frequent cause of ischemic stroke in young adults. Most EAD have a favorable prognosis and are managed conservatively with antithrombotic therapy, with current guidelines supporting either antiplatelet or anticoagulant treatment. Endovascular stenting is reserved for selected high-risk cases, and this article reports a multicenter experience with this approach and reviews the available literature.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Eighty-four EAD patients who underwent stenting were included. A standardized follow-up protocol at 12 months consisting of a clinical neurological assessment accompanied by imaging studies, including either Computed Tomography, Magnetic Resonance Imaging or Digital Subtraction Angiography was adopted.

RESULTS: In our cohort, most dissections were spontaneous (81 %) and predominantly involved the internal carotid artery (85 %), with acute stroke being the most common indication for stenting. Technical success was achieved in 85.7 % and complications occurred in 10 %. Three patients with initial stent implantation failure underwent successful secondary attempt. No significant predictors of technical success were identified. At discharge, good functional outcome was observed in 83 % of patients and at 12 months most followed patients showed favorable radiological results with high stent patency (86 %) and excellent clinical outcomes (mRS 0-2 in 97 %).

CONCLUSION: The results of our study suggest that for selected patients with medical therapy failure or hemodynamic compromise, stenting is a reasonable alternative. Given the limited evidence on indications, safety and efficacy, further randomized studies comparing stenting with medical management are warranted.

Most EAD have a favorable prognosis and are managed conservatively with antithrombotic therapy, with current guidelines supporting either antiplatelet or anticoagulant treatment. Endovascular stenting is reserved for selected high-risk cases, and this article reports a multicenter experience with this approach and reviews the available literature.

title: Perceptions of decompressive craniectomy following endovascular thrombectomy in the Middle East and North Africa: A multi-specialty cross-sectional survey of attitudes, reported practices, and barriers.
abstract: Decompressive craniectomy (DC) can be a life-saving rescue therapy for malignant cerebral edema after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), yet DC practices following EVT have not previously been examined across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). We conducted a web-based, bilingual (English/Arabic) cross-sectional survey of physicians involved in acute stroke care across 15 MENA countries (January-March 2025) using a 22-item instrument that underwent expert content-validity review (S-CVI/UA = 0.86) and cognitive-interview pilot testing, to describe self-reported attitudes, perceived practices, and barriers regarding DC after EVT, and to determine whether key findings remained consistent among clinicians with the most direct relevant experience. Of 440 physicians invited, 179 responded; five respondents from zero-EVT-volume institutions were excluded, yielding an analytic cohort of 174 (response rate 41%) from 13 countries, of whom 49% (n = 85) were neurosurgeons. Eighty-four percent of respondents endorsed DC over medical management in selected patients, but only 51% perceived DC was performed in a timely manner "always/often." The mean physician-estimated, recall-based consent rate was 52% (SD 19%), with a Gulf Cooperation Council versus North African difference (59% vs. 44%, p < 0.001) that persisted when restricted to clinicians with direct family-meeting or operative involvement. Leading perceived barriers were patient/family preferences (79%), surgical resource constraints (55%), and delayed detection (30%). These findings, which reflect physician perceptions rather than institutionally verified practice, support development of culturally adapted consent pathways, standardized DC candidacy algorithms, regionalized stroke networks, and a prospective MENA stroke registry to confirm whether these perception-based signals correspond to actual clinical practice and outcomes.

title: Adjuvant Systemic Hypothermia During Mechanical Thrombectomy (ReCCLAIM II): A Multicenter, Randomized, Controlled Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypothermia reduces ischemic injury in preclinical stroke models, yet translation into the clinical setting remains challenging. We aimed to assess the feasibility of inducing adjuvant systemic hypothermia among patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke during mechanical thrombectomy.

METHODS: This was a phase II randomized feasibility-controlled trial involving 10 sites in the United States, conducted between May 2019 and May 2024. All eligible patients had confirmed proximal middle cerebral artery or internal carotid artery occlusions, an Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Score of 6 to 10, and symptom onset within 24 hours. Patients underwent mechanical thrombectomy and were randomly assigned to either treatment with adjuvant hypothermia using a novel intravascular cooling catheter or standard of care. The primary feasibility end points were the ability to achieve a target temperature of <34 °C within 1 hour of arterial puncture and overall door-to-reperfusion times. The primary safety end point was core-laboratory-adjudicated hemorrhagic conversion within 36 hours, and secondary end points included final infarct volume and serious adverse events.

RESULTS: A total of 95 patients were enrolled (29 in the roll-in phase and 66 randomized). The mean age of the randomized cohort was 65±12 years, with a median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score of 15. Among patients in the treatment arm, 30 of 33 (91%) achieved hypothermia within 1 hour of arterial puncture during thrombectomy, and 23 of 33 (70%) patients were at target temperature (<34 °C) before reperfusion. The median time to hypothermia was 10 minutes (interquartile range [IQR], 7-22) from arterial puncture. There were no significant differences in door-to-reperfusion times (hypothermia: 95 minutes [IQR, 54-116] versus control: 94 minutes [IQR, 77-121]; P=0.70). Final infarct volumes were numerically lower in the hypothermia treatment arm (hypothermia: 11 cm3 [IQR, 5-42] versus control: 30 cm3 [IQR, 6-80]; P=0.13), with no significant differences in the rates of hemorrhagic conversion or pneumonia. There was a higher number of serious adverse events in the hypothermia arm (45.5% versus 24.2%; P=0.12), although the trial was not powered for differences in serious adverse events or clinical efficacy.

CONCLUSIONS: This is the first clinical trial to demonstrate the feasibility of early and rapid systemic hypothermia as an adjunct therapy during mechanical thrombectomy without delaying time to reperfusion. The potential impact on infarct volumes and serious adverse events, however, warrants further investigation.

METHODS: This was a phase II randomized feasibility-controlled trial involving 10 sites in the United States, conducted between May 2019 and May 2024.

title: Sitting Baduanjin-based rehabilitation programme following endovascular therapy in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia: protocol for a WeChat mini program-assisted multicentre randomized controlled trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Endovascular therapy (EVT) is an important revascularization strategy for limb salvage in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, despite restoration of blood flow, patients may continue to experience residual haemodynamic impairment and ischaemia-related burden after EVT, with a persistently high risk of adverse limb outcomes. Therefore, effective post-EVT rehabilitation strategies are needed to further improve limb perfusion and promote functional recovery and symptom improvement in this population. Exercise rehabilitation is widely recommended for patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), but current evidence is largely derived from individuals with intermittent claudication, and its applicability and additional benefits in patients with CLTI after EVT remain uncertain. Sitting Baduanjin (SBDJ) is a low-intensity mind-body exercise modality that reduces lower-limb loading and postural demands while providing exercise stimulation, with potential cardiovascular regulatory effects, and may therefore be suitable for patients with limited exercise tolerance after EVT. However, evidence regarding the effects of SBDJ on target-limb haemodynamic status and patient-centred outcomes in patients with CLTI following EVT remains limited.

METHODS: This prospective, multicentre, parallel-group randomised controlled trial incorporates blinded outcome assessment. A total of 146 eligible patients with CLTI following EVT will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention group or the control group. The intervention group will receive SBDJ combined with ankle pump exercise, whereas the control group will receive ankle pump exercise. A WeChat mini program will support exercise delivery, adherence monitoring, follow-up management, and questionnaire data collection during the home-based phase. The primary outcome is the longitudinal change in target-limb ABI over the 12-week rehabilitation period. Secondary outcomes include walking ability, quality of life, anxiety symptoms, lower-limb rest pain, and safety. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, week 4, and week 12.

DISCUSSION: This trial aims to determine whether an SBDJ-based rehabilitation programme provides additional benefits over ankle pump exercise alone on index-limb haemodynamic status among patients with CLTI following EVT, while exploring its potential effects on functional outcomes and patient-reported outcomes during the early post-EVT rehabilitation period.Clinical Trial Registration: http://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/, identifier: ITMCTR ITMCTR2022000113.

Therefore, effective post-EVT rehabilitation strategies are needed to further improve limb perfusion and promote functional recovery and symptom improvement in this population.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Image-Guided Navigation in Complex Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Complex endovascular aortic repair exposes patients and operators to substantial radiation, contrast, and long procedures. Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted image-guided navigation, based on cloud-based 3-dimensional image fusion, has been proposed to improve intraoperative guidance, but its comparative benefit is uncertain.

METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science (last search July 2025) for studies comparing AI-assisted image-guided navigation with conventional fluoroscopy and digital subtraction angiography during complex endovascular aortic repair. No navigation platform was prespecified. Random-effects meta-analyses yielded mean differences (MD) with 95% confidence intervals (CI); heterogeneity was quantified with I2. Risk of bias was assessed with Risk Of Bias In Non-randomised Studies of Interventions and certainty with Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation.

RESULTS: Three retrospective cohorts (332 patients; 189 AI, 143 control), all evaluating one cloud-based platform (Cydar EV), were eligible. AI-assisted navigation was associated with a lower radiation dose (2 studies, 216 patients; MD -1,435.85 mGy, 95% CI -2,208.84 to -662.86; I2 = 0%). No significant differences were found in fluoroscopy time (MD -11.04 min, 95% CI -25.37 to 3.29; I2 = 65%), operative time (MD -16.39 min, 95% CI -37.21 to 4.42; I2 = 0%), or contrast volume (MD -30.59 mL, 95% CI -73.95 to 12.76; I2 = 94%). Mortality and major adverse events (single studies) did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSION: Cydar EV-assisted navigation may reduce radiation dose during complex endovascular aortic repair, but evidence is limited to retrospective studies of a single platform and does not establish a class effect for other AI-assisted navigation systems. Prospective comparative studies across platforms are needed.

METHODS: We searched MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science (last search July 2025) for studies comparing AI-assisted image-guided navigation with conventional fluoroscopy and digital subtraction angiography during complex endovascular aortic repair.

title: Endovascular Management of Life-Threatening Hemoptysis in Rare Pulmonary Vascular Diseases.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Massive hemoptysis in patients with complex pulmonary vascular disease is difficult to manage because surgery is frequently contraindicated, making endovascular therapy an important treatment option.

CASE SUMMARY: We report 3 patients with life-threatening hemoptysis caused by distinct rare etiologies: systemic-to-pulmonary collateral bleeding in Eisenmenger syndrome due to patent ductus arteriosus, complex collateral bleeding associated with left upper lobe aspergilloma, and post-tubercular collateral hemorrhage. Angiography-guided transcatheter embolization was individualized using particles, coils, and a vascular plug according to vascular anatomy. All patients achieved immediate hemostasis without major procedural complications, with sustained freedom from recurrent hemoptysis during 6-12 months of follow-up.

DISCUSSION: Successful bronchial artery embolization depends on meticulous angiographic evaluation and anatomy-driven device selection. This series demonstrates the versatility of endovascular techniques, including vascular plug implantation for high-flow bronchial collaterals in cases where conventional embolization is technically challenging.

TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Individualized, anatomy-guided endovascular therapy provides a safe, effective, and organ-preserving treatment for life-threatening hemoptysis in complex pulmonary vascular disease. Careful procedural planning is essential for durable clinical success.

Angiography-guided transcatheter embolization was individualized using particles, coils, and a vascular plug according to vascular anatomy.

title: Risk-benefit profile of upper versus lower extremity peripherally inserted central catheter placement in neonates: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The optimal insertion site for peripherally inserted central catheters in neonates remains uncertain. International guidelines differ in their recommendations regarding upper- versus lower-extremity placement, and existing systematic reviews are limited by small samples, narrow outcome coverage, or outdated evidence.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the potential risk-benefit profile of upper- versus lower-extremity peripherally inserted central catheter placement in neonates.

DESIGN: Systematic review and meta-analysis.

METHODS: MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL, and CINAHL were searched from inception to January 6, 2026, for studies comparing upper- versus lower-extremity placement in neonates. Primary outcomes were venous thromboembolism, central line-associated bloodstream infection, and catheter tip malposition; secondary outcomes included phlebitis, catheter migration, catheter leakage, catheter occlusion, catheter breakage, total complications, dwell time, unplanned removal, pericardial or pleural effusion, sepsis, and all-cause mortality. Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias. Crude estimates were pooled, sparse and heterogeneous adjusted estimates were summarised narratively, and certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach.

RESULTS: Twenty-one observational studies from 10 countries, involving 15,289 catheters, were included. For primary outcomes, upper-extremity placement was associated with a lower risk of venous thromboembolism (RR = 0.51, 95% CI 0.30-0.89; P = 0.017; low certainty) but higher risks of central line-associated bloodstream infection (RR = 1.44, 95% CI 1.07-1.95; P = 0.018; very low certainty) and catheter tip malposition (RR = 2.63, 95% CI 1.61-4.30; P < 0.001; very low certainty). For secondary outcomes, upper-extremity placement was associated with lower phlebitis risk (RR = 0.64, 95% CI 0.43-0.94; P = 0.022; low certainty) but higher risks of catheter migration (RR = 1.74, 95% CI 1.27-2.38; P < 0.001; low certainty), catheter leakage (RR = 2.24, 95% CI 1.35-3.73; P = 0.002; moderate certainty), and a marginally higher risk of unplanned removal (RR = 1.23, 95% CI 1.00-1.51; P = 0.048; very low certainty). A post hoc exploratory analysis suggested a possible higher risk of pericardial or pleural effusion (RR = 3.79, 95% CI 1.20-12.02; P = 0.024; very low certainty). No statistically significant between-site differences were observed for other secondary outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Crude observational evidence suggested a potential bidirectional risk-benefit profile across catheter-related outcomes. The findings should be interpreted cautiously because non-randomised designs remain susceptible to residual confounding. The observed associations may inform risk-informed, individualised site selection but do not establish a universally preferred site. Prospective studies with standardised outcomes and adjusted analyses are needed.

title: Impact of portable point-of-care ultrasound on clinical decision-making and referrals in general practice: a cross-sectional study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly used in general practice, but evidence on its impact on clinical decision-making when performed with portable devices remains limited. Most existing studies have used cart-based systems, which may not reflect real-world general practice.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of portable POCUS on clinical decision-making and reduction of referrals to secondary care in general practice.

METHODS: Cross-sectional observational study conducted over 12 months in a primary care centre in Barcelona, Spain. Three general practitioners with accredited training performed POCUS examinations using portable devices in 108 patients. Inclusion criteria were patients aged ≥15 years requiring clinical ultrasound. Clinical management plans were documented before and after POCUS using same questionnaire. Changes in decision-making and referral patterns were analysed using McNemar's test. Reporting followed the STROBE statement for cross-sectional studies.

RESULTS: POCUS changed clinical decision-making in 66.7% of cases. Intended referrals to secondary care decreased from 44.4% to 25.0% (absolute risk reduction 19.4%, 95% CI 8.4-30.5%, relative risk reduction 44%). Musculoskeletal examinations represented 73.1% of cases, with management modified in 63.3%. All seven patients with suspected deep vein thrombosis were managed without hospital referral. Referrals for conventional radiology ultrasound decreased from 32.4% to 12.0%, while GP-performed invasive procedures (infiltrations) increased from 0.9% to 18.5%.

CONCLUSION: Portable POCUS substantially influences clinical decision-making and reduces secondary care referrals in general practice. Further research is needed, especially longitudinal studies, to evaluate whether these changes translate into improved health outcomes for patients.

Most existing studies have used cart-based systems, which may not reflect real-world general practice. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of portable POCUS on clinical decision-making and reduction of referrals to secondary care in general practice.

title: Clinical and economic impact of central venous catheter-associated or catheter-related bloodstream infections in pediatric intensive care units: protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Central venous catheter-associated and catheter-related bloodstream infections may increase mortality, length of stay, and hospital costs in critically ill children. This systematic review will estimate their clinical and economic impact in pediatric intensive care and examine how infection definitions, confounding, and the time-dependent nature of infection influence the evidence.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Comparative longitudinal observational studies including patients aged 18 years or younger admitted to pediatric intensive care units and exposed to central venous catheters will be eligible. The exposure will be catheter-associated or catheter-related bloodstream infection, compared with patients from the same catheter-exposed source population who are infection-free at the relevant risk time. Mortality, length of stay, and hospital costs are co-primary outcomes. Multiple bibliographic databases, gray-literature sources, and study registries will be searched without date restrictions. Two reviewers will independently select studies, extract data, assess risk of bias, and evaluate certainty. Meta-analysis will be performed when studies are sufficiently comparable; otherwise, structured synthesis will be used.

RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: The review is expected to clarify the magnitude and methodological robustness of the clinical and economic consequences of these infections and identify priorities for future pediatric intensive care research.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: Central venous catheter-associated and catheter-related bloodstream infections may increase mortality, length of stay, and hospital costs in critically ill children. This systematic review will estimate their clinical and economic impact in pediatric intensive care and examine how infection definitions, confounding, and the time-dependent nature of infection influence the evidence. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Comparative longitudinal observational studies including patients aged 18 years or younger admitted to pediatric intensive care units and exposed to central venous catheters will be eligible.
